title: Case-variant duplicate app config keys resolve nondeterministically via HashMap iteration
description:
Root cause: app_config_for (config.rs:103-110) resolves class lookups via find_map over a HashMap with eq_ignore_ascii_case; HashMap iteration order is randomized per process (RandomState). TOML legally allows [apps.kitty] and [apps.Kitty] as distinct keys.
Failure: config with case-variant duplicate keys and different binary values -> repeated hyprloom restore launches DIFFERENT binaries across runs for the same window class. Nondeterminism in an authorized-executable decision path.
Fix: detect case-insensitive key collisions at load and error, or sort candidates deterministically before find_map.
close_reason: Duplicate of hyprloom-production-bug-audit-2026-08-30-gqg.4 — same root cause: unordered case-insensitive app-key fallback

title: Interrupted atomic writes leave private session temp files permanently orphaned
description:
## Problem
session.rs:1220-1266 creates .<target>.json.<pid>.<sequence>.tmp with mode 0600 and renames it only after writing and syncing. Termination after create_new succeeds but before rename leaves that file forever. Session listing, deletion, migration, and rotation ignore it. The earlier theory that lock contention normally kills a writer was incorrect: a process waiting for the operation lock has not created a session temporary file.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. In an isolated XDG data directory, create a current-user-owned private regular file whose basename exactly matches the atomic-write grammar.
2. Place a valid saved session beside it.
3. Invoke any storage-using Hyprloom CLI command after acquiring the exclusive operation lock.
4. Observe that current code leaves the hidden temporary file indefinitely while the valid session remains usable.

## Acceptance Criteria
Cleanup uses exclusive-lock ownership proof rather than an age guess. Only strict Hyprloom temp-name matches that are current-user-owned private regular files are removed, without following symlinks. Valid snapshots and unrelated hidden files remain unchanged. Cleanup is idempotent, directory durability is preserved, and unsafe candidates produce bounded diagnostics.
design: Run orphan cleanup only after the process has acquired the exclusive OperationLock and before migration or session-store use. Parse the complete basename grammar, inspect with symlink_metadata, require current UID, regular-file type, and private permissions, unlink without following, then sync the directory when removals occurred. Do not use mtime, PID liveness, or a grace period. Irregular or unsafe matches are reported and left untouched.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover exact names for sessions and markers, malformed PID and sequence fields, unrelated dotfiles, symlinks, directories, ownership and mode rejection, multiple orphans, cleanup failure, idempotence, and directory sync failure. A real-CLI e2e through fixture gqg.36.4 pre-seeds a valid session plus orphan and negative-control files, invokes list through isolated XDG paths, and asserts exact remaining files, exit status, stdout session listing, stderr diagnostics, and ordered redacted JSONL filesystem events. Use readiness events only: no sleeps, live store, or nondeterministic timestamps.

title: autosave status and config print store errors to stdout with exit 0 while list correctly fails
description:
Root cause: informational subcommands route genuine session-store failures through cli_println! (stdout) and fall through to exit 0: autosave status at main.rs:659 (Could not list sessions), config Brave section at main.rs:546. The list command shows the intended opposite (main.rs:500-503: stderr + exit 1).
Failure (reproduced): sessions dir as a regular file (unsafe path) with active timer: hyprloom autosave -> stdout prints 'Autosave is active' + 'Could not list sessions: unsafe session path ...', EXIT 0 — a monitoring script sees success. hyprloom config -> 'Could not read Brave profiles: JSON parse error ...' on stdout, exit 0.
Fix: store-error arms to stderr and nonzero exit (config's Brave notice may stay exit-0 but belongs on stderr).
close_reason: Rejected as non-material: autosave status still reports the independently established timer state and visibly reports the ancillary listing failure; config reports optional Brave inventory failure. No correctness or destructive path follows from exit 0.

title: Autosave installer writes user units outside systemd user-unit search paths
description:
## Problem
autosave.rs:20-27 derives the installation directory from dirs::config_dir(), so an explicit XDG_CONFIG_HOME produces XDG_CONFIG_HOME/systemd/user. The systemd user-unit search path includes the account-home .config/systemd/user directory and XDG_DATA_HOME/systemd/user, not XDG_CONFIG_HOME/systemd/user. Hyprloom can therefore report two created files that the documented systemctl --user enable command cannot discover. Loss of installer XDG values inside the service is separately owned by gqg.37.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start the isolated storage/systemd fixture with HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, and XDG_DATA_HOME set to distinct absolute directories.
2. Run hyprloom autosave --install.
3. Follow the printed enable command through the fake user manager using the documented user-unit search paths.
4. Observe that current code placed both units only under XDG_CONFIG_HOME/systemd/user and the manager cannot resolve the timer by name.

## Acceptance Criteria
Installation commits both units to a documented discoverable user-unit location independent of XDG_CONFIG_HOME, or fails before claiming success. Existing transactional writes, ownership, privacy, symlink rejection, migration, and rollback remain intact. This record does not duplicate or solve service execution-environment inheritance.
design: Resolve the account-home user configuration unit directory explicitly instead of dirs::config_dir. Require an absolute account home and preserve ensure_systemd_directory plus the existing two-file transaction. Keep service environment behavior out of scope and link gqg.37 as related. Render and return the exact committed paths so CLI instructions and discovery use the same location.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover default and custom XDG_CONFIG_HOME, distinct XDG_DATA_HOME, spaces and percent signs in HOME, missing or relative home, symlink ancestors, wrong ownership, interrupted service or timer write, rollback, reinstall, and legacy-unit migration. A real-CLI e2e through fixture gqg.36.4 installs with three distinct roots, asks the fake user manager to resolve and enable the timer by name, and asserts exact unit bytes, paths, transaction cleanup, argv order, exit code, human stdout, empty-success stderr, and ordered redacted JSONL. Negative controls prove gqg.37 remains reproducible and no live systemd or sleeps are used.

title: Brave profile inventory reads only the stable-channel Local State, breaking Beta/Nightly/Dev
description:
Root cause: local_state_path (src/brave.rs:20-24) hardcodes BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser/Local State. Window-side identity (--profile-directory from cmdline) is channel-independent, but the profile INVENTORY reads only the stable channel path.
Failure: Brave Nightly/Beta/Dev as the only Brave: SessionClient stores profile_directory=Some("Profile 1") while read_profiles() reads the absent stable path -> Ok(vec![]) -> session internally inconsistent (client references a profile the inventory cannot name); a stable install alongside a dev channel contributes wrong profile names. Restore then maps profiles from the wrong channel.
Fix: resolve channel from the running process (--user-data-dir or binary path) or scan BraveSoftware/*/Local State and union inventories keyed by channel.
close_reason: Rejected as an unproven unsupported-variant claim: Beta/Nightly/Dev windows must first pass the exact brave-browser class gate, and no supported channel-class production path to this stable-only inventory code was established.

title: Mixed Brave profile expansion silently omits ambiguous saved windows
description:
## Problem
capture.rs:212-247 can retain one positively identified Brave profile while other saved Brave clients remain profile_identity_ambiguous. In plain restore, restore.rs:1308-1340 enters profile mode and continues past every raw Brave client; restore.rs:3149-3236 synthesizes only positively represented profiles. The ambiguous remainder receives no outcome or counter. Reconciliation performs the same omission while replacement already fails ambiguity preflight at restore.rs:1992-2004.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Load a saved session containing one Brave client with profile_directory Default and two nonignored Brave clients with profile_identity_ambiguous=true, plus brave_profiles for Default and Profile 1.
2. Leave profile_workspaces unset and provide no current Brave windows.
3. Run plain restore and reconcile in real and dry-run modes.
4. Observe that only Default becomes an effective target and the two ambiguous requested windows disappear from reporting while the command can report success.

## Acceptance Criteria
Effective-target expansion returns every synthesized target and every omitted raw requested client. A profile target subsumes only raw clients backed by matching positive profile evidence. Every nonignored ambiguous remainder is reported as incomplete and causes nonzero status in plain restore, reconcile, dry-run, and replacement preflight, without guessing, spawning, or dispatching for it. Ignore policy runs before ambiguity classification.
design: Replace Option<Vec<BraveProfile>> style expansion with an EffectiveTargets result containing targets plus typed omissions. Carry omission identity and reason into both RestoreReport and ReconcileReport. Apply current ignore policy first; mark an ambiguous raw Brave client represented only when a positive same-profile target safely subsumes it. Preserve one-profile-one-launch behavior and existing replacement preflight.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover one-safe plus two-ambiguous, total ambiguity, all-safe, repeated same profile, missing inventory, explicit empty map, mapped and unmapped profiles, later ignore rules, initialClass matching, plain and reconcile, real and dry-run, and replacement preflight. E2e uses fixtures gqg.36.2 and gqg.36.3 with fixed clients, process trees, profile discovery, and launch traces; assert exact target and outcome order, at most one safe launch, zero ambiguous spawn or dispatch, second-pass convergence, exit 1 for incomplete work, human stdout and stderr separation, parseable report-only JSON stdout, and ordered redacted JSONL without sleeps.

title: profile_directory_from_cmdline swallows trailing URL/path args into the profile name
description:
Root cause: profile_directory_from_cmdline (src/process.rs:345-354) assembles the profile from ALL tokens after --profile-directory= until one starts with '-'. A URL or path arg after the flag gets folded in. Reproduced: "brave --profile-directory=Profile 1 https://youtube.com" -> Some("Profile 1 https://youtube.com").
Failure: single Brave window launched that way captures profile_directory = "Profile 1 https://youtube.com" — a fabricated per-window identity matching no Local State profile; restore launches Brave with a bogus --profile-directory (creating/attaching a wrong profile). Simultaneously active_brave_profile_directories contains only the garbage string so filter_profiles_by_active_directories (brave.rs:93-102) DROPS the genuine Profile 1 — session fails to capture what restore needs.
Fix: operate on the argv vector before joining; take only the --flag=<value> entry (or flag + exactly one following argv entry); a URL/positional must terminate parsing.
close_reason: Duplicate of hyprloom-production-bug-audit-2026-08-30-gqg.2 — same root cause: flattened argv breaks profile-directory parsing

title: Brave profile fail-closed gate is keyed on booleans inside the untrusted session file
description:
Root cause: the fail-closed rule "automatic restore must not use an ambiguous client to move or launch a guessed Brave profile" (session.rs:136-139, restore.rs:999-1001) is enforced solely by two booleans stored IN the session file: profile_identity_ambiguous and brave_profiles inventory. An editor sets profile_identity_ambiguous:false plus a crafted brave_profiles entry.
Failure: restore synthesizes a launch target and spawns brave --profile-directory=Work (restore.rs:3195-3236, 3348-3357) — a logged-in browser profile the user never saved opens automatically at login; validate_replacement_targets unsafe-target check (1997-2004) bypassed the same way. Verified by code path.
Fix: re-derive profile identity at restore from non-session evidence (live Local State inventory / matched windows' /proc), and require the config profile_workspaces allowlist for any profile-derived launch.
close_reason: Duplicate of canonical owner hyprloom-session-file-arbitrary-exec-sk0. The same untrusted session can forge application identity and executable authority directly; the Brave profile booleans are a narrower consequence of that trust-boundary defect, not an independent root.

title: Browser handoff can consume and reposition an already owned window
description:
## Problem
restore.rs:1113-1135 accepts a stable focused browser handoff after an active-window transition even when that address existed before launch. The launch-correlation path at restore.rs:3533-3708 does not receive reconciliation consumed, reserved, protected, or failed-launch identities. A later same-class target can therefore claim a window already assigned to an earlier target, move it, and report a launch that never created its requested window.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Save two same-class web-app targets A and B with distinct placement.
2. Present A as an already matched current window and leave B missing.
3. Make the authorized B launcher hand off to the existing browser process and focus A without creating B.
4. Observe current correlation accept A as B after settling, dispatch B placement to A, and count B launched.

## Acceptance Criteria
Launch correlation excludes every consumed, reserved, caller-protected, and failed-launch-protected window identity before browser handoff evidence is evaluated. Exclusion is stable-ID aware so true address reuse by a new window remains eligible. Focus transition alone never establishes ownership of a pre-existing sibling. Legitimate new-window and exact-target handoffs continue to work, with one-to-one ownership and convergence on a second pass.
design: Introduce a LaunchCorrelationContext carrying ConsumedWindows observations plus reserved and protected identities into the launch helper and browser handoff predicate. Compare stable IDs when present and use the existing conservative observation identity rules otherwise. Permit a pre-existing candidate only when it proves the exact saved target identity; ordinary handoff candidates must be newly observed. Revalidate the selected identity immediately before dispatch.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover consumed A focused by B, reserved future target, unrelated user focus, failed-launch late window, new stable ID reusing an address, disappeared stable ID, exact saved handoff, Brave positive profile handoff, and ordinary new web-app creation. Stateful e2e uses gqg.36.2 plus gqg.36.3 and asserts exact active-window sequence, candidate exclusions, no dispatch to A, no false launched count, actionable failure, fixed exit status, JSON-only stdout where requested, human stderr separation, ordered redacted JSONL, and idempotent second pass without sleeps.

title: One transient zombie child aborts the whole /proc child walk, silently dropping a terminal's CWD and hint
description:
Root cause: read_task_children (src/process.rs:196-217) returns Err(()) when ANY child's cmdline reads empty (zombie or mid-execve race between readdir and read); get_children (152-176) converts one child failure into whole-call Err(IoError(Interrupted)); get_descendants propagates via '?' (65-81); select_terminal_process maps Err -> None.
Failure: user presses Enter (command finishing) at the instant hyprloom save walks that window's tree -> the readable shell's cwd AND last-command hint are silently dropped for that window; identical data captured 50ms later. Blast radius is all-or-nothing per subtree instead of per-process. Fail-closed but over-broad; ProfileDiscovery.complete already models partial-ness correctly elsewhere.
Fix: distinguish child-gone/empty-cmdline (skip entry, mark partial) from readdir race (fail); retry-read the child /proc entry once before condemning it.
close_reason: Duplicate of hyprloom-production-bug-audit-2026-08-30-gqg.11 — same root cause: all-or-nothing /proc child walk discards valid evidence

title: Config output contradicts active-only Brave capture when no profile map exists
description:
## Problem
main.rs:528-543 labels every unmapped Local State profile as skipped and then says all profiles will be captured when profile_workspaces is absent. capture.rs:225-227 instead retains only profiles positively observed in active Brave process evidence. The same profile is therefore described by two mutually exclusive and inaccurate statements.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create an isolated Brave Local State with Default and Profile 1.
2. Leave apps.brave-browser.profile_workspaces unset.
3. Run hyprloom config.
4. Observe each profile shown as not mapped and skipped followed by a footer claiming all profiles are captured.

## Acceptance Criteria
No-map output says profiles are eligible only when positively observed active and that inactive inventory entries are omitted. A present map prints the configured workspace for mapped entries and skipped for unmapped entries; an empty map skips all. Ordering and wording are deterministic and agree with capture policy.
design: Extract a pure profile-status renderer taking sorted profile inventory and Option<profile_workspaces>. Give None, Some(nonempty), and Some(empty) distinct branches. Keep inventory read failures diagnostic-only and do not make this formatter infer live activity it has not observed.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover none, nonempty, empty, partial map, empty inventory, duplicate-looking names, Unicode display names, and deterministic directory ordering. A simple real-CLI e2e blocked on gqg.36.1 creates private config and Local State fixtures, runs hyprloom config for each mode, and asserts exact stdout lines, stderr behavior, and exit codes; malformed Local State is a negative control. JSONL records only ordered path categories and exit metadata, redacted of profile names where diagnostic logging is not needed. No live Brave or sleeps.

title: Any config parse failure silently defaults autosave_retain=5 and rotation then prunes user snapshots
description:
Root cause: load_config_file (config.rs:195-208) substitutes Config::default() for ANY failure — malformed value, truncated/oversized file, group-writable file, root-owned file from sudo. Default autosave_retain=5 silently replaces the user's retention. The warning goes to stderr, which for the systemd timer path lands only in the journal.
Failure: user sets autosave_retain=1000, later introduces any unrelated TOML type error (restore_delay_ms="500"). Next timer tick (main.rs:603/611): defaults -> capture -> rotate_autosaves(dir,5) irreversibly prunes ~995 snapshots. A read failure silently authorizes destructive pruning at a retention the user never configured.
Fix: on config fallback, hard-fail commands that would prune, or distinguish absent-vs-unreadable and skip rotation in the latter case.
close_reason: Duplicate of hyprloom-production-bug-audit-2026-08-30-gqg.13 — same root cause: config fallback defaults retention then rotation prunes

title: Process start times are jiffies-since-boot but are compared across reboots as process identity
description:
Root cause: process "start time" is /proc stat field 22 — clock TICKS SINCE BOOT (process.rs:233-241) — stored in markers (restore.rs:2303-2311) and sessions, then compared verbatim after a reboot (main.rs:890-896; restore.rs:727-740): both operands are "uptime at their own boot", dimensionally meaningless across boots. No boot epoch (btime) is persisted anywhere.
Failure: reboot between Closing marker and recovery (the normal crash->reboot flow): post-boot process reusing the marker address+PID with similar uptime -> false "same process" -> keeps polling -> timeout -> None -> marker stays -> same permanent lockout as sticky-close-marker-lockout from a DIFFERENT trigger; the mirror error claims a brand-new process IS the saved window's owner (spurious completion evidence in restore matching at 727-740).
Fix: store absolute epoch (btime + starttime) in markers/sessions, or refuse any start-time comparison when the recorded boot epoch differs from the current boot.
close_reason: Rejected as unsupported materiality. Proc field 22 is boot-relative, but ordinary session matching refuses process-only identity at restore.rs:751-777. The marker claim additionally requires simultaneous cross-boot reuse of address, PID, exact start tick, and absent or reused stable ID before recovery at main.rs:833-905; that is not the claimed normal reboot path. Reviser: reopen on an observed production recovery trace satisfying those exact identities.

title: systemctl daemon-reload never called after install/update/uninstall, leaving stale cached units live
description:
Root cause: no systemctl daemon-reload anywhere (grep 0 hits across src/). install (autosave.rs:215-254), uninstall (402-429), and migrate_legacy_units (475-501) write/remove unit files without refreshing systemd's loaded unit cache.
Failure: user relocates the binary and re-runs autosave --install -> ExecStart rewritten, "Created:" printed, but the running user manager keeps firing the OLD cached service (old path — possibly a removed binary or stale hyprloom) until manual daemon-reload/relogin. After uninstall, deleted units remain loaded and the timer can keep firing that session.
Fix: run systemctl --user daemon-reload after the committed marker in install and after removal in uninstall; warn (not silently ignore) on failure.
close_reason: Rejected: successful systemctl enable/disable implicitly reloads unit definitions unless --no-reload is used; install only writes files and instructs enable, while uninstall disables before removal. Actual disable failures are owned by gqg.5.

title: delete_session can destroy the pending replacement's protected safety snapshot, permanently blocking recovery
description:
Root cause: rotate_autosaves deliberately protects the pending replacement backup (session.rs:1204-1207 checks pending_replace_backup), but delete_session (session.rs:463-478) has NO such guard — verified via library API repro: save_session(autosave-x) -> mark_replace_in_progress(autosave-x) -> delete_session(autosave-x) -> Ok.
Failure: user prunes an old-looking autosave-* snapshot (hyprloom list tags it [auto]) while an interrupted replacement names it as its backup. recover_pending_replace -> load_session(backup) -> Err -> return false -> all recovery-requiring commands (including delete and recover) exit 1 with no clearing path — permanent lockout, self-inflicted and silent (same terminal state as sticky-close-marker-lockout).
Fix: refuse (or require --force for) deleting a backup named by a live marker, mirroring the rotation guard; make "backup unrecoverable" a clearable-with-consent state, not a hard block.
close_reason: Rejected as unreachable through the production CLI: the global operation lock and mandatory startup recovery gate run before Delete. The reproduction calls the public storage helper directly and bypasses both guards.

title: dispatch_batch treats hyprctl exit-0-with-per-segment-errors as success, hiding all placement failures
description:
Root cause: RealHyprctl::dispatch_batch (src/hyprctl.rs:195-205) checks only output.status.success(). hyprctl --batch prints per-segment errors but exits 0 even when EVERY segment fails. Verified live on Hyprland 0.56.2: hyprctl --batch "dispatch unknownseg1 ; dispatch unknownseg2" -> both error, exit=0.
Failure: any reconciliation repair via restore.rs:1879 counts success (report.restored += 1 at 1570/1408) while the desktop was untouched; later batch segments keep executing against wrong state. Mocks use the trait default sequential dispatch_batch and always Ok, so the suite cannot see this.
Fix: treat non-empty hyprctl error output as failure (inspect stdout+stderr), or fall back to per-command dispatch with identity revalidation; add a fake that exercises real --batch exit-code semantics.
Priority: every other dispatch-path bug is silently invisible because of this one.
close_reason: Duplicate of hyprloom-production-bug-audit-2026-08-30-gqg.14 — same root cause: dispatch_batch trusts exit-0 only

title: Direct Hyprctl dispatch accepts non-success stdout replies as success
description:
## Problem
RealHyprctl dispatch at src/hyprctl.rs:186-193 checks only process status and discards stdout. Hyprland v0.56.2 hyprctl prints IPC replies to stdout and returns nonzero only for replies beginning with error:, while the server can return Invalid dispatcher or dispatcher-specific error text. A direct dispatch can therefore exit zero, mutate nothing, and be reported by Hyprloom as accepted. Nonzero query branches also lose stdout-only transport diagnostics. Batch reply parsing remains owned by gqg.14.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Put a deterministic fake hyprctl first on PATH.
2. Make direct dispatch return exit 0 with stdout Invalid dispatcher and empty stderr.
3. Invoke a path using direct dispatch, including replacement close.
4. Observe current RealHyprctl return Ok, advance success handling, and omit the rejection reason.

## Acceptance Criteria
Direct dispatch accepts only the documented success reply for the negotiated provider; every other reply is a contextual CommandFailed even with exit 0. Nonzero command errors retain bounded trimmed stdout and stderr without exposing unbounded content. Batch parsing remains separate. Callers never count a rejected direct command as moved, restored, launched, or accepted.
design: Inject a process runner returning status, stdout, and stderr. Centralize bounded lossy diagnostic rendering with command context. For direct dispatch, parse the full provider success token after trimming and reject empty or non-success replies regardless of exit status. For JSON queries, preserve current parsing on success and combine both streams on nonzero. Do not infer batch-member semantics here.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover exit-0 ok, whitespace, Invalid dispatcher, dispatcher-specific rejection, empty stdout, exit-nonzero stdout-only, stderr-only, both streams, invalid UTF-8, oversized output, and command context. Stateful real-CLI e2e blocked on gqg.36.2 drives restore and replacement direct commands, asserts exact argv, no false state transition or success counter, nonzero exit, bounded stderr, JSON-only stdout when applicable, ordered redacted JSONL, and success compatibility. No live compositor or sleeps.

title: Single-dispatch path strips quotes, corrupting workspace names with spaces
description:
Root cause: on the single-dispatch path, RealHyprctl::dispatch re-tokenizes the command with parse_dispatch_args (hyprctl.rs:269-329), which strips quotes, then passes tokens as argv; hyprctl rejoins them with plain spaces (verified via live error echo). quote_dispatch_token (placement.rs:214-222) quoting survives only on the batch path. The comment at hyprctl.rs:221-223 ("single-dispatch parser and batch builder cannot drift apart") is false — they drift in opposite directions.
Failure: saved named workspace "Writing Desk" -> movetoworkspacesilent 'name:Writing Desk' arrives as ... name:Writing Desk,address:0x1 -> whitespace tokenizer sees phantom workspace "Writing", the address token is orphaned; window goes nowhere or to the wrong workspace. Unit test hyprctl.rs:425-434 checks only the isolated parser, never the wire.
Fix: don't re-tokenize for the single path (pass raw quoted string) or re-quote tokens when rejoining; test through a fake hyprctl-join boundary.
close_reason: Rejected: the single-dispatch parser removes quote delimiters but preserves the spaced workspace as one argv element; hyprctl retains the full dispatcher remainder. The real inverse batch-quoting defect is gqg.15.

title: Legacy dispatch strings are incompatible with Hyprland Lua providers
description:
## Problem
README declares Hyprland 0.54+ support. placement.rs:224-329 emits legacy dispatcher strings and hyprctl.rs:186-204 sends them without provider negotiation. In Hyprland v0.56.2 Lua mode, dispatch evaluates hl.dispatch(<input>); legacy tokens are not valid Lua dispatcher objects. Direct close, focus, workspace and monitor moves, geometry, state repairs, and recovery can therefore fail after a supported configuration switches provider.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure the stateful Hyprland fixture for the pinned v0.56.2 Lua provider.
2. Load a valid session requiring at least one placement repair, and separately a replacement requiring close.
3. Run restore, reconcile, and replacement through RealHyprctl transport.
4. Observe current legacy token payloads rejected; replacement can already have entered its destructive workflow before full capability is known.

## Acceptance Criteria
Hyprloom negotiates provider capability with a read-only probe and emits verified typed operations for supported legacy and Lua providers without a version-only guess. Every required operation is preflight-serializable before replacement closes a window. Unsupported or ambiguous capability fails closed with the logical operation named. Direct and batch transports preserve exact ordering, identity selection, and real compositor errors.
design: Define a typed DispatchOp model for close, focus, workspace and monitor movement, geometry, floating, pin, and both fullscreen channels. Detect provider once through a read-only capability probe. Implement independent legacy and Lua serializers from logical values, not prequoted command strings. Preflight the complete replacement operation set. Keep batch framing and member-reply validation delegated to gqg.15 and gqg.14 while preserving atomic focus-sensitive sequences.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover every DispatchOp and value edge under pinned legacy 0.54 and Lua 0.56.2 grammars, provider probe success, unsupported, malformed, and version/provider disagreement, plus serialization rejection before mutation. Real-CLI e2e blocked on gqg.36.2 runs normal restore, both reconcile strategies, replacement, recovery, and dry-run through provider fakes; assert exact argv and batch order, server-observed logical state, zero close on failed preflight, exit/status counters, stdout/stderr contracts, ordered redacted JSONL, negative dialect controls, and second-pass convergence without live Hyprland or sleeps.

title: Dry-run launch placement plan diverges from the real executor
description:
## Problem
Dry-run renders build_dispatch_commands_for_monitor at restore.rs:4020-4051, while real launch uses direct process spawn followed by build_reconcile_dispatch_commands_with_geometry at placement.rs:262-329 against the observed window. Dry-run invents a hyprctl exec, uses different operation order, prints geometry real mode suppresses for fullscreen, and cannot omit already-satisfied state. The preview is not the execution plan.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create targets covering floating, fullscreen, pinned, absent-monitor, and already-matching mapped-window states.
2. Run dry-run and record its rendered spawn and dispatch plan.
3. Run the same deterministic scenario with fixture-controlled mapped window observations.
4. Compare current output with actual process and Hyprctl traces and observe differing transport, command set, and order.

## Acceptance Criteria
Dry-run and execution share one typed launch and placement intent. Preview renders the real argv and explicitly conditional post-map placement rather than a fictitious exec command or synthesized observation. Eligibility, trust, ambiguity, and failure decisions are identical before the mode split. Dry-run performs no spawn, dispatch, filesystem mutation, or state change.
design: Introduce LaunchPlan containing authorized argv and a typed placement goal. Render argv separately from conditional placement intent. Real mode spawns argv, observes the correlated window, and realizes the same goal with the common placement planner; dry-run does not fabricate current geometry. Move all identity and safety guards before dry-run branching and keep provider-specific serialization downstream.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover tiled, floating, fullscreen, pinned, named workspace, missing monitor, binary failure, ambiguous identity, and actual window states that are already correct or partly mismatched. E2e blocked on gqg.36.2 and gqg.36.3 compares dry-run intent with deterministic real process and dispatch traces; assert no fake exec, exact argv and operation order, zero dry-run mutation, identical eligibility and exit semantics, stable human stdout, parseable JSON-only stdout, stderr diagnostics, ordered redacted JSONL, negative controls, and second-pass convergence without sleeps.

comments.author: thethracian
comments.text: Second finding of same divergent-builder root cause: the SPAWN dry-run preview (restore.rs:4020-4051 used at 3031-3033) additionally lists geometry BEFORE togglefloating for a freshly spawned tiled window (impossible to apply, F1-class), prints 'exec ...' though real launches go through the process spawner, and shows a placeholder address:0xNEW that matches nothing.

title: Define and implement policy-gated empty-workspace topology restore
description:
## Problem
capture.rs:41-98 and the Session schema in session.rs:59-174 persist windows and monitor geometry, not independent workspace topology. Empty focused workspaces and workspace-to-monitor bindings therefore cannot be represented. This is a feature-policy gap, not a demonstrated regression: additive restore must not move live workspaces containing unmatched user windows, and no current Canon rule defines topology precedence.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. In the stateful Hyprland fixture, create an empty focused named workspace bound to a monitor and save a session.
2. Change or remove that workspace before restore.
3. Run normal restore, reconcile, replacement, and dry-run.
4. Observe that current snapshots contain no topology record and no mode can describe or recreate it.

## Acceptance Criteria
Implementation begins only after decision gqg.38 defines mode-specific ownership, precedence, invalid cases, and focus behavior. The approved schema is backward compatible, capture represents the allowed topology, and restore applies only authorized topology changes without moving extras or stealing focus. Missing monitors, named and special workspaces, conflicts, dry-run, reporting, and repeated convergence follow the decision exactly.
design: This feature is blocked on gqg.38. After that decision, add an optional default-empty workspace topology field, Hyprctl workspace observation, and typed topology plan. Keep additive and destructive behavior separate, preserve legacy sessions, and reject any topology action not supported by the decided contract. Use the stateful fixture to model workspace lifetimes and monitor bindings before source implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Unit contract tests first encode every outcome from gqg.38: legacy JSON, empty focused workspace capture, numeric, named, and special workspaces, monitor disappearance, conflicting live topology, unmatched windows, normal restore, both reconciliation strategies, replacement, recovery, dry-run, and reporting. Stateful actual-CLI e2e is blocked on gqg.36.2 and asserts exact workspace operations, focus and pointer state, exit status, stdout/stderr, ordered redacted JSONL, compatibility controls, no live compositor or sleeps, and second-pass convergence.

title: escape_batch_command backslash/semicolon escaping is ignored by hyprctl's batch splitter
description:
Root cause: escape_batch_command (hyprctl.rs:232-246) escapes \ -> \\ and ; -> \; assuming hyprctl's batch splitter honors escapes. Verified live: it does not — ';' inside quotes splits the batch mid-command ("invalid escape sequence near ...", leftover fragment sent as separate request), and a literal backslash reaches the compositor unpaired.
Failure: workspace legally named "Fun;Desk" (embedded by placement.rs:198) corrupts the whole repair batch: that command, the next command, and everything after receive torn fragments; exit status stays 0 so nothing is reported (compounds dispatch-batch-exit0-masks-errors).
Fix: cannot escape at this layer — detect ; or \ in any token and route that window through single dispatch (after fixing dispatch-quote-stripping-named-workspaces) or the socket API per-command; stop emitting escapes the parser ignores.
close_reason: Duplicate of gqg.15: semicolon/backslash failure is another case of serializing shell-like tokens into Hyprland raw batch grammar; delimiter coverage was folded into the owner.

title: Global operation lock makes every CLI command wait silently behind long restore
description:
## Problem
main.rs:120-143 acquires one blocking OperationLock before every command, and session.rs:283-315 calls file.lock without a nonblocking observation or notice. A list, config, status, or autosave invocation behind a multi-window restore can therefore appear hung with no output. The previous claim that the generated Type=oneshot service receives the manager default 90-second startup timeout was false: oneshot startup timeout is disabled by default, so autosave normally waits and later runs.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Use the locking fixture to acquire the real Hyprloom operation lock and signal readiness.
2. Start hyprloom list, config, or autosave --now in a second isolated CLI process.
3. Keep the holder active without using a timed sleep.
4. Observe that current code emits no stdout or stderr until the holder releases the lock.

## Acceptance Criteria
A contending CLI detects the busy lock and immediately emits one bounded stderr notice before preserving current serialized waiting behavior. No command runs migration, storage, restore, or autosave work concurrently. After release it completes normally. This bead does not introduce fail-fast, skip, timeout, or holder-kill policy.
design: Add OperationLock try_acquire or an equivalent busy probe. On WouldBlock, write a single contention diagnostic and then take the existing blocking lock. Keep the lock lifecycle and exclusive serialization unchanged. Any optional holder PID or start identity is diagnostic only and must never authorize unlock or process termination.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover immediate acquire, busy detection, release, holder process exit, malformed lock metadata, and exactly-once notice. A two-process real-CLI e2e blocked on gqg.36.4 coordinates through fixture readiness events, asserts the waiter emits stderr before release, produces no premature stdout or side effect, then completes with exact output and exit status after release. Ordered redacted JSONL proves acquire and release order. Include list, config, autosave, and mutating-command controls; no sleeps, live systemd, forced signal, or nondeterministic timeout.

title: Focus-based repairs can change user focus, workspaces, and pointer state
description:
## Problem
placement.rs:224-231 and 284-326 emit focuswindow before focus-only monitor and fullscreen operations, and restore.rs:1851-1880 executes the sequence as a batch. Focusing an inactive-workspace target can change active monitor workspaces and warp the pointer. Nothing restores the complete interaction context. Simply appending focuswindow for the prior address is insufficient and can overwrite concurrent user input.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. In the stateful Hyprland fixture, focus a window on monitor A and record all active workspaces plus cursor coordinates.
2. Put a repair target on an inactive workspace on monitor B requiring a focus-only monitor or fullscreen action.
3. Run background reconciliation while the fixture also models a user focus or pointer change at the allowed event boundary.
4. Observe current repair leave focus, monitor workspace, or pointer at the target-derived state.

## Acceptance Criteria
Address-targetable provider operations do not change focus. A legacy focus-only fallback preserves the full pre-operation context only when it is still current; it never restores a stale snapshot over concurrent user input. If exact noninterference cannot be proved, the focus-only repair is skipped or reported as partial failure rather than success. All target and context identities are revalidated.
design: Use the typed provider operations from the Lua-dispatch work whenever they support an explicit window target. For legacy focus-only actions, capture an interaction-context generation plus active window, per-monitor active workspaces, and cursor. Execute target action and conditional compare-and-restore in one transport transaction; restore only if no user-input generation changed. When provider capability, identity, or conditional restoration is unavailable, return a typed incomplete outcome without guessing.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover address-targeted no-focus commands, inactive-workspace target, multiple monitors, fullscreen and monitor moves, prior-window disappearance, address reuse, partial dispatch failure, and user focus, workspace, or pointer input before and during the operation. Stateful real-CLI e2e blocked on gqg.36.2 asserts exact argv and operation order, final focus/workspace/cursor state, no stale-context overwrite, correct partial-failure counters and exit, JSON-only stdout, human stderr, ordered redacted JSONL with input generations, negative controls, and second-pass convergence without sleeps.

title: fullscreenstate emits invalid real-mode value 2 for maximized windows
description:
Root cause: placement.rs:320-323 emits fullscreenstate <val> <val> duplicating the internal value. Legacy semantics: fullscreenstate <internal:0|1|2> <real:0|1>. A captured maximized window (fullscreen=2) produces "2 2" — real mode out of domain. Related: placement.rs:224-232 movewindow 'mon:X' silent uses a trailing argument whose syntax is not confirmed for movewindow (silent variants exist on movetoworkspace/workspace).
Failure: maximized window restore sends malformed fullscreen command -> window ends plain-tiled or errors (invisible under dispatch-batch-exit0-masks-errors and dispatch-syntax-incompatible-hyprland-056). Confidence: likely — could not empirically confirm on 0.56 because legacy syntax is dead there.
Fix: map internal -> (internal, real) explicitly (2 -> "2 0"); verify monitor-move dispatcher signature against the target Hyprland dialect during the 0.56 syntax fix.
close_reason: Duplicate consequence of gqg.16 with a false mechanism in this record: Hyprland permits client fullscreen state 2, but Hyprloom still loses and fabricates the independent client channel as documented by gqg.16.

comments.author: codex-audit
comments.text: Reopened: Reopening only to correct the imported close rationale: client state 2 is valid; the retained issue is independent-state loss, not an invalid-domain value.

title: dirs fallback is literal ~/... path: storage and systemd units land relative to CWD
description:
Root cause (verified in code): dirs::config_dir()/data_dir() fallbacks use unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("~/.config"|~/.local/share")) at config.rs:294-297,303-306,312-316,321-325 and autosave.rs:22-27 (systemd_user_dir). '~' is never expanded; the path is RELATIVE. dirs-sys only returns None exactly when HOME/XDG are unusable (relative/empty/unset), so the fallback fires precisely when it is wrong. Safety checks pass because create_dir_all makes the process own the ./~ tree it just built.
Failure: env -u HOME hyprloom autosave --install -> writes ./~/.config/systemd/user/hyprloom-autosave.*, prints absolute-looking paths, claims success; systemd never loads them; status says "not configured". env -u HOME hyprloom save x -> snapshots land in CWD-relative ./~/.local/share/hyprloom/sessions (session JSON with cwd/titles written wherever the command ran; only the leaf dir forced 0700); from any other CWD the store appears empty.
Fix: when dirs returns None, fail with an explicit error ("set XDG_DATA_HOME or HOME") like operation_lock_dir already does (session.rs:318-329); never substitute an unexpandable literal.
close_reason: Rejected as lacking an ordinary reachable trigger: dirs-sys falls back to the account home through getpwuid when HOME is unset, and a true no-home environment normally fails OperationLock before these mutation paths.

title: Last-command hint is space-joined argv, so restore re-executes corrupted commands with quoted/empty args
description:
Root cause: read_cmdline (src/process.rs:219-231) rebuilds the terminal last-command hint by joining argv with single spaces after dropping empty and non-UTF-8 elements; capture.rs:270-279 stores it verbatim; restore.rs:3858-3862 re-executes it through sh -c '<hint>; exec zsh'.
Failure: user ran nvim "my file.txt" -> hint "nvim my file.txt" -> restore opens TWO empty buffers (my, file.txt). find . -name "" -type f loses the empty arg and shifts arguments, changing semantics. Single-quote escaping prevents injection but not corruption.
Fix: shell-quote each argv element when joining (POSIX single-quote escaping), or store the hint as an argv vector and let the restore layer build the -c content.
close_reason: Rejected because the claimed semantic corruption cannot occur: restore single-quotes and echoes the hint, then starts a shell; it never re-executes the captured argv. Remaining display fidelity is a nitpick; substantive wrong-command selection is gqg.8.

title: Legacy migration puts user snapshots in the autosave deletion namespace
description:
## Problem
Current user saves reject autosave- names at session.rs:520-528, but migrate_legacy_sessions at session.rs:544-610 accepts them and copies them unchanged. rotate_autosaves at session.rs:1180-1217 treats every autosave- snapshot as generated retention data. A valid historical user snapshot can therefore be deleted by an ordinary later autosave, including immediately when retention is zero.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Put a valid legacy user snapshot named autosave-0-archive.json in the isolated legacy directory.
2. Run a Hyprloom command to perform migration.
3. Run enough deterministic autosaves to exceed retention, or configure retention zero.
4. Observe current rotation delete the migrated user snapshot solely because of its prefix.

## Acceptance Criteria
Every migrated reserved-prefix source is durably preserved outside automatic retention without pretending provenance can distinguish a historical generated autosave from a user save. Source data remains intact, destination name and payload agree, collision handling is deterministic and fail-closed, migration is idempotent, and no completion marker is committed while a valid source is unresolved.
design: Rename every migrated autosave-prefixed source into a deterministic valid nonreserved namespace and rewrite only Session.name to match. Preserve created_at and all client data. Use a bounded basename with digest suffix for length and collision safety. Treat an equivalent existing destination as idempotent; a different collision or write failure prevents the migration marker. Retain all legacy source files as rollback data.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover positive and zero retention, ordering around generated names, maximum-length input, deterministic digest collision names, equivalent and different existing destinations, interrupted writes, marker idempotence, filename and payload agreement, source preservation, list, load, and delete. Real-CLI e2e blocked on gqg.36.4 migrates fixed legacy fixtures, performs fake autosave and rotation, and asserts exact paths, bytes except rewritten name, survival, exit code, stdout/stderr, ordered redacted JSONL, negative malformed and unsafe sources, and second-pass convergence without sleeps.

title: Plain restore can assign a late failed-launch window to a later target
description:
## Problem
The plain restore launch path at restore.rs:1498-1518 records no observation baseline after a spawned target times out. Reconciliation separately protects windows created after failed launches at restore.rs:2452-2457, 2757, and 3097-3116. A still-running target A can map late and be claimed through broad fallback as later same-identity target B, moved to B placement, and counted as B.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Save same-identity targets A and B with an intervening distinct target.
2. Launch A through the deterministic fixture and make its window appear only after A times out.
3. Complete the intervening target, then begin B.
4. Observe current plain restore select late A as B, dispatch B placement to it, and never create the requested B window.

## Acceptance Criteria
Plain restore retains failed-launch baselines and excludes every later-created protected window from subsequent matching, handoff, and launch correlation without killing the late process. Protection is stable-identity aware and allows true address reuse. Each requested target receives its own accurate outcome and repeated restore converges without stealing prior work.
design: Share a FailedLaunchLedger between plain restore and reconciliation. Snapshot observed identities immediately before each spawn. On every post-spawn correlation error, retain that baseline and classify newly observed stable identities as protected before later matching or correlation. Pass the protected observation set through browser handoff and existing-window lookup. Use stable ID first and conservative legacy identity fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover late A with intervening target and B, multiple failed launches, exact and reused addresses, new stable ID reuse, legitimate pre-existing B, browser handoff, launcher exit, timeout, retry, and dry-run. Real-CLI e2e blocked on gqg.36.2 and gqg.36.3 drives deterministic process and client event sequences and asserts late A is never dispatched or counted as B, exact spawn and dispatch order, per-target counters, nonzero exit, human stdout/stderr, report JSON where supported, ordered redacted JSONL, negative controls, and second-pass convergence without sleeps.

title: Session listing silently omits unsafe or unreadable snapshot candidates
description:
## Problem
list_sessions at session.rs:418-455 continues past each candidate-level failure: irregular or unsafe path, ownership failure, oversized read, JSON error, structure limit, and payload-name mismatch. main.rs:482-504 then prints a truncated list or No saved sessions and exits zero. Restore of the same named file fails, so operators and automation receive contradictory store state.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. In an isolated sessions directory, place one valid session and one candidate .json that is a symlink, wrong-owner file, malformed JSON, oversized payload, or name mismatch.
2. Run hyprloom list.
3. Observe current output include only the valid session, or claim none exist, with empty diagnostics and exit 0.
4. Run restore for the omitted name and observe the explicit failure.

## Acceptance Criteria
Listing returns valid summaries plus ordered typed diagnostics for every session-candidate failure. The CLI prints valid summaries only on stdout, bounded basename and category diagnostics on stderr, and exits nonzero when any candidate was omitted. It never prints No saved sessions when diagnostics exist. Rotation performs no deletion from an incomplete autosave scan. Non-session files remain ignored by documented grammar.
design: Introduce a SessionScan result containing summaries and per-candidate diagnostic categories. Identify candidates by supported .json naming before checking file type and safety. Keep user-owned wrong-mode repair behavior, but report wrong owner, symlink, irregular type, read, size, JSON, structure, and name mismatch distinctly. Sort both outputs deterministically. Require a complete autosave scan before retention deletes anything.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover every diagnostic alone and mixed with valid sessions, wrong mode versus wrong owner, symlink, directory, malformed and oversized JSON, structural limits, name mismatch, stable sorting, unrelated non-JSON files, atomic temp files, and replacement markers. Real-CLI e2e blocked on gqg.36.4 asserts partial stdout, ordered bounded stderr, exit 1, absence of misleading empty text, no retention deletion after incomplete scan, exact ordered redacted JSONL, clean-store compatibility, and deterministic repeated results without live storage or sleeps.

title: Login-shell argv0 (-zsh/-bash) never recognized, silently disabling kitty CWD/hint capture
description:
Root cause: is_plain_shell (src/process.rs:247-258) matches argv0 via Path::new(cmd).file_name() against zsh|bash|fish|sh without stripping a leading '-'. POSIX login shells expose argv0 as "-zsh"/"-bash". Verified: is_plain_shell("-zsh") == false. The loop below only tolerates leading '-' in LATER arguments.
Failure: kitty start_with_login_shell defaults to YES on Linux and kitty implements it by prefixing argv0 with '-'. With [apps.kitty] capture_cwd=true (the headline feature), select_terminal_process counts 0 plain shells -> None -> every real kitty window stores NO --directory arg and NO last-command hint, silently. Unit tests only feed "zsh", so CI is green while capture is dead in production.
Fix: strip a single leading '-' from argv0 before the file_name match (do not strip '--').
close_reason: Rejected as a custom-wrapper edge, not the claimed Kitty default: Kitty starts the configured shell normally and documents login flags as explicit configuration. No ordinary leading-dash argv0 trigger was established.

title: --max-age login guard misjudges clock state: wall-clock rewind between save and boot silently skips session restore
description:
Root cause: login restore guard computes age = Utc::now() - session.created_at (main.rs:245) from two wall-clock instants possibly on different clock epochs; exec-once (main.rs:199) typically runs BEFORE systemd-timesyncd finishes, races RTC sync, and runs exactly once per boot.
Failure: clock stepped forward at save time (NTP during session, VM rollback, dual-boot RTC-as-localtime) -> at boot now < created_at -> age<0 -> "session has a future timestamp" skip with notice, exit 0; exec-once consumed -> NO restore on login. Backward step mirrors it as false "too old". The least-trustworthy clock reading gates the most important restore.
Fix: treat negative age on the login path as clock skew: wait for time sync (poll /run/systemd/timesync or CLOCK_REALTIME vs /proc/uptime sanity) or clamp with tolerance rather than skip.
close_reason: Rejected as defensive policy invention. main.rs:242-269 detects a future timestamp, reports it, and fails closed because cross-boot age is not trustworthy. Polling time sync, clamping, or restoring anyway would weaken the stale-session guard without an approved trusted-time and retry contract. Reviser: reopen on repeated ordinary correctly configured boot traces showing pre-sync failure plus an owner-supplied authoritative time-readiness and retry policy.

title: Migration silently drops valid legacy sessions when destination is a dangling symlink, then writes completion marker
description:
Root cause: migration 'do not overwrite existing Hyprloom snapshots' is implemented as 'any filesystem object exists at the destination' — session.rs:577-579 symlink_metadata(&destination).is_ok() -> continue — including BROKEN SYMLINKS and directories, which are not snapshots. The completion marker is then written unconditionally at loop end (session.rs:609), so the candidate is never revisited. Reproduced.
Failure: legacy work.json valid + destination work.json is a dangling symlink (dotfile-sync leftover) -> copied=0, .hyprflow-migration-complete written, session_exists("work")==false, load/delete both fail UnsafePath: the session is invisible in list, unrecoverable via CLI, and migration reported success. Violates storage-and-recovery canon invariant 3 (skip only malformed/oversized SOURCES).
Fix: count only a loadable regular-file destination as existing; on symlink/irregular destinations either report a migration failure (defer the marker) or replace non-snapshot objects atomically (rename already replaces links without following).
close_reason: Rejected as an exceptional external-filesystem obstruction: Hyprloom creates no dangling destination symlink, retains the valid legacy source, and does not make it unrecoverable. The claim overstates data loss.

title: Connector reuse or swapped enumeration can bind saved geometry to the wrong physical monitor
description:
Root cause: monitor matching is connector-name-only: find_monitor_by_name (placement.rs:10-15); HyprMonitor (hyprctl.rs:63-81) does not parse make/model/serial/description (verified present on live hyprctl monitors -j) and saved Monitor (session.rs:77-95, capture.rs:50-60) stores only name+w/h/transform/x/y. No serial/position fallback exists.
Failure: after dock replug/reboot, connector reuse or swapped enumeration can make DP-1 denote a different physical display -> adapt_client_geometry (placement.rs:28-36) confidently rescales and re-anchors ALL saved geometry onto the wrong physical monitor and actively moves windows there. If the name is simply gone, placement is skipped with no position-based recovery (windows land on whatever is focused, compounding movewindow-mon-clobbers-workspace).
Fix: capture identity attributes (make/model/serial, position as tiebreak); match unique physical identity first; use connector fallback only for legacy or incomplete identity; same-name-different-serial is a positive conflict that refuses automatic monitor/geometry movement.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Save a session with physical monitor A exposed as DP-1 and a window with monitor-relative geometry.
2. Script the next compositor state with A exposed as DP-2 and physical monitor B exposed as DP-1.
3. Reconcile the session.
4. Observe that connector-only lookup selects B and applies A's geometry there instead of proving physical identity or reporting the saved monitor unavailable.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires the deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence specified there while preserving existing supported behavior and failing closed on ambiguity or external-command rejection.
design: Extend captured and persisted monitor metadata with optional make, model, serial, and description while retaining the existing connector name and backward-compatible serde defaults. Resolve a saved monitor by unique physical identity first. When both saved and current physical identifiers are present and conflict, do not fall back to the reused connector; treat the target monitor as unavailable and leave unrelated windows untouched. Use connector-name fallback only for legacy or genuinely incomplete identity, require uniqueness, and keep existing monitor-origin/geometry adaptation and additive-extra behavior. Centralize the resolver so plain restore, reconcile, replacement, and recovery cannot diverge.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests cover exact physical identity, connector renumbering, two connectors swapping physical monitors, positive serial conflict, missing/duplicate serials, description-only ambiguity, negative origins, and legacy snapshots containing only connector names. Serialization tests prove old sessions still load and new optional fields round-trip. Actual-CLI e2e uses the stateful fake-Hyprland fixture to run save then reconcile with scripted A/B monitor swaps; assert the exact ordered monitor queries and dispatches, final window/monitor state, complete versus unavailable report status, exit code, stdout/stderr separation, and mutation-free second pass. Capture bounded redacted JSONL with normalized argv and before/after monitor identities, never titles/CWD/user content. Include unchanged-layout and extra-window preservation controls. Use readiness signals only—no sleeps or live compositor. In --report-json mode stdout is exactly one JSON document and diagnostics are stderr-only.

title: movewindow mon:X after movetoworkspacesilent destroys the workspace assignment, breaking reconcile idempotency
description:
Root cause: placement plan dispatches movetoworkspacesilent N,address:... FIRST (creating the missing workspace on the CURRENTLY FOCUSED monitor — Hyprland resolveWorkspace, DispatcherTranslator.cpp:342-352 v0.56.2) and THEN movewindow mon:X, which Hyprland implements as a WORKSPACE move to the target monitor's ACTIVE workspace (DispatcherTranslator.cpp:383-394) — clobbering the workspace assignment. The comment at placement.rs:295-296 ("so the final placement wins") encodes the wrong model.
Failure: reconcile into a fresh boot (saved window ws 4 on DP-3, focus elsewhere): window lands on DP-3's active ws, NOT ws 4; phantom empty ws 4 left on the focused monitor; every subsequent reconcile re-issues movews (ws mismatch) then movewindow mon (monitor mismatch) -> permanent ping-pong, never idempotent. Violates session-operations canon "repeated reconciliation must be idempotent". Mocks only record strings and never model ws/monitor state (hyprctl.rs:340-373) so tests cannot see it. Verified against Hyprland 0.56.2 source and code order (restore.rs:3697-3704, placement.rs:288-299).
Fix: bind the WORKSPACE to the monitor (moveworkspacetomonitor) or ensure ws is created on the saved monitor (focus it there first); drop movewindow mon: when a workspace move for the same window is planned; add a stateful mock modeling active-ws semantics.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Save a window assigned to workspace 3 on DP-1.
2. Before reconcile, make workspace 9 the active workspace on DP-1 and place the window elsewhere.
3. Reconcile.
4. Observe movetoworkspacesilent 3 followed by movewindow mon:DP-1; Hyprland moves the window to DP-1's active workspace 9, so the saved workspace is lost and the next reconcile repeats the repair.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires the deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence specified there while preserving existing supported behavior and failing closed on ambiguity or external-command rejection.
design: Plan workspace and monitor placement as one transition. When a monitor correction is required, move the addressed window to the target monitor first and assign the exact saved workspace afterward, then refresh and verify both postconditions before reporting success. If an existing workspace-to-monitor binding makes both targets impossible without moving unrelated windows or workspace topology, fail that window explicitly rather than moving the whole workspace. Preserve focus, unrelated workspaces, extra windows, named/special workspace syntax, and the existing additive reconciliation contract.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests use a stateful compositor model where movewindow mon selects the destination monitor's active workspace. Cover inactive desired workspace, named/numeric/special workspaces, no monitor change, existing desired binding on another monitor, command failure at each step, and final-state verification. Actual-CLI e2e uses the fake-Hyprland fixture with DP-1 active on workspace 9 and saved target workspace 3; assert exact query/dispatch order, final monitor and workspace, focus preservation, report and exit truth, and an empty mutation log on the second reconcile. Record bounded redacted JSONL with logical before/after state and exact argv; no sleeps or live compositor. Preserve extra windows and unrelated workspace bindings. In --report-json mode stdout is one JSON document only and diagnostics remain on stderr.

title: restore --on-login silently accepts and discards --max-age/--dry-run/session name, hardcoding 24h
description:
Root cause: restore --on-login is handled by early return at main.rs:196-204, before any other handling, emitting a FIXED string; clap wiring (main.rs:76-80) has no conflicts_with/requires tying max_age/dry_run/name to on_login (only report_json conflicts).
Failure (reproduced): hyprloom restore tricky --on-login --max-age 1h -> stdout: exec-once = hyprloom restore --reconcile --max-age 24h, exit 0. A user scripting hyprloom restore --on-login --max-age 1h >> hyprland.conf silently gets 24h behavior. --dry-run and the session name likewise accepted and discarded. Contrast: other invalid combos correctly rejected with exit 2.
Fix: interpolate max_age (and honor dry_run) into the emitted line, or conflicts_with_all = [max_age, dry_run, greedy, name] on on_login.
close_reason: Rejected as a low-impact CLI validation issue: --on-login is documented and designed as a fixed 24-hour configuration-line generator. Accepting irrelevant combined flags is UX, not a material production failure.

title: Pin/unpin dispatches violate 0.56.2 preconditions (floating, not-fullscreen): rejected forever or fixed only on second pass
description:
Root cause: placement.rs:281-283 emits unpin BEFORE the fullscreen-exit block (284-287) and placement.rs:325-327 emits pin even when the planned final state is tiled. Actions::pinWindow (ConfigActions.cpp:225-231) hard-rejects !floating || fullscreen. Real reachable states: pinned+tiled (windowrule pin writes m_pinned; floatWindow never clears it) and pinned+fullscreen (no guard in fullscreenWindow) — live host JSON exposes both.
Failure (verified vs 0.56.2 source): (1) saved pinned+fullscreen target unpinned: batch sends pin (rejected, still fullscreen) then fullscreenstate 0 0 -> window stays pinned (appears on every workspace) though target said unpinned; fixes itself only on a SECOND restore pass. (2) pinned+tiled target: pin rejected every run -> window never pins, reported Moved forever, never Unchanged.
Fix: exit fullscreen before unpin; when target is tiled and a pin toggle is planned wrap setfloating->pin->settiled; drop unsatisfiable pin diffs from the plan.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Script a current pinned fullscreen window whose saved target is unpinned, and separately a current tiled window whose saved target is pinned/floating.
2. Reconcile each case.
3. Observe unpin emitted before leaving fullscreen, or pin emitted while the window is tiled.
4. The compositor rejects the transition, yet later commands/reporting can continue and a second pass may repeat or partially repair it.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires the deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence specified there while preserving existing supported behavior and failing closed on ambiguity or external-command rejection.
design: Introduce one legal window-state transition planner shared by ordinary placement, Brave repair, replacement, and recovery. Exit internal/client fullscreen before unpinning, establish floating state before pinning or pixel geometry, perform workspace/monitor/geometry operations while legal, then restore target pin and both fullscreen channels. Reject contradictory target state before mutation. Execute the plan through the common checked-dispatch path and verify final state before success; preserve already-correct windows and unrelated extras.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic unit/property tests cover the cross-product of current/target pinned, floating, internal fullscreen, and client fullscreen states, including contradictory saved state and an injected rejection at every transition. Assert exact legal ordering and no redundant commands. Actual-CLI e2e uses the stateful fake-Hyprland fixture, whose dispatch implementation enforces pin/unpin preconditions; assert exact argv/state transitions, final state, nonzero exit and failed report on rejection, stdout/stderr separation, and mutation-free second pass after success. JSONL evidence is bounded/redacted and excludes real titles/CWD/commands. Include legacy single-fullscreen sessions, already-correct and extra-window controls, no sleeps/live compositor, and JSON-only stdout where report JSON is supported.

title: Pinned windows cannot enter special workspaces: move silently dropped, repair never converges
description:
Root cause: CGlobalWindowController::moveWindowToWorkspace (GlobalWindowController.cpp:39-40, v0.56.2) silently returns when window is pinned AND destination is a special workspace. The planner (placement.rs:281-294) emits unpin only when the TARGET is unpinned, yet still issues movetoworkspacesilent special:X against a currently-pinned window.
Failure (verified source): user pinned a window while special:1 was visible (pinWindow succeeds against the regular active ws); session stores pinned=true + workspace_name=special:1; window later lives on ws 2 -> plan is the single command movetoworkspacesilent special:1,address:X -> compositor drops it silently -> window stays on ws 2 forever, every restore re-plans the same no-op, reported Moved, never Unchanged.
Fix: when workspace_selector(target) is special and current.pinned: emit unpin -> move -> re-pin.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Save a pinned floating window on a special workspace.
2. Place the same pinned window on a regular workspace.
3. Reconcile while the target remains pinned.
4. Observe the workspace move is issued without a temporary unpin, is rejected by Hyprland, and the repair never converges although pin is already the desired final state.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires the deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence specified there while preserving existing supported behavior and failing closed on ambiguity or external-command rejection.
design: Keep this as a distinct workspace-transition defect but implement it on the legal state planner owned by hyprloom-pin-precondition-rejections-4nh. Whenever a pinned current window must change workspace, temporarily leave fullscreen if necessary, unpin, perform and verify the regular/special workspace move, then restore pin if the target is pinned. Do not unpin an already-correct window, do not change unrelated windows, and fail closed if any intermediate transition is rejected.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover regular-to-special, special-to-regular, named special workspaces, target pinned/unpinned, fullscreen combinations, already-correct placement, and rejection at unpin/move/repin. Assert exact command order and final pin/workspace state. Actual-CLI e2e uses the stateful fake-Hyprland fixture enforcing pinned-move rejection; assert exact argv and ordered states, truthful report/exit/output channels, preserved extras, and zero second-pass mutations. Evidence is bounded redacted JSONL with synthetic identifiers only; use readiness signals, no sleeps or live compositor, and exactly one stdout JSON document in supported report mode.

title: Production bug audit findings (2026-08-30)
description:
Tracking epic for production defects found during a multi-wave read-only audit of Hyprloom.

Scope: correctness, reliability, security, and material production performance. Nitpicks, speculative hardening, and purely defensive-design suggestions are excluded. Every retained child must identify its observable trigger, underlying causal boundary, user impact, safe design, compatibility constraints, and evidence that could overturn the conclusion.

This epic documents and sequences findings; it does not itself authorize source or Canon changes. Policy-dependent work remains gated by an explicit decision Bead.

## Success Criteria

- Every live child is a distinct material defect, verification-infrastructure task, or explicitly labeled policy/feature item; duplicates and falsified claims are closed with evidence and linked to the canonical owner when one exists.
- Designs preserve established functionality, additive restore semantics, current unrelated windows, old data formats, dry-run nonmutation, and conservative replacement recovery.
- Dependencies express real implementation ordering rather than topic similarity; related edges record coordination without manufacturing blockers; the graph is acyclic.
- Every retained implementation child requires comprehensive deterministic unit tests and real-CLI e2e regressions with ordered redacted evidence, exact state/exit/output assertions, negative controls, and compatibility/idempotence coverage.
- Completion is determined from the live child rollup and passing Beads lint/dependency validation, not stale historical counts.
design: Triage each candidate at its smallest causal boundary: retain only reproducible material production defects; consolidate shared roots under one canonical owner; close false, purely timing-universal, policy-free, or duplicate claims with a discriminating reviser. Sequence foundational safety contracts first (typed config loading, full launch-spec authorization, dispatch capability/reply truth, identity ambiguity, and durable recovery), then dependent behavior. Preserve additive restore, current extras, old session/config formats through additive defaults, dry-run nonmutation, replacement preflight, and fail-closed recovery. Verification is layered through child epic gqg.36: reusable isolated boundaries first, then issue-owned unit/e2e regressions and feature-preservation controls.
acceptance_criteria: Every candidate is independently triaged at its causal boundary and either retained with a concrete feature-preserving design or closed with falsifying/consolidating evidence and a plausible reopen condition. Every retained implementation child has comprehensive deterministic unit tests, actual-CLI e2e coverage, ordered redacted diagnostic logging, exact state/argv/exit/stdout/stderr assertions, negative and legacy controls, and the smallest applicable verification-fixture blocker. Policy-dependent behavior remains blocked on an explicit decision and routed Canon update. Before closure, the live child rollup must be complete; Beads lint, dependency cycles, duplicate ownership, parent linkage, JSONL/DB synchronization, and verification-contract audits must pass.
