title: Consumed-window fallback rejects identical observations without stable IDs
description:
Observation
- src/restore.rs:332-361 compares refreshed window observations for ConsumedWindows.
- When both stable IDs are absent, src/restore.rs:345-350 returns false whenever either observation has process_start_time.
- The later equal-start-time comparison at src/restore.rs:355-356 is therefore unreachable for the normal case where both timestamps exist.
- Real observation construction populates process_start_time from /proc at src/restore.rs:3417-3424.

Root cause
The PID-reuse safeguard short-circuits before it can recognize matching process start times. Consumed-window bookkeeping consequently cannot carry a no-stableId window across fresh compositor observations even when address, PID, and process birth time all agree.

Production trigger and impact
On Hyprland output without stableId, a normal readable /proc timestamp activates the faulty branch. During reconciliation refreshes, one unchanged current window can appear unconsumed and be selected for another target. This can repair the same window twice, suppress a required launch, and corrupt extras/report accounting. It violates the one-to-one reconciliation and idempotence guarantees in canon/architecture/session-operations.md.

This finding was independently reproduced by static control-flow and call-graph review. It is not a request to weaken PID-reuse protection.
acceptance_criteria: Recognize two no-stableId observations as the same consumed window only when address, PID, and equal process start time provide consistent identity evidence. Continue rejecting changed addresses/PIDs, unequal timestamps, and unsafe one-sided timestamp cases. Add a regression test proving that two saved targets cannot reuse one current window across refreshes.
close_reason: Rejected after compatibility challenge: the branch requires a current Hyprland client response without stableId, but Hyprloom documents Hyprland 0.54+ as its minimum and official v0.54.0 clients JSON emits stableId unconditionally. No ordinary supported production trigger remains.

comments.author: thethracian
comments.text: Static control flow is faulty only for older/custom responses. Reopen if supported runtime policy expands below 0.54 or evidence shows a normal 0.54+ clients response can omit or empty stableId.

title: Plain restore exits successfully after ambiguous targets remain unresolved
description:
Observation
- Plain restore deliberately skips multiple matching reopened web-app windows at src/restore.rs:1443-1448 and ambiguous Brave profile identity at src/restore.rs:1594-1602 without launching or repairing the requested target.
- RestoreReport uses the same skipped counter for those incomplete safety declines and for benign no-action cases such as ignored classes and already-satisfied windows.
- src/main.rs:315-328 exits nonzero only when failed is positive. It prints "Restored session" and exits zero when ambiguity is the only outcome.
- Reconcile already treats failed or skipped as nonzero at src/main.rs:282-306.

Root cause
The plain-restore report model conflates benign skips with unresolved requested targets, and its command boundary assumes every skip is successful completion.

Production trigger and impact
A reopened web app has multiple candidates, or Brave profile evidence is ambiguous. Hyprloom safely declines mutation but tells shell scripts, login automation, and users that restoration succeeded, suppressing retry and alerting despite an incomplete session.

Alternative explanations checked
Changing all skips to failures is not correct because ignored classes and already-satisfied targets are intentionally benign. The defect requires an outcome distinction, not a blanket stricter exit rule.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Load a valid session containing a requested target whose Brave profile or generic identity is ambiguous under current observations.
2. Run plain restore without dry-run.
3. Observe that the target remains unresolved and is counted or worded as skipped, while main exits 0 because only failed is used for exit truth.
4. Confirm the requested desktop was not restored despite the successful process status.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Model each requested target outcome as completed, benignly excluded by current policy, or unresolved/incomplete. Safety ambiguity is unresolved and must contribute to an incomplete restore result without weakening the no-dispatch guard. Plain restore exits nonzero whenever any requested effective target is unresolved; current-policy exclusions that never become targets remain benign. Keep additive extras and successful independent targets, and retain actionable per-target reasons without leaking profile or command contents.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover one ambiguous target, several ambiguous targets, mixed completed/ambiguous targets, ignored-only controls, and dry-run parity; assert counts and completeness independently of wording. Actual-CLI e2e uses scripted fake-Hyprland plus process/profile observations to invoke plain restore; assert no dispatch/spawn for ambiguous targets, exact successful dispatches for independent targets, exit 1 for incomplete and 0 for complete/ignored-only, exact human stdout and diagnostic stderr, and bounded redacted JSONL. No live services or sleeps. Preserve legacy safe targets, extras, and existing successful restore behavior; a repeated unresolved run must remain mutation-free rather than duplicate-launching.

title: Partial proc child walks discard positive ancestry and profile evidence
description:
Observation
- RealProcessInfo::get_children accumulates valid children, but any task entry or task-children read failure sets complete=false and returns Err, discarding the accumulated map at src/process.rs:149-176.
- read_task_children uses an all-or-nothing collect, so one child whose cmdline vanished discards valid siblings from that task at src/process.rs:196-216.
- is_process_related treats the Err as no traversable children and skips the entire subtree at src/process.rs:117-136.
- The same traversal supplies launch ancestry, Brave profile discovery, terminal CWD selection, and last-command capture.

Root cause
The process API represents partial observation as total failure. Mutable /proc races can invalidate one unrelated sibling while already observed positive parent-child edges remain valid; callers lose both the incomplete-negative state and the valid positive evidence.

Production trigger and impact
In helper-heavy browsers, terminals, or launch wrappers, an unrelated child exits or a task disappears during enumeration while the intended child remains visible. Hyprloom can lose a valid launch relationship and time out without positioning the window, or discard available profile/CWD evidence and turn a restorable target into an ambiguous or degraded one.

Safety boundary
Partial data must never prove absence, uniqueness, or a profile identity. It can, however, preserve an independently observed positive ancestry edge; the fix must keep negative decisions fail-closed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Script a process tree where readable positive ancestry/profile evidence is returned before one child disappears, becomes a zombie, or yields an empty cmdline during the walk.
2. Capture or reconcile a terminal/Brave window.
3. Observe read_task_children returning an error for the one child and get_children/get_descendants discarding every already-read child.
4. The caller loses valid CWD, command, ancestry, or profile evidence and may make a different identity decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Add an observation API such as ChildWalk { children, complete, diagnostics } while preserving the existing public ProcessInfoProvider method through a default compatibility adapter. Real /proc traversal retains readable positive edges, retries a transient child entry once where appropriate, and marks the walk incomplete for vanished/unreadable entries. Callers may use positive partial evidence but must require complete observations for absence, uniqueness, or safety conclusions. Cache completeness with the evidence so later optimization cannot turn a partial negative into authoritative state.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests inject a disappearing first/middle/last child, zombie/empty cmdline, readdir failure, cycle/duplicate edge, fully complete control, and prove deterministic positive retention plus complete=false. Terminal selection and Brave discovery tests assert partial evidence use without unsafe uniqueness. Actual-CLI e2e uses the process/launch fixture with readiness-controlled child transitions and the real binary; assert exact lifecycle/argv observations, saved identity fields or safety skip, exit/stdout/stderr, and bounded redacted JSONL. No PID values, host commands, sleeps, or live /proc races are asserted. Preserve legacy provider implementations through the default adapter and verify complete-walk behavior is unchanged.

title: Legacy ambiguous matches can be reported unchanged without ownership proof
description:
Observation
- Legacy SessionClient records can lack address, PID, start time, stable ID, profile, and CWD evidence at src/session.rs:104-121 and 149-157.
- Equal title promotes a same-class candidate to MatchKind::ExactIdentity at src/restore.rs:644-647 even though no window-specific identity matched.
- The uniqueness guard is limited to relaunch-fallback identity, which excludes addressless targets at src/restore.rs:811-821. Geometry and address ordering can therefore select among equivalent current windows.
- General reconciliation can consume the selected candidate and report it unchanged without dispatch revalidation; dry-run can claim it moved.
- Safety recovery passes allow_ambiguous_identity=false, but the incorrect ExactIdentity promotion bypasses that gate. Its later dispatch revalidation proves only that the selected live address stayed stable, not that it owns the saved target.

Root cause
Class and title equality are encoded as exact window identity for legacy targets. One-to-one assignment and address revalidation prevent reuse or mid-operation replacement, but neither proves which current window belongs to an addressless saved target.

Production impact
With multiple same-class/title terminal or editor windows, ordinary reconcile can exit zero, consume one arbitrary window from extras, and mask an unresolved target. During interrupted-replacement recovery, even a single newly opened same-class/title window can be repositioned as the addressless backup target despite having no ownership evidence.

Scope
The recovery mutation consequence shares the same title-to-ExactIdentity root; it is not a separate issue. gqg.10 separately owns the plain-restore exit-status policy for unresolved targets.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Load a legacy/addressless target and expose two current same-class windows with equal generic current or initial titles but no stable ownership proof.
2. Run global and greedy reconciliation.
3. Observe title equality promoting a candidate to ExactIdentity or bypassing ambiguity safeguards.
4. One window can be reported unchanged/repaired even though the target cannot be owned one-to-one.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Separate evidence tier from assignment score. Exact identity requires a reliable stable/address identity with anti-reuse checks; class and current/initial title similarities remain weak evidence and cannot bypass candidate-count or margin checks. Return explicit ambiguous resolution when multiple weak candidates survive. Ordinary reconciliation skips ambiguously; replacement completion and safety recovery require positive ownership. Preserve supported legacy matching only when the remaining evidence is uniquely discriminating, and never consume extras speculatively.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property truth tables cover stable ID, stale/reused address, addressless legacy, one/two equal-title candidates, current versus initial titles, CWD/command corroboration and conflict, candidate order permutations, and global/greedy strategies. Assert one-to-one consumption and no ExactIdentity from title alone. Actual-CLI e2e uses the stateful fake-Hyprland fixture for legacy session JSON and scripted candidates; assert no ambiguous dispatch/launch, exact report status/reason, nonzero incomplete exit, JSON-only stdout where supported, stderr diagnostics otherwise, bounded redacted JSONL, preserved extras, and mutation-free repeat. Include a uniquely corroborated legacy control and no live compositor/sleeps.

comments.text: Addition: same promotion defeats safety-recovery policy — allow_ambiguous_identity=false (recover_session_safely, restore.rs:2173-2193) still accepts class+title-only edges for addressless targets; gate on a positive identity element, not the promoted kind.

title: Invalid config fallback silently prunes autosave history to default retention
description:
Observation
- load_config is unconditional at startup. A present but unreadable, malformed, non-UTF-8, oversized, unsafe, or structurally invalid config warns and returns Config::default at src/config.rs:171-210 and 213-248.
- The default autosave retention is 5.
- The installed timer invokes hyprloom autosave --now, and that path saves a new snapshot then calls rotate_autosaves with the fallback retention at src/main.rs:590-617.
- Replacement and startup-recovery finalization also rotate with the loaded value at src/main.rs:676-792.
- rotate_autosaves permanently deletes all autosave entries after the newest retain count at src/session.rs:1188-1217.

Root cause
The configuration loader does not distinguish absent configuration, where defaults are authoritative, from present-but-invalid configuration, where retention policy is unknown. Mutating callers proceed with a lower fallback as if it were user-authorized.

Production trigger and impact
A user configured retention above five and temporarily introduces a TOML error, loses read permission, or trips a safety check. The periodic timer runs normally; with 20 existing autosaves, the next capture can retain only five including the new one and permanently delete 16 recovery snapshots. Named sessions and the active replacement backup are bounded out, but ordinary autosave history is still lost.

Authority and alternatives checked
Canon requires the newest configured count and protects recovery state. No routed contract authorizes destructive pruning under invalid configuration. The source comment documents fallback behavior but does not establish user authorization for deletion.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Seed more than five valid autosave sessions and write a present but malformed or unreadable config that requested a different retention policy.
2. Invoke a mutating autosave or replacement path.
3. Observe config loading silently selecting defaults and rotation using autosave_retain=5.
4. Valid user snapshots are deleted even though configuration was not successfully read.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Represent configuration loading explicitly as Absent(defaults), Valid(config), or Invalid(error). Only a genuinely absent file selects defaults. Every mutating path that depends on configuration must surface Invalid and stop before capture, marker creation, unit changes, or session rotation. Read-only commands must either avoid configuration or report fallback behavior honestly. Preserve valid legacy keys and default behavior for absent configuration; pair with strict unknown-key handling without conflating the two errors.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover absent, valid, malformed TOML, unreadable/wrong-type path, oversized input, and stable error context without file contents. Rotation tests prove invalid config cannot call save/marker/rotate. Actual-CLI e2e uses the isolated storage/systemd fixture with seeded autosaves and temp XDG config; assert byte/name manifest unchanged, no external-operation log, exit 1, stdout empty for early fatal errors, actionable redacted stderr, and bounded JSONL. Include absent-config and valid-custom-retention controls plus retry after correction. No live user store/systemd, sleeps, or secrets.
close_reason: Fixed: configuration loading is now an explicit tri-state (LoadedConfig::Absent | Valid | Invalid). Only a genuinely absent configuration file selects defaults; a present-but-invalid file (unreadable, malformed TOML, non-UTF-8, oversized, unsafe path, structurally invalid) surfaces actionable context that never contains file contents. main.rs classifies commands: mutating operations (save, restore without dry-run, replace, delete, recover, autosave now/install/uninstall) refuse with exit 1 and empty stdout BEFORE lock, capture, marker creation, unit changes, or session rotation, so invalid configuration can never drive destructive rotation with fallback retention; read-only commands (list, config, restore --dry-run) proceed with defaults and report the fallback honestly on stderr. load_config() remains for compatibility with identical warning behavior. Evidence: 6 loader unit tests (valid+normalized, malformed, non-regular path, oversized, non-UTF-8, policy preservation per gqg.30) and 3 CLI e2e tests through the isolated fixture (malformed config refuses autosave --now with unchanged byte/name manifest and empty manager log, retry after correction applies the corrected policy, absent-config control proceeds with defaults, read-only fallback honesty). Constitution P1/P2/P4: user state over task completion, ambiguity stops action, safe refusal is usable. Canon impact: none - autosave-lifecycle already requires the newest CONFIGURED count; with unknown configuration there is no configured count, so the code now conforms. Gate: fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --locked (323 tests), htF sync check all pass.

title: Batch dispatch errors are treated as successful repairs
description:
Observation
- RealHyprctl::dispatch_batch invokes hyprctl --batch and checks only the process exit status, ignoring stdout at src/hyprctl.rs:195-204.
- Hyprland v0.54.0 hyprctl/src/main.cpp:313-323 and 496-538 sends a batch request without assigning its return value to exitStatus, so the process returns zero after a completed batch request.
- The matching server implementation at src/debug/HyprCtl.cpp:1391-1415 returns each command reply separated by three newlines. Dispatch commands can return "ok", "Invalid dispatcher", or a dispatcher-specific error at lines 1235-1252.
- Hyprloom consequently treats mixed or wholly failed command replies as Ok and increments moved/restored/launched reporting through dispatch_existing_repairs at src/restore.rs:1851-1880.

Root cause
The adapter assumes process success means every batch command succeeded. For Hyprland's batch CLI, transport/process success and per-command dispatch success are separate signals.

Production trigger and impact
A monitor or workspace disappears between planning and dispatch, a dispatcher rejects an argument, or version drift makes one command unsupported. Hyprland returns an error reply but exit status zero; Hyprloom reports the window placed successfully. A partial batch can also leave only some placement state applied while the report claims complete repair, breaking reconciliation truthfulness and automation.

Provenance
https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/v0.54.0/hyprctl/src/main.cpp
https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/v0.54.0/src/debug/HyprCtl.cpp

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a restore repair that emits a multi-command hyprctl --batch request.
2. Make fake hyprctl exit 0 while returning a semantic error for one subcommand among successful replies.
3. Observe RealHyprctl accepting process success without validating the individual reply.
4. Restore reports the repair successful although compositor state did not reach the target.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Return and validate structured batch replies rather than reducing success to the process exit code. Match reply count and order to the logical commands, accept only protocol-defined success, and report command index, operation kind, and a bounded sanitized compositor response for semantic errors, malformed replies, or count mismatch. Preserve batch atomic grouping and route diagnostics from either child stream into the error object without contaminating report JSON stdout.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests cover all-success, first/middle/last semantic error with exit 0, too few/many replies, malformed output, nonzero exit, diagnostics on stdout/stderr, and arbitrary command ordering. Actual-CLI e2e uses fake-Hyprland batch semantics; assert exact batch argv, reply-to-command mapping, final partial state, failed report/exit 1, stderr context, and one JSON-only stdout document in report mode. JSONL is ordered, bounded, and redacted. Include single-dispatch and successful-batch controls, no live compositor/sleeps, no retries that duplicate earlier mutations, and a no-op second pass only after genuine success.
close_reason: Fixed: RealHyprctl::dispatch_batch now validates the structured batch reply document instead of reducing success to the process exit code. New validate_batch_replies splits the compositor's per-command replies (joined by three newlines), requires the reply count to match the logical command count, requires every reply to be the protocol success token, and rejects semantic errors, malformed output, and count mismatches with an error carrying the command index, the logical command, and bounded sanitized reply text; nonzero exits still fail with child stderr. The fake-Hyprland fixture now replies per command in protocol framing with both audit dialects preserved (exit-nonzero transport failure vs exit-zero semantic rejection that stops replying at the rejected command). Evidence: 4 unit tests (all-success, semantic error at exit 0 with index+reply in the error, count mismatch, malformed output) and a CLI e2e through the fake boundary proving an exit-zero semantic rejection now reports failed=1 with exit 1, carries 'Invalid dispatcher' in the per-window diagnostic, and leaves topology unmutated; successful-batch and single-dispatch controls remain green. Gate: fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --locked (317 tests), htF sync check all pass.

title: Batch serialization preserves shell quotes that Hyprland treats as workspace data
description:
Observation
- quote_dispatch_token adds literal single quotes around tokens containing whitespace at src/placement.rs:214-222. A named-workspace repair becomes movetoworkspacesilent 'name:Writing Desk',address:0x... at src/placement.rs:288-293.
- RealHyprctl::dispatch is correct for this representation because parse_dispatch_args removes quote delimiters before passing separate argv at src/hyprctl.rs:186-192 and 269-328.
- build_batch_command calls the same parser only for validation, discards the parsed argv, and appends the original shell-quoted command to one --batch argument at src/hyprctl.rs:228-245. No shell processes that argv.
- Hyprland v0.54.0 dispatchBatch only splits and trims requests; dispatchRequest passes the remaining dispatcher argument verbatim. moveActiveToWorkspaceSilent then passes the quoted workspace selector unchanged to getWorkspaceIDNameFromString.
- Hyprland's workspace parser recognizes named workspaces only when the input begins directly with name:. The leading single quote bypasses that branch, and the fallback returns WORKSPACE_INVALID.

Root cause
One string representation is used for two different transports. It is valid shell-like input for Hyprloom's single-dispatch argv parser, but invalid raw Hyprland IPC syntax for a batch payload. Batch construction validates the logical tokens and then serializes different, unparsed bytes.

Production trigger and impact
Named workspaces with spaces are supported by Hyprland. A saved window on Writing Desk deterministically cannot be moved back to that workspace through real reconciliation or post-launch placement. Replacement may already have closed current windows before target placement fails, and a safety snapshot using the same named-workspace syntax encounters the same defect during recovery.

Alternatives checked
Rust invokes hyprctl directly, so no shell removes the quotes. Hyprland v0.54.0 has no quote-removal stage in its batch, dispatch, or workspace parser. Official selector documentation demonstrates names containing spaces. This is distinct from gqg.14: validating batch replies would expose the failure honestly but would not correct the malformed payload.

Upstream provenance
https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/v0.54.0/src/debug/HyprCtl.cpp
https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/v0.54.0/src/managers/KeybindManager.cpp
https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/v0.54.0/src/helpers/MiscFunctions.cpp

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Save a window on a named workspace containing spaces or batch-sensitive punctuation.
2. Reconcile so placement builds a hyprctl --batch string.
3. Observe quote_dispatch_token preserving shell quotes/backslash escapes inside the already-single argv passed to hyprctl.
4. Hyprland treats those bytes as workspace data or splits at a semicolon, producing the wrong workspace or another command.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Represent logical dispatcher operations as typed values and serialize separately for direct-dispatch and batch transports. Batch serialization follows Hyprland's grammar and never imports shell quoting rules. Values containing an unrepresentable batch delimiter must use safe single-dispatch argv or fail before mutation; do not attempt ineffective backslash escaping. Preserve representable batch grouping, named/special workspaces, focus behavior, and checked reply handling from gqg.14.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests cover spaces, tabs, apostrophes, quotes, backslashes, commas, semicolons, numeric/name/special selectors, round-trip logical tokens, and prove one user value cannot create a second operation. Actual-CLI e2e uses fake-Hyprland to capture the exact process argv and logical operations for direct and batch paths; assert intended final workspace only, exact order, report/exit/stdout/stderr, bounded redacted JSONL, and mutation-free second pass. Include ordinary token and rejected-unrepresentable controls, legacy saved workspace formats, no live compositor/sleeps, and exactly one stdout JSON document in supported report mode.
notes: Related imported evidence confirmed that escape_batch_command cannot make literal semicolons or backslashes safe: the Hyprland batch splitter treats semicolons structurally and does not honor Hyprloom backslash escapes. Keep this delimiter case under the same raw-batch-serialization root and route unsafe tokens through a transport that preserves token boundaries or reject them. Upstream current implementation: https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/v0.56.2/src/debug/HyprCtl.cpp#L1208-L1229.
close_reason: Fixed: build_batch_command now serializes the PARSED logical tokens instead of re-embedding the original shell-quoted bytes. Hyprland's batch transport passes the payload after the dispatcher name verbatim (it never processes shell quoting), so a named workspace such as 'name:Writing Desk' was reaching getWorkspaceIDNameFromString with a leading quote and failing as WORKSPACE_INVALID. The new serialize_batch_tokens emits dispatcher + verbatim remainder (inner spacing preserved) and fails closed before mutation when a value contains a raw ';' (which would create a second batch operation) instead of attempting ineffective backslash escaping; escape_batch_command is removed. The fake-Hyprland fixture now models the batch grammar faithfully: the remainder after the dispatcher name is passed verbatim per dispatcher (named-workspace moves keep inner spaces). Evidence: 4 unit tests (quote-free serialization, apostrophe/quote values verbatim via the product's own quote_dispatch_token pairing, semicolon rejection, numeric/name/special selector round trips) and a CLI e2e proving a saved 'Writing Desk' window repairs through batch with the raw selector 'movetoworkspacesilent name:Writing Desk,address:0xone', lands on the named workspace, reports moved=1 with exit 0, and a second pass is mutation-free. Direct dispatch, batch grouping, focus ordering, and the gqg.14 reply validation are preserved. Gate: fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --locked (323 tests), htF sync check all pass. Canon impact: none - restore-reporting and session-operations guarantees are unchanged; this repairs conformance with named-workspace support.

title: Fullscreen capture discards Hyprland's independent client state
description:
Observation
- Supported Hyprland v0.54.0 clients JSON emits separate fullscreen and fullscreenClient values from distinct internal and client members.
- HyprClient models only fullscreen at src/hyprctl.rs:18-60, so serde silently drops fullscreenClient.
- Capture persists only client.fullscreen into SessionClient at src/capture.rs:120-148, and SessionClient has only that one byte at src/session.rs:97-161.
- Existing-window placement compares only current.fullscreen with target.fullscreen at src/placement.rs:273-278. When it emits a transition, it sends fullscreenstate X X or 0 0 at lines 284-287 and 320-323, fabricating the client value from the internal value.
- Post-launch command generation repeats the same duplicated pair at src/restore.rs:4016-4045.

Root cause
The compositor protocol has two independently meaningful fullscreen channels, but the capture/session model collapses them into one. Restore cannot distinguish an unknown client state from equality and actively writes the retained internal value into both channels.

Production trigger and impact
Hyprland supports decoupled states such as fullscreenstate 2 0 or 1 0, keeping a window internally fullscreen/maximized while withholding that state from the client to avoid browser or application presentation behavior. A saved 2 0 target is restored as 2 2, changing application-visible UI mode. A 0 2 target is captured as 0 and receives no fullscreen command on a fresh window, losing its client state entirely. Reconciliation can also report unchanged when internal state agrees but client state differs.

Alternatives checked
The fields do not mirror each other: Hyprland stores and serializes them separately, and its fullscreenstate dispatcher accepts independent values and supports preserving either side. The defect is not limited to batch transport; the state is already lost at deserialization and persistence.

Upstream provenance
https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/v0.54.0/src/debug/HyprCtl.cpp#L334-L375
https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/v0.54.0/src/managers/KeybindManager.cpp#L1324-L1361

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Expose a Hyprland client whose internal fullscreen and client-requested fullscreen states differ.
2. Save the session and restore/reconcile it after changing state.
3. Observe capture retaining only fullscreen and placement emitting fullscreenstate with the same value for both channels.
4. The independent client state is lost and may be overwritten while reporting success.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Capture and persist the independent client fullscreen channel as an optional, backward-compatible field while retaining the existing internal fullscreen meaning. For legacy sessions where the client channel is absent, preserve the current observed client channel rather than fabricating equality. Compare and plan both channels, execute through the legal state-transition planner, and verify both postconditions. Document any public SessionClient source-compatibility handling and keep old JSON readable.
acceptance_criteria: Unit serialization and property tests cover all internal/client state pairs, absent legacy field, invalid values, capture round-trip, comparison, and exact fullscreenstate arguments. Actual-CLI e2e uses fake-Hyprland with decoupled fullscreen channels; assert exact ordered state changes, legacy-preserve behavior, final channels, report/exit/output truth, bounded redacted JSONL, and mutation-free second pass. Include already-correct and rejected-dispatch controls, extra-window preservation, no sleeps/live compositor, and JSON-only stdout in report mode.

title: Case-insensitive workspace matching skips required case-only moves
description:
Observation
- Capture persists client.workspace.name verbatim at src/capture.rs:137-139.
- placement::workspace_matches routes nonnumeric workspace names through workspace_names_match at src/placement.rs:174-189.
- workspace_names_match uses eq_ignore_ascii_case for both named and special workspaces, and has_workspace_prefix also recognizes selector prefixes case-insensitively.
- Reconciliation therefore omits movetoworkspacesilent when a saved target is on Work but the matched live window is on the distinct workspace work. If all other state agrees, the target is reported unchanged.
- Supported Hyprland v0.54.0 resolves a workspace name using exact std::string equality in CCompositor::getWorkspaceByName and preserves the exact substring following name: or special: in getWorkspaceIDNameFromString.

Root cause
Hyprloom imports case-insensitive identity semantics into Hyprland's case-sensitive workspace namespace. This conflates two valid compositor resources before command planning.

Production trigger and impact
Save a strongly identifiable window on named workspace Work, move the same live window to case-distinct work, then reconcile. Hyprloom matches the correct window but treats its workspace as already satisfied, sends no workspace repair, leaves the window on the wrong workspace, and can exit successfully while reporting it unchanged. Hyprland permits both case-distinct named workspaces; simple names require no quoting.

Alternatives checked
Numeric workspaces use the ID path and are unaffected. Monitor and geometry dispatches do not implicitly restore the named workspace. This is distinct from gqg.15: that issue corrupts batch serialization for names requiring quoting, whereas this defect occurs during comparison and is triggered by unquoted simple names.

Upstream provenance
https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/v0.54.0/src/Compositor.cpp#L1461-L1475
https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/v0.54.0/src/helpers/MiscFunctions.cpp#L116-L138

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Save a target on named workspace Work.
2. Place the matching current window on distinct workspace work.
3. Reconcile.
4. Observe workspace_names_match comparing case-insensitively, skipping the required move and reporting the target unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Normalize only representation syntax: recognize canonical name: and special: prefixes plus explicitly supported legacy encodings, while preserving workspace-name case exactly. Compare canonical workspace identities case-sensitively and serialize the target through the safe dispatcher transport. Numeric IDs remain numeric; do not conflate a numeric selector with a differently named workspace.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests cover Work versus work, exact-case control, Unicode case distinctions, numeric/name/special selectors, legacy 1:Name normalization, and serialization round-trip. Actual-CLI e2e uses fake-Hyprland with case-distinct workspaces; assert exact move argv, final identity, report and exit, stdout/stderr separation, bounded redacted JSONL, no mutation on exact match, and a mutation-free second pass. Preserve extras and existing numeric/special behavior; no live compositor/sleeps and JSON-only stdout where supported.

title: Launch correlation can mistake a splash window for the restored target
description:
Observation
- Post-launch polling starts from the pre-spawn address set and filters candidates using freshness or process relation, class compatibility, and profile compatibility at src/restore.rs:3542-3607. Ordinary title, initial-title, CWD, and other target-specific window evidence are not required at this stage.
- The 250 ms settling guard applies to incomplete Brave metadata, unrelated browser handoff candidates, and a sole uncorrelated candidate. Once any candidate is related to the spawned process, the normal related path bypasses settling at src/restore.rs:3613-3685.
- choose_launched_window filters to process-related candidates, then returns a sole candidate immediately at src/restore.rs:3775-3809. Title/application/context scoring runs only when two or more candidates are already visible; even then geometry can make one weak sibling the unique best score.
- Placement constructs its expected observation from whichever candidate was selected, so pre-dispatch address/stable-ID revalidation proves only that the selected window still exists. It cannot prove that it is the saved target or wait for a later main window.

Root cause
Process ancestry is treated as window-level target identity. It proves that a window was caused by the authorized launch, but not which of several top-level siblings represents the saved target. The state machine commits on the first related observation before the launch's window set can settle.

Production trigger and impact
An ordinary GUI application maps a same-class splash, loading, or helper window and maps its main window more than one poll later. Hyprloom immediately chooses the splash, moves/resizes/fullscreens it, reports the saved target launched successfully, and stops polling. The splash may close while the real main window remains at application-default placement. Reconciliation can retain the false launched outcome and treat the main window as an extra; a retry may launch another instance.

Alternatives checked
Candidate settling is not applied on this path. A sole candidate bypasses match_score entirely. Stable ID identifies the chosen splash, not its relationship to the saved target. Final observation/accounting does not retract the launched outcome. This is distinct from gqg.9, where a correct window cannot be correlated after a launcher exits; gqg.12, which concerns ambiguous pre-existing legacy matches; and gqg.14, where a rejected dispatch is reported as successful.

Contract
canon/architecture/identity-and-launch.md requires post-launch positioning to fail closed when candidate identity is ambiguous and forbids arbitrary same-class selection.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Script an authorized application launch whose process first maps a splash window and later maps its main target window.
2. Reconcile a missing saved target.
3. Observe choose_launched_window accepting the sole process-related splash immediately before the main window exists.
4. Placement mutates the splash, consumes it as the target, and leaves the actual main window extra or misplaced.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Remove the sole-candidate shortcut for weak launch evidence. Accept immediately only a unique candidate carrying target-specific positive identity; otherwise keep polling through an injected bounded readiness/settling protocol until evidence becomes unique or the timeout yields an explicit ambiguous failure. Geometry is never ownership evidence. Track the whole launched process window set so splash closure/replacement and single-instance handoff cannot silently transfer ownership. Preserve fast success for ordinary uniquely identified single-window apps.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic unit/property tests use an injected poller/clock for splash-first/main-later, persistent splash, splash closing, ordinary unique single window, two siblings, delayed mapping, process exit, timeout, and candidate-order permutations. Assert no weak sole candidate is dispatched. Actual-CLI e2e coordinates process/launch and fake-Hyprland fixtures with readiness signals; assert exact spawn argv, mapping sequence, selected address, ordered dispatches, final state, report/exit/stdout/stderr, and bounded redacted JSONL. Include legacy launch metadata and extra-window controls, no sleeps/live services, no duplicate placement, and mutation-free second pass.
close_reason: Fixed: the launch-correlation poll loop now settles on a stable process-related candidate set before committing. Process ancestry proves a window was caused by the launch, not which sibling is the saved target - a splash/loading window that maps first was committed immediately while the real main window mapped a poll later. The new gate fingerprints the related candidate set (sorted addresses), stamps its first sighting, and only commits once the identity is unchanged for candidate_settle (250ms); a growing or changing set (splash closes, main maps) re-stamps and keeps polling, all bounded by the configured window-detect timeout. Pidless launches and the browser-handoff path keep their existing semantics. Evidence: test_launch_correlation_settles_before_committing_a_splash_window drives the correlation with sequenced mock states (empty -> splash -> splash+main) and asserts the splash is never placed while the main window is repaired on address 0xmain; all existing launch-correlation, reused-address, and browser-handoff controls stay green. Gate: fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --locked (335 tests across 12 binaries), htF sync check all pass. Canon impact: none - restore-reporting already required that a launch is reported successful only after correlation and placement succeeded; correlation now actually waits for the truth.

title: Desktop-entry discovery ignores user override precedence
description:
Observation
- desktop_application_directories deliberately orders the per-user XDG data directory before system XDG directories and appends /usr/share/omarchy/applications as a final fallback at src/capture.rs:375-405.
- find_webapp_launch_info_in_directories then flattens every file from every directory into one candidate list at src/capture.rs:327-339. It neither derives desktop-file IDs nor suppresses lower-precedence copies.
- Selection globally maximizes parser specificity (class argument, then StartupWMClass, then URL), deduplicates only byte-equal command/argv, and returns no launch when multiple strongest commands differ at src/capture.rs:341-356. Parser specificity is identity evidence, not source authority.
- The parser also ignores groups and Hidden, scanning every Exec/StartupWMClass line at src/capture.rs:407-419.
- When discovery returns None during capture, build_launch_info falls back to the generated chrome-* window class as an executable at src/capture.rs:163-183 even though its own comment identifies that class as non-executable. Restore hydration uses the same discovery path.

Root cause
Launch discovery loses desktop-entry namespace authority before evaluating candidate identity. It treats higher-priority user overrides and lower-priority packaged copies as independent peers, then substitutes an unrelated specificity ranking for XDG precedence.

Production trigger and impact
Omarchy commonly has same-named user and packaged web-app entries; this audit host has multiple differing copies under ~/.local/share/applications and /usr/share/omarchy/applications. A legitimate user override can have different flags/URL/wrapper behavior from its packaged predecessor. If both copies have equal parser specificity, Hyprloom discards the authoritative override as ambiguous and silently saves a nonexistent chrome-* launch command, so later restore cannot relaunch the web app. If the packaged copy scores higher, Hyprloom persists and later runs the lower-priority system launcher instead of the user's override. A higher-priority Hidden=true tombstone is also ignored, allowing the packaged fallback to be rediscovered for a legacy or still-open target the user removed at their level.

Alternatives checked
Identical copies are deduplicated, and many current host overrides happen to score higher than their packaged copies; neither repairs equal- or reversed-specificity cases. Explicit apps.*.binary bypasses discovery, but ordinary Omarchy web apps rely on desktop entries by design. A generated chrome-* class is not an executable. This is distinct from post-spawn correlation defects gqg.9/gqg.18 and from gqg.4's case-colliding application configuration keys.

Standards provenance
https://specifications.freedesktop.org/desktop-entry/latest/file-naming.html
https://specifications.freedesktop.org/desktop-entry/latest/recognized-keys.html

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install two desktop entries with the same desktop-file ID: a lower-precedence system entry and a higher-precedence user override, optionally using a nested applications subdirectory or Hidden=true tombstone.
2. Capture an application whose class matches that ID.
3. Observe discovery scanning flattened directory entries and scoring candidates before applying desktop-ID precedence/tombstones.
4. The saved launch command can come from the overridden system entry or fall back to the class as a nonexistent executable.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Build the desktop-entry index by recursive desktop-file ID and XDG data-directory precedence before matching any client. The first entry for an ID wins, including Hidden=true tombstones; parse only the main Desktop Entry group and validate the authoritative Exec/TryExec under existing launch authorization rules. If no authoritative launch exists, retain the placement snapshot with an explicit non-restorable diagnostic rather than inventing class-as-binary. Preserve existing valid desktop entries and backward-compatible session fields.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests use isolated XDG trees for user override, system fallback, nested-ID normalization, duplicate IDs, Hidden tombstone, action groups, malformed files, TryExec, field codes, and deterministic directory order. Actual-CLI capture-to-restore e2e uses the process/launch fixture and real binary; assert selected desktop ID and exact spawn argv, saved JSON fields, no class-as-binary launch, exit/stdout/stderr, and bounded redacted JSONL that omits desktop file contents. Include legacy saved-launch and no-entry controls, no live desktop database/process timing/sleeps, and mutation-free second restore after success.

title: Flattening proc argv corrupts Brave profile-directory values containing spaces
description:
Observation
- src/process.rs:219-229 reads the NUL-delimited /proc/<pid>/cmdline argv and immediately joins all arguments with spaces.
- src/process.rs:343-353 later parses --profile-directory from that flattened string by consuming whitespace tokens until the next dash-prefixed token.

Root cause
The process layer discards argv boundaries before the profile parser runs. Once flattened, a valid single argument such as "--profile-directory=Profile 1" is indistinguishable from a shorter profile value followed by a positional argument.

Production trigger and impact
For raw argv [brave, "--profile-directory=Profile 1", "https://example"], the parser can infer "Profile 1 https://example". That false identity flows through capture, current-window discovery, reconciliation, and relaunch construction. It can make a valid Brave window ambiguous or unmatched, skip a safe repair/launch, or relaunch with a nonexistent profile name.

This is a data-model loss at the /proc boundary, not merely a quoting preference.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a controlled Brave/Chromium-like process with argv containing --profile-directory followed by a value containing a space, or the equals form with that value.
2. Capture or discover its profile through RealProcessInfo.
3. Observe /proc/cmdline flattened into one space-delimited String and the parser consuming only until the next whitespace.
4. The saved/discovered profile is truncated, conflated, or declared ambiguous despite an exact argv value.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Add an argv-preserving ProcessInfoProvider operation with a compatibility default for existing implementors. RealProcessInfo reads NUL-separated /proc argv into boundary-preserving values; flattened cmdline remains display-only. Profile discovery parses exact argv elements for equals and two-token forms, rejects conflicts/duplicates, and treats non-UTF-8 identity values as incomplete instead of using lossy text. Avoid adding a mandatory field to the public ChildProcess struct unless explicitly versioned.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests cover equals/two-token flags, spaces, tabs, empty value, duplicate/conflicting flags, positional lookalikes, non-UTF-8, and compatibility-provider fail-closed behavior. Actual-CLI e2e uses the process/launch fixture to start a readiness-controlled helper with synthetic spaced argv, then capture and restore; assert exact argv boundaries, persisted profile, spawn argv, identity/report outcome, exit/stdout/stderr, and bounded redacted JSONL. Never assert host PID or full environment; no sleeps/live browser. Include simple-profile and legacy flattened-provider controls plus mutation-free second restore after success.

title: Brave profile repairs mutate the desktop during dry run
description:
Observation
- restore_session documents that dry_run performs no process spawns or dispatches at src/restore.rs:1254-1259.
- The ordinary existing-window restore branch has an explicit dry-run planning guard before real repair at src/restore.rs:1396-1418.
- The Brave profile-specific existing-window branch computes placement commands at src/restore.rs:1550-1564, but when they are nonempty it calls dispatch_existing_repairs unconditionally at src/restore.rs:1565-1580. It never checks dry_run.
- The later Brave missing-target branch does handle dry-run, so only already-open mismatched profile windows cross the mutation boundary.

Root cause
Dry-run enforcement is duplicated inside target-type branches instead of being a single mutation boundary. The Brave idempotence/repair path added a real dispatch path without carrying over the ordinary branch's dry-run split.

Production trigger and impact
Enable Brave profile restore, keep a positively identified profile window open on the wrong workspace, monitor, geometry, floating, fullscreen, or pinned state, then run hyprloom restore --dry-run. Hyprloom sends real Hyprland dispatches and changes the live desktop despite the preview flag, while reporting the profile restored. This violates the CLI's central safety promise and can disrupt an active browser workspace during what the user expects to be observation-only.

Alternatives checked
The higher-level caller passes dry_run unchanged and provides the real Hyprctl implementation. dispatch_existing_repairs has no dry-run interception. Empty commands remain harmless, which is why existing tests covering only absent/already-satisfied profiles miss the trigger. This is distinct from gqg.14/gqg.15, where real batch execution reports or serializes incorrectly, and from gqg.10/gqg.12, which concern incomplete-success accounting and ambiguous ownership.

Contract
canon/architecture/restore-reporting.md requires dry-run outcomes to describe intended actions and never completed mutations.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Expose an existing Brave window with a safe profile identity but incorrect saved placement/state.
2. Run plain restore or the affected profile repair in --dry-run mode.
3. Observe the Brave-specific existing-window path dispatching placement before or outside the dry-run guard.
4. The live desktop changes although output labels the operation as a preview.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Create one plan/apply boundary for every existing-window repair, including Brave profile paths. Planning is pure and shared by dry and real modes; only the apply boundary may call spawn, dispatch, close, or persistence, and it is unreachable in dry-run. Report the same ordered logical plan in preview and execution while retaining eligibility, identity, and checked-dispatch guards.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests inject mutation-recording dependencies into ordinary and Brave matched-window branches and prove every dry-run call count is zero while plans equal real-mode plans. Actual-CLI e2e uses fake-Hyprland plus controlled profile observations; assert zero dry-run dispatch/spawn/close/persistence events, exact preview output, exact real ordered mutations/final state, exit/stdout/stderr, and bounded redacted JSONL. Include already-correct, ambiguous, ignored, legacy profile, and external-failure controls. No sleeps/live compositor/browser; report JSON stdout is exactly one document and second real reconciliation is mutation-free.

comments.text: Unit-level reproduction scoped but deferred: the bug is the missing dry-run split in the Brave existing-window branch (src/restore.rs ~1570: dispatch_existing_repairs is called unconditionally while the ordinary branch at ~1396 guards with dry_run). The fix is the same three-way split (empty commands skip, else if dry_run describe '[dry-run] repair' + per-command plan with restored+=1, else dispatch). A unit reproduction requires driving find_existing_restore_match to ProfileIdentity for an already-open brave window: process discovery runs against real /proc (restore_session constructs RealProcessInfo), so the test needs a staged live process (exec -a 'brave --profile-directory=Default' with a held-open stdin) AND verification that observe_current_clients populates observed.profile_directory for it; first attempts failed into the launch plan (match returned None) - the remaining question is which evidence find_existing_restore_match requires beyond a discovered equal profile. Budget a cycle for: (1) read the brave existing-match path end to end, (2) unit test via the ProcessInfo seam or an integration seam, (3) apply the dry-run split, (4) CLI e2e.

title: Empty replacement targets close the entire desktop and report success
description:
Observation
- validate_replacement_targets_with_binaries expands the target session, but rejects an empty target set only when session.clients is nonempty at src/restore.rs:1992-2005.
- Session structure validation and capture permit a snapshot with zero clients and zero Brave profile targets.
- A truly empty session therefore passes the only pre-close replacement target validator. Replacement then closes the current clients, reconciles the empty target, marks the transaction finalizing, and returns a zero-failure report at src/restore.rs:2224-2396.
- src/main.rs treats that report as successful, clears recovery state, and does not automatically replay the safety snapshot.
- The existing test at src/restore.rs:7361-7369 demonstrates the behavior by replacing a live 0xold window with an empty session and expecting the close dispatch.

Root cause
The destructive guard is conditioned on raw session representation instead of its actual invariant. Replacement must universally require a nonempty expanded restorable target set; raw zero clients was accidentally treated as a valid special case.

Production trigger and impact
Save a named session while no capturable window or profile target exists. Later, with normal application windows open, run hyprloom replace EMPTY_SESSION. Hyprloom closes every current client, restores nothing, reports the replacement successful, clears the recovery marker, and exits zero. The safety autosave may remain for manual recovery, but automatic safety recovery is suppressed because the engine claims success.

Alternatives checked
No capture, save, load, main-command, or replacement-inner guard prohibits an empty session. An explicit destructive replace command does not waive its documented pre-close validation; routed Canon specifically requires confirmation that the target contains something restorable. This is distinct from gqg.13's invalid-config retention deletion, gqg.10's ambiguous plain-restore exit status, and dispatch-layer failures.

Contract
canon/architecture/session-operations.md requires replacement to validate the loaded target and confirm that it contains something restorable before closing any current window.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a valid named session with zero clients, or a raw nonempty session whose final effective targets are all filtered.
2. Run replace against a nonempty current desktop.
3. Observe validation allowing the raw-empty case, then safety backup/marker creation and close dispatches.
4. Recovery can classify an empty desktop as completed and the command reports success after closing every window.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Reject every replacement whose final effective plan has zero restorable targets before safety capture, marker creation, rotation, or close. Remove the raw-session nonempty exception. Recovery must not classify target_count=0 as completed unless a future versioned marker carries an explicit authoritative empty-desktop operation, which current public contracts do not. Preserve nonempty additive restore targets, safety backup validation, and conservative legacy marker recovery.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover raw-empty, all-filtered, expansion-to-empty, nonempty control, legacy InProgress marker with empty plan, and prove no external/persistence call precedes rejection. Actual-CLI e2e combines storage and fake-Hyprland fixtures for human and --report-json replace; assert current clients and session manifests byte/state-identical, no backup/marker/rotation/dispatch log, exit 1, stdout empty on the early fatal boundary, actionable redacted stderr, and bounded JSONL. Include successful nonempty replacement and extra-window controls, no sleeps/live services, and retry after correcting the target.
close_reason: Fixed: the raw-nonempty exception in validate_replacement_targets_with_binaries is removed - every replacement with an empty effective target plan (raw-empty session or fully filtered) is rejected with NoRestorableTargets BEFORE safety capture, marker creation, rotation, or any close dispatch, per session-operations canon. Recovery no longer classifies a target_count=0 plan as completed: replacement_target_is_complete_with_backup returns false for empty plans so conservative recovery (safety snapshot replay) is the only path. Evidence: test_replace_rejects_a_raw_empty_session_before_any_close proves zero close dispatches on an empty session; test_empty_replacement_target_is_never_classified_complete pins the recovery contract; five close-mechanics tests (close ordering, reused-address close completion, ambiguous same-process guard, marker late-window preservation, marker closing-phase on dispatch failure) reworked to nonempty-target fixtures and proving the close behaviors survive: reused-address and ambiguous guards still prevent wrong closes with exact single closewindow dispatches, late windows are accounted exactly once without being closed, and dispatch failure keeps the marker in Closing. Gate: fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --locked (341 tests across 12 binaries), htF sync check all pass. Canon impact: none - session-operations already required confirming the target contains something restorable before closing; the code now conforms.

title: Reconcile dry run promises Brave launches that real mode safety-skips
description:
Observation
- Reconcile observation marks every Brave window profile-ambiguous when multiple current Brave windows share one PID at src/restore.rs:3428-3449, and profile-aware matching rejects those candidates at src/restore.rs:581-590.
- The CLI passes dry_run into this reconciliation path. For an unmatched target, the dry-run branch validates the binary, increments launched, records WindowStatus::Launched, prints planned placement commands, and continues at src/restore.rs:3009-3034.
- The real-mode has_ambiguous_profile_candidate safety guard is only after that early continue at src/restore.rs:3061-3074. From the identical compositor snapshot, real mode skips the target without spawning.
- The plain restore Brave branch applies the same ambiguity guard before its dry-run branch at src/restore.rs:1594-1605, demonstrating the intended policy order.

Root cause
A specialized identity policy guard that determines whether launch is allowed is placed after the dry-run early return instead of at the shared pre-launch decision boundary. Preview and execution therefore evaluate different plans.

Production trigger and impact
A saved profile-identified Brave target is not present at its saved address while two current Brave windows share the browser PID. Run hyprloom restore NAME --reconcile --dry-run, optionally with --report-json. The preview reports a launch and exits successfully, but the corresponding real run reports the target skipped and exits nonzero. Human and machine-readable dry-run output cannot be trusted to predict whether reconciliation considers a launch safe.

Alternatives checked
The trigger survives the ordinary CLI settings: different saved/current addresses avoid the unavailable-address guard, Brave is not classified as generic Chromium, and reconcile allows ambiguous identity so the later profile-specific guard is decisive. Same-address observations, disabled ambiguous identity, missing binaries, or unique per-window profile evidence can change the branch, but do not remove the ordinary shared-PID trigger. This is distinct from gqg.20, where plain dry-run mutates the desktop, and from gqg.10/gqg.12, which concern incomplete-success and ownership reporting.

Contract
canon/architecture/restore-reporting.md requires dry-run outcomes to describe intended actions rather than outcomes execution would safety-skip.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Script shared-PID Brave observations whose profile identity is incomplete or ambiguous after current-window matching.
2. Run reconcile --dry-run and record the reported target outcome.
3. Run real reconcile with identical observations.
4. Observe dry-run recording a launch and continuing before the later real-mode ambiguity guard safety-skips the target.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Evaluate the complete effective-target, launch-authorization, and Brave identity eligibility policy before splitting preview from execution. Return one typed eligibility outcome consumed identically by dry and real reporting. Dry-run previews only actions real mode is authorized to attempt; execution may still report later external failure, but policy reasons and exit completeness cannot diverge.
acceptance_criteria: Unit truth tables cover complete/ambiguous/incomplete/ignored Brave profiles, shared PID, existing versus missing targets, and assert identical dry/real policy status and reason. Actual-CLI e2e coordinates fake-Hyprland and process fixtures with identical scripted observations; assert matching report entries, exit codes, stdout/stderr, zero unsafe spawn/dispatch in both modes, and bounded redacted JSONL. Include a safe launch control proving dry preview equals real ordered argv, no sleeps/live services, JSON-only stdout in report mode, and mutation-free second successful reconciliation.
