title: Interrupted replacement recovery can accept a config-shrunken Brave plan
description:
Observation
- Replacement fingerprints only the serialized target Session at src/main.rs:346-352 and stores only that raw target digest in ReplaceMarker; the marker schema at src/session.rs:241-270 contains no configuration or expanded-target fingerprint.
- Initial replacement validation expands Brave targets with the then-current config at src/restore.rs:1992-2003. brave_profile_targets filters saved profile inventory through the current profile_workspaces map at src/restore.rs:3149-3192.
- The transaction enters InProgress before target reconciliation and reaches Finalizing only after the whole target report has no failures or skips at src/restore.rs:2327-2396. An interruption after one of several sequential profile targets leaves InProgress.
- The next invocation loads the fresh current config before startup recovery at src/main.rs:121-136. Because the raw target file is unchanged, its digest passes at src/main.rs:738-752. replacement_target_is_complete_with_backup then rebuilds target count and clients with the new config at src/restore.rs:2587 and 2616-2632.
- If a removed profile mapping was the only unfinished target, the shrunken plan now matches. Recovery returns true, clears the marker, rotates autosaves, and bypasses replay of the safety snapshot at src/main.rs:753-757.

Root cause
The durable transaction fingerprints a raw snapshot while completion is defined over config-dependent expanded targets. Post-crash verification therefore substitutes mutable current configuration for the authoritative plan that actually began.

Production trigger and impact
Start replacement with a valid session and config that expand Brave profiles Default and Profile 1. After Default is restored but before Profile 1 and finalization, the process or machine stops. Before the next CLI invocation, validly remove Profile 1 from profile_workspaces. Startup accepts only Default as the complete target, finalizes an incomplete destructive operation, abandons automatic recovery, and removes active-marker protection from the safety snapshot so it becomes rotation-eligible.

Alternatives checked
The existing config-drift guard rejects ignored-class changes but does not cover profile mappings. The marker stores neither the effective target set nor its expansion inputs, and Finalizing cannot be written before the full original target loop succeeds. This is distinct from gqg.21, whose plan starts empty, and gqg.13, where malformed config falls back to defaults; both configurations here are valid.

Contract
canon/architecture/session-operations.md requires an interrupted replacement to retain enough durable state for safety recovery. Completion must be judged against the plan that began, not a later mutable proxy.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Begin replacement of a session whose Brave targets expand under the current configuration and stop after InProgress target placement but before finalization.
2. Change configuration so the same raw saved session expands to fewer targets.
3. Restart recovery.
4. Observe the marker authenticating only the raw session fingerprint while completion uses the newly shrunken effective plan and may clear the marker despite never completing the original request.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Build one immutable EffectiveReplacementPlan after all filtering, hydration, Brave expansion, identity checks, and launch preflight. Persist a versioned digest covering every target identity, launch, placement, and policy-dependent expansion input; execute that exact plan and require the same digest for completion recovery. Missing, legacy, or mismatched evidence triggers conservative additive safety recovery and retains actionable marker state. Preserve backward-readable marker/session formats and never weaken safety-snapshot validation.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests prove deterministic plan canonicalization/digest across ordering, every included field, unchanged config, config shrink/growth/remap/ignore, and legacy/malformed marker versions. Crash-point tests cover every marker phase and completion decision. Actual-CLI e2e combines storage, process, and fake-Hyprland fixtures; interrupt through deterministic readiness boundaries, alter config, restart, and assert exact marker/session manifests, target/safety state, dispatch/spawn argv, marker clearing/retention, subsequent command availability, exit/stdout/stderr, and bounded redacted JSONL. No sleeps/live services/secrets. Include unchanged-plan completion, additive extras, and idempotent recovery retry.

title: Brave profile expansion resurrects targets excluded by ignore filters
description:
Observation
- brave_profile_targets derives saved Brave profiles without consulting filters.ignore_classes at src/restore.rs:3149-3236.
- build_reconcile_targets correctly filters raw session clients and its Brave template pool at src/restore.rs:3247-3282. When all raw Brave clients are excluded, however, each saved profile falls through to a synthesized SessionClient with class and initial_class brave-browser at src/restore.rs:3291-3346, and that target is pushed unconditionally at src/restore.rs:3348-3362. There is no final filter over constructed targets.
- Replacement validation trusts this rebuilt list at src/restore.rs:1992-2025. The synthetic target makes the effective list appear nonempty and launchable, so the NoRestorableTargets guard does not fire before current windows are closed.
- Plain restore and reconciliation likewise consume the profile-derived targets without a later ignore check. Current ignored Brave windows are filtered from observation, so an already-open excluded profile can even be treated as missing and duplicated.

Root cause
Ignore filtering is applied to raw inputs rather than at the effective target boundary. Brave profile expansion is a second source that can synthesize new clients after the policy filter and thereby resurrect an excluded class.

Production trigger and impact
Capture a session containing a safely identified Brave profile, then validly add brave-browser to filters.ignore_classes. Restoring or reconciling the older session can launch or repair the excluded browser profile. Replacing with an otherwise Brave-only target should cancel because nothing remains restorable, but instead passes preflight, closes every current client, launches the explicitly ignored profile, reports success, and clears its recovery marker.

Alternatives checked
A session newly captured after the ignore rule is added will omit the profile, but config changes applied to existing sessions are ordinary and explicitly supported for raw classes. Missing or untrusted binaries abort pre-close, but an installed authorized Brave binary reaches the defect. No downstream trust, ambiguity, observation, or launch check reapplies ignore policy. This is distinct from gqg.21, where a truly empty plan bypasses a raw-session conditional, and gqg.23, which requires an interrupted transaction and later profile-map drift.

Contract
canon/architecture/session-operations.md requires replacement to confirm an effective restorable target before any close. Existing raw-target filtering and replacement regressions establish ignore_classes as restore policy, not capture-only metadata.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Save a legacy Brave client whose raw class is allowed but whose current profile expansion synthesizes a target class now listed in ignore_classes.
2. Run plain restore, reconcile, or replacement.
3. Observe ignore filtering applied before synthesis and not reapplied to the expanded target.
4. The ignored application is launched/repaired, or prevents the replacement plan from becoming correctly empty.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Create one effective-target builder used by validation, plain restore, reconciliation, replacement digest/execution, and recovery. Apply ignore policy after every raw, hydrated, and synthesized target source, retaining provenance for diagnostics. Ignored targets never reach ambiguity validation, launch, placement, or close logic. If final replacement targets are empty, gqg.21 rejects before mutation. Preserve included Brave profiles, non-Brave targets, legacy sessions, and additive extras.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests cover raw ignored class, synthesized ignored class, initial-class rule, mixed profiles, no profile expansion, legacy session, and identical effective targets across all callers. Actual-CLI e2e coordinates profile/process and fake-Hyprland fixtures for plain/reconcile/replace; assert zero ignored spawn/repair/close, exact included-target argv/state, report accounting and exit, stdout/stderr, and bounded redacted JSONL. Include ignored-only replacement preflight, safe mixed control, no sleeps/live services, JSON-only stdout where supported, and mutation-free second pass.

title: Direct-profile Omarchy webapps are captured with nonexistent launch binaries
description:
Observation
- Omarchy supports direct desktop entries such as Exec=omarchy-launch-webapp URL --profile-directory="Profile 1"; /usr/bin/omarchy-launch-webapp forwards arguments after the URL to Chromium. A normal runtime class for that entry is chrome-HOST__-Profile_1.
- capture.rs tokenizes the complete Exec line at src/capture.rs:407-423, and its URL/class helpers recognize Profile_# suffixes. However, the direct omarchy-launch-webapp match at src/capture.rs:432-454 ignores the explicit profile argument and accepts only identities whose class suffix is Default.
- Discovery therefore returns None for a unique valid non-default-profile entry. build_launch_info falls through to the window class as launch.command at src/capture.rs:163-183, even though chrome-HOST__-Profile_1 is a class and not an executable. Save succeeds because the persisted structure is otherwise valid.
- Restore hydration retries the same discovery and leaves the class command unchanged at src/restore.rs:3377-3396. Once the web app is closed, plain restore rejects the class command through webapp launch trust at src/restore.rs:1480-1488, and reconciliation rejects it at src/restore.rs:2991-3007. Both exit nonzero without relaunching the saved target.

Root cause
The direct desktop-entry parser infers profile identity only from a hard-coded Default class suffix even when the authoritative, already-tokenized Exec argv explicitly names a non-default profile. Valid evidence is discarded before launch metadata is persisted.

Production trigger and impact
Save an open Omarchy web app whose unique desktop entry launches directly with --profile-directory=Profile N, then close it and restore or reconcile the session. Hyprloom reports the save successful but deterministically cannot relaunch that target. This occurs with ordinary generated/user-installed desktop-entry syntax and breaks the core restore path without requiring malformed input or configuration.

Alternatives checked
The launcher really forwards the profile argument; the matching URL and runtime class can be proven; a unique entry still fails, so XDG precedence is not causal. Hydration uses the same rejecting parser and no app override exists in the ordinary trigger. This is distinct from gqg.2, which loses Brave proc argv boundaries, and gqg.19, which ignores desktop-ID override precedence.

Scope
The failure is safe and non-destructive: replacement preflight also rejects the unusable launch before closing clients. Severity is P2 because normal additive relaunch fails.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch an Omarchy webapp directly with a non-Default Brave profile, such as Profile 1.
2. Capture its window, whose class is Profile_1.
3. Observe direct-launch recognition handling only Default and falling through to desktop/class discovery.
4. The saved launch binary becomes Profile_1 or another nonexistent command, so later restore cannot launch the valid webapp.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Using the argv-preserving process API from gqg.2, recognize direct Omarchy launcher invocations and parse the exact profile-directory argument. Map only Default and canonical Profile N values to Default/Profile_N classes, reject conflicting or ambiguous evidence, and persist the complete authorized launcher argv rather than the class. Keep desktop-entry discovery as an independent fallback and preflight every effective nested launcher before replacement closes windows.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests cover Default, Profile 1/Profile 10, equals/two-token forms, spaced values, class/profile conflict, duplicate flags, malformed profile, and unrelated processes. Actual-CLI capture-to-restore e2e uses the process/launch fixture; assert saved launch JSON and exact spawn argv, no Profile_N executable attempt, missing-launcher preflight before replacement mutation, exit/stdout/stderr, and bounded redacted JSONL. Include desktop-entry and legacy-session controls, no sleeps/live browser/services, no secret URL/profile logging, and mutation-free second restore.

title: Flipped monitor transforms bypass geometry adaptation
description:
Observation
- adapt_client_geometry applies transform-aware canonical conversion only when both saved and current transform values are less than 4 at src/placement.rs:41-64 and 94-95.
- If either transform is 4 through 7, the fallback at src/placement.rs:65-75 merely scales the original unreflected x/y and size. displayed_monitor_dimensions still treats odd values as rotated, so flipped-rotation cases can also be scaled in one axis convention and clamped in another.
- Hyprland 0.54 officially supports 0 normal, 1/2/3 rotations, 4 flipped, and 5/6/7 flipped plus rotation. Wayland defines the flipped values as a vertical-axis flip followed by rotation.
- At equal 1920x1080 resolution and scale, changing transform 0 to 4 for a floating rectangle at x=100 with width=400 should place its reflected left edge at 1920-100-400=1420. Hyprloom leaves x=100.

Root cause
The monitor model persists the full Hyprland transform domain, but geometry conversion implements only its rotational subset. Unsupported valid values silently fall through to a transform-agnostic scaling algorithm instead of applying reflection and rotation.

Production trigger and impact
Save a floating-window session on a monitor, change that monitor between normal/rotated and any flipped transform, then restore or reconcile. Hyprloom deterministically moves and sizes windows using the wrong coordinate frame, often on the opposite side of the display; flipped 90/270 transitions can also use mismatched axes. The command can report a successful repair even though the saved relative placement was not restored.

Alternatives checked
Transforms 4-7 are supported production values, not malformed input. A stable same-flip configuration can retain unchanged coordinates, but any transition involving those values exposes the omitted conversion. The failure reproduces at equal resolution and scale, so it is distinct from gqg.7, whose cause is missing physical-to-logical scale conversion.

Upstream provenance
https://wiki.hypr.land/0.54.0/Configuring/Monitors/
https://wayland.freedesktop.org/docs/html/apa.html

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Save window geometry on a monitor using Wayland transform 4, 5, 6, or 7.
2. Restore after monitor layout/origin/transform changes.
3. Observe geometry adaptation taking the unsupported-transform fallback instead of applying reflection plus rotation.
4. The window is placed on the wrong side or outside the intended logical monitor area while reporting success.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Implement all eight Wayland output transforms in one canonical logical-coordinate geometry engine, including the specified reflection followed by rotation and a defined inverse. Apply origin, scale, and transform in an explicit order and reject invalid dimensions. Retain legacy/session geometry fields and untransformed behavior; share the engine across plain, reconcile, replacement, and verification so no caller bypasses reflected adaptation.
acceptance_criteria: Unit table tests and property tests cover transforms 0-7, inverse/round-trip, corners/edges, odd dimensions, negative origins, layout changes, invalid monitor sizes, and composition with scale. Actual-CLI e2e uses fake-Hyprland for normal-to-flipped, flipped-to-normal, and flipped-to-rotated cases; assert exact adapted coordinates, ordered dispatch/state, report/exit/stdout/stderr, bounded redacted JSONL, and mutation-free second pass. Include legacy transform-absent and unchanged-monitor controls, preserved extras, no sleeps/live compositor, and JSON-only stdout where supported.

title: Ignored ambiguous Brave clients fail plain restore before filtering
description:
Observation
- Capturing multiple Brave windows sharing one PID cannot assign a window-specific profile, so the saved clients are profile_identity_ambiguous=true while capture_brave_profiles can still retain the positively discovered active profile inventory at src/capture.rs:62-89, 118, 156-160, and 212-247.
- If brave-browser is later added to ignore_classes, brave_profile_targets still examines those raw saved clients. With no per-window profile directories and an ambiguous multiwindow snapshot, it returns Some(empty) at src/restore.rs:3195-3219.
- Plain restore consequently sets unsafe_empty_brave_profile_mode at src/restore.rs:1308-1316. Its per-client loop increments failed and continues for every ambiguous Brave client at src/restore.rs:1328-1336 before it reaches the ignore filter at src/restore.rs:1342-1349.
- Main treats any such failure as a nonzero restore. Reconciliation filters the same saved clients before target construction at src/restore.rs:3247-3254 and exits cleanly with zero effective targets. Replacement ambiguity validation also explicitly exempts ignored clients.

Root cause
Plain restore runs a raw-client ambiguity validator before determining whether policy includes that client in the effective target set. Identity failure is therefore attributed to a class that ignore policy has removed from the requested operation.

Production trigger and impact
Save an ordinary session with two Brave windows sharing a browser PID and a retained profile inventory. Later add brave-browser to ignore_classes and run plain restore or dry-run. Hyprloom performs no work for the excluded class but reports each client failed and exits nonzero. Mixed sessions can complete every included target yet still appear failed, breaking automation and disagreeing with reconciliation over the same configuration.

Alternatives checked
An explicit empty profile map suppresses this particular branch, but the ordinary no-map configuration reaches it. Ignore is not capture-only: capture, current observation, reconcile target building, replacement validation, and the later plain-restore branch all enforce it. This is related to but distinct from gqg.24: that issue synthesizes and mutates a nonempty ignored profile target after filtering, while this path synthesizes nothing and falsely fails solely because the early ambiguity continue precedes filtering.

Contract
Ambiguity safeguards apply to requested Brave targets. A class excluded by current restore policy is not a target and cannot make the operation incomplete.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Save an ambiguous Brave client whose class or initial class is now ignored by configuration.
2. Run plain restore.
3. Observe the ambiguity safety check executing before ignore filtering.
4. The command reports failure/nonzero for a target policy says must not be considered or mutated.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Run current-policy ignore filtering at the first effective-target boundary before Brave ambiguity or launch validation, and reapply after synthesis through the builder from gqg.24. Ignored clients produce no effective target and no failure; included ambiguous clients remain unresolved and nonzero. Preserve mixed-session independent targets, legacy filters, and no-action guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Unit truth tables cover ignored current/initial class, included ambiguous class, mixed ignored/included, absent/incomplete profile maps, synthesis, and caller parity. Actual-CLI e2e coordinates fake-Hyprland and process fixtures; assert ignored targets cause no process/profile work beyond necessary filtering and no spawn/dispatch, included ambiguity exits 1, ignored-only exits 0, exact stdout/stderr, and bounded redacted JSONL. Include safe included and legacy config controls, no sleeps/live services, and mutation-free repeat.

title: Generic relaunch ambiguity is treated as absence and launches duplicate windows
description:
Observation
- relaunch_fallback_identity_matches at src/restore.rs:811-850 recognizes a changed-address non-browser target from matching class and title plus working-directory or executable evidence.
- Planning and refreshed matching deliberately reject assignment when more than one current window satisfies that fallback at src/restore.rs:455-466 and 1728-1737.
- Normal restore and reconciliation then distinguish ambiguity only for web apps, same-address identity loss, generic Chromium, or conservative safety recovery. Ordinary generic targets fall through from no match to the launch path at src/restore.rs:2930-3079; plain restore has the same gap at src/restore.rs:1379-1475.

Root cause
The match API represents both genuinely absent and present-but-ambiguous as None. Its callers do not preserve the reason the uniqueness guard rejected a match, so they infer absence and spawn another instance.

Production trigger and impact
Save a Kitty or editor target, restart the compositor or application so its address changes, then have two current same-class windows with the same initial title and executable or project CWD. Both are valid relaunch fallbacks, neither is assigned, and Hyprloom launches a third window and reports it restored. Repeated runs can add further duplicates instead of converging.

Alternatives checked
Creating the saved logical instance is not safe when live evidence already shows multiple indistinguishable candidates. The uniqueness guards explicitly reject that ownership inference, and canon/architecture/session-operations.md permits launches only for genuinely missing targets. This is distinct from gqg.12, where an addressless legacy title match is promoted to arbitrary ownership, and gqg.10, which concerns success status after safe skips; this path mutates the desktop by launching an extra process.

We would substantially revise this conclusion if supported generic applications could not produce two current windows sharing these fallback signals, or if a normal-mode ambiguity gate stopped before spawn. Neither condition is present.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Load a missing/stale generic target and expose two equally plausible relaunch candidates.
2. Run reconciliation through the relaunch fallback.
3. Observe candidate resolution returning None for both no candidate and ambiguous candidates.
4. The caller interprets ambiguity as absence and spawns a duplicate window.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Return a typed candidate resolution of Matched, Absent, or Ambiguous(reason) from every relaunch matcher. Only proven Absent authorizes a spawn. Ambiguous preserves every candidate as an extra, reports the target unresolved, and exits incomplete. Build on gqg.12 evidence tiers and use the same result in global/greedy reconciliation, replacement completion, and recovery.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests cover zero/one/two candidates, score ties/margins, stale/reused addresses, stable identity, candidate-order permutations, global/greedy strategies, and prove only Absent reaches spawn. Actual-CLI e2e coordinates fake-Hyprland and process fixtures; assert exact observations, zero ambiguous spawn/dispatch, report reason and exit 1, stdout/stderr, bounded redacted JSONL, preserved extras, and mutation-free repeat. Include uniquely matched and genuinely absent launch controls, no sleeps/live services, and JSON-only stdout where supported.

title: Tiled restore and repair report geometry success without restorable topology
description:
Scope clarification: this Bead is the sole owner of geometry/topology truth for both newly launched tiled windows and already-matched tiled windows. Pixel geometry no-ops or split-ratio mutations on matched windows and layout-insertion reversal for launched windows are two manifestations of the same missing tiled-topology model.

Observation
- Placement emits absolute resizewindowpixel and movewindowpixel repairs whenever coordinates differ, regardless of the saved target being tiled, at src/placement.rs:300-317. Newly launched targets receive the same absolute pixel operations at src/restore.rs:4012-4050.
- Hyprland 0.54 dispatches these calls through its layout manager. moveTarget returns without moving a non-floating target, while tiled resizing changes shared layout ratios and can reflow sibling windows. The dispatcher can therefore acknowledge transport while the requested tiled position is not established: https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/v0.54.0/src/managers/KeybindManager.cpp#L2052-L2099 and https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/v0.54.0/src/layout/LayoutManager.cpp#L49-L90.
- Hyprloom never verifies the final geometry after placement. It increments moved after successful dispatch at src/restore.rs:2897-2907 and records a launched target after launch correlation and placement return at src/restore.rs:3691.

Root cause
The restore model treats floating absolute geometry commands as a universal tiled-layout reconstruction primitive and equates dispatcher acknowledgement with satisfaction of the requested postcondition. It persists neither tiling topology nor insertion order and performs no final-state verification.

Production trigger and impact
Under Dwindle force_split=1, save equal tiled windows after opening A then B, which leaves B on the left and A on the right. Target construction sorts them spatially, so an empty restore launches B then A. The layout inserts A on the left and reflows B right. A already has the requested half-size, and its absolute move to the saved right side is a no-op while tiled. The final order is reversed even though both targets are reported successfully launched. Matched tiled repairs can likewise be counted moved when their position did not change, and a later launch can invalidate geometry previously reported successful.

Alternatives checked
Sequential tiled resizes cannot repair the equal-size reversal because the second target needs no resize and absolute tiled movement is the no-op. This is distinct from gqg.14, where hyprctl batch errors are hidden: here Hyprland accepts the dispatcher while the placement postcondition remains false. It is also independent of monitor scale and transform conversion defects.

We would substantially revise this conclusion if supported Hyprland moved tiled targets to absolute pixels, Hyprloom replayed layout topology or insertion order, temporarily floated targets for exact placement, or verified final tiled geometry and surfaced mismatch. None occurs.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Save multiple tiled windows with known relative geometry/order.
2. Test both paths: launch them into an empty target workspace, and reconcile already-matched tiled windows whose apparent pixel geometry differs.
3. Observe compositor layout insertion reordering launched windows, while pixel move/resize on matched tiled windows no-ops or changes split ratios rather than restoring saved rectangles.
4. Restore/reconcile reports geometry success although no verified tiled topology matches the session and later passes churn or remain reversed.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Treat tiled placement as topology, not floating pixel geometry. One shared planner must distinguish floating geometry from tiled windows in both launch and matched-repair paths. Until a supported layout topology can be captured, represented backward-compatibly, replayed, and verified, preserve safe workspace/monitor/state placement but return an explicit unsupported/incomplete tiled-topology outcome instead of emitting misleading pixel commands or success. If topology replay is implemented, verify the final complete layout only after all layout-affecting launches. Preserve additive extras and never reorder unrelated tiled windows speculatively.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests cover newly launched and already-matched tiled windows under Dwindle and Master models, insertion order permutations, pixel-command rejection/no-op/split changes, mixed floating+tiled targets, one window, extras, unsupported layout, and truthful completion. Assert no floating-only pixel geometry command is issued for tiled repair unless an explicitly supported topology algorithm requires it. Actual-CLI e2e uses stateful fake-Hyprland for both branches; assert exact ordered states/argv, final topology or explicit incomplete status, exit/stdout/stderr, bounded redacted JSONL, preserved unrelated windows, and mutation-free second pass after a supported success. No sleeps/live compositor; report JSON stdout is exactly one document.

title: Process enrichment repeats per shared PID and per reconciliation target
description:
Observation
- src/capture.rs:62-73 invokes Brave profile discovery for every Brave client and only then inserts into a PID-keyed map; multiple windows sharing one browser PID repeat identical work.
- src/restore.rs:3402-3460 enriches every observed client with process-tree, terminal, and Brave evidence.
- Reconciliation performs a full enriched observation at src/restore.rs:2731, repeats it before every non-dry-run target at 2803-2812, and performs another final observation. Target zero repeats the initial process enrichment before any mutation.
- The supported ceiling is 512 targets and 512 current windows.

Root cause
Cheap compositor freshness and expensive process discovery are fused into one per-window operation. There is neither a per-snapshot unique-PID cache nor a narrower cross-refresh validity policy, so the wrong scope is recomputed at both levels.

Production trigger and impact
An ordinary browser session repeats the same process-tree walk once per shared-PID window during capture and each restore observation. A many-target desktop additionally re-walks every unrelated client tree before each sequential target, producing O(targets * clients * process-tree) reads. This adds user-visible latency and widens exposure to transient /proc races.

Constraint
Process evidence can change between restore polls, so a blanket persistent PID cache would be unsound. Per-close lightweight client queries used for destructive identity revalidation are outside this finding.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Reconcile a session with many targets and several current windows sharing the same PID/profile process.
2. Instrument ProcessInfoProvider and hyprctl observation calls.
3. Observe full client/process/profile enrichment repeated for shared PIDs and again before successive targets.
4. Whole-snapshot work grows with targets times clients/process descendants even though most process identity is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Split lightweight compositor refresh from expensive process/profile enrichment. Cache positive evidence and completeness by (pid, process_start_time) for one reconciliation transaction, invalidate on process identity change, and enrich only newly mapped or otherwise affected PIDs after launch. Preserve targeted pre-dispatch address/state revalidation and one-to-one matching; do not cache incomplete negatives as authoritative. Keep dry/real reports and dispatch plans behaviorally identical apart from execution.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic unit tests with a counting provider prove expensive calls scale with unique process identities plus launched replacements rather than targets times clients. Cover shared PID, PID/start-time reuse, incomplete walks, new mappings, disappearing clients, Brave profiles, global/greedy matching, and identical report/dispatch results to an uncached reference model. Actual-CLI e2e coordinates process and fake-Hyprland fixtures with a many-target scripted session; assert exact observation/spawn/dispatch order, bounded call counts (not timing), final state, exit/stdout/stderr, bounded redacted JSONL, and mutation-free second pass. No profiler thresholds, sleeps, live services, or host PID assumptions.

title: Valid autosave retention above 1000 is silently clamped before destructive rotation
description:
Observation
- autosave_retain is a recognized usize setting documented as the number of snapshots to keep, with no stated maximum in README.md:195-200.
- Config::normalize silently rewrites any accepted value above 1000 to 1000 at src/config.rs:55-62. rotate_autosaves independently applies the same cap at src/session.rs:1198-1204 and deletes all older snapshots.
- The ordinary autosave --now and timer path captures a new snapshot, rotates, and reports success at src/main.rs:590-625. The config display does not reveal the configured or effective retention value at src/main.rs:514-525.
- canon/architecture/autosave-lifecycle.md requires rotation to keep the newest configured count.

Root cause
A resource-safety bound is implemented as silent normalization immediately before irreversible deletion. Parsing success is treated as operator authorization even though the accepted value is then changed, and no validation or user-visible contract distinguishes damaged input from a legitimate larger retention window.

Production trigger and impact
Set autosave_retain = 2016 for two weeks of history at the documented ten-minute schedule. The value parses successfully, but the next ordinary autosave retains only 1000 snapshots, roughly six days and twenty-two hours, and permanently deletes the rest while reporting success. An upgrade or configuration change on a store already holding more than 1000 snapshots can remove the excess in one run.

Alternatives checked
The internal constant, comment, and normalization test show that the cap is deliberate. They do not make silent destructive reinterpretation safe or satisfy the routed user-visible guarantee. This is distinct from gqg.13, which requires a detected invalid config falling back to defaults, and unknown-config-keys-silent-us5, which requires an unrecognized key; this path uses a syntactically valid recognized setting.

We would substantially revise this conclusion if a routed normative or user-facing contract stated the 1000 maximum and its clamping behavior, or if unsupported values were rejected with a warning before any capture or pruning. Neither exists.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure autosave_retain to a valid value greater than 1000, such as 1001, and seed more autosaves than that value.
2. Invoke an autosave-producing or replacement path that rotates sessions.
3. Observe Config::normalize silently clamping the value to 1000.
4. A valid snapshot that the configured policy says to retain is deleted without warning.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Remove the undocumented destructive clamp and honor every successfully parsed usize retention value. If a maximum is later authorized, encode it as explicit validation with a public documented contract and reject before capture/rotation; never normalize it silently. Preserve absent-config default retention, retain=0 semantics, unknown/invalid-config failure behavior, protected replacement roots, and backward-compatible TOML.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests cover 0, default, 999, 1000, 1001, larger representable values, overflow/parse error, config round-trip, and exact rotation survivor sets. Actual-CLI e2e uses the isolated storage fixture with 1002 minimal valid autosave names and retain=1001; assert exactly the policy-authorized deletion, preserved file manifest/content hashes, no silent normalization, exit/stdout/stderr, and bounded redacted JSONL. Include absent-config, retain=0, invalid/unknown-key, active-marker protection, and retry controls. No live user store/systemd, sleeps, timestamps beyond deterministic fixture names, or secret file contents.
close_reason: Fixed: removed the undocumented destructive autosave_retain clamp at both boundaries. Config::normalize no longer rewrites parsed retention values (the MAX_AUTOSAVE_RETAIN constant is deleted) and rotate_autosaves honors the configured usize exactly, keeping the newest configured count per canon/architecture/autosave-lifecycle.md ('rotation keeps the newest configured count' - the code now conforms to the routed normative guarantee instead of silently contradicting it). Absent-config defaults, retain=0 semantics, unknown/invalid config keys, and backward-compatible TOML are unchanged. Evidence: config unit tests prove normalize preserves 1001 and usize::MAX and keeps 0; a rotation survivor-set test proves 6 seeds with retain=4 prune exactly the 2 oldest and retain=0 clears the store; the CLI e2e seeds 1002 valid autosaves with retain=1001 and asserts through the real binary that exactly one new capture lands, exactly the two oldest seeds are deleted, all 1000 remaining survivors are byte-identical (content hashes), and the effective retention is the configured 1001 with no silent normalization. Gate: fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --locked (317 tests), htF sync check all pass.

title: Replacement rotation can delete its active autosave target before the transaction starts
description:
Observation
- replace accepts any valid session name and loads the selected target at src/main.rs:338-352, including an autosave-prefixed snapshot.
- It then captures and saves a new safety autosave, records a Prepared marker naming both backup and target, and rotates retention before replacement starts at src/main.rs:365-394.
- rotate_autosaves protects only pending_replace_backup at src/session.rs:1198-1215. It does not protect the target_name already stored in the same marker.
- Startup completion verification for an interrupted InProgress transaction must reload target_name and compare its fingerprint at src/main.rs:737-770. A target pruned by the pre-start rotation cannot be verified.

Root cause
Retention protection models the active transaction as owning only its safety backup, while durable recovery also depends on the exact selected target. The marker persists both names and a target digest, but rotation consults only the backup name and can destroy the other required input.

Production trigger and impact
With retention full at N snapshots, run replace on the oldest retained autosave. Creating the safety backup pushes that target past N; the immediate rotation deletes the explicitly selected snapshot while replacement continues from its in-memory copy. Even an uninterrupted successful command silently removes the target the user selected. If the process stops after target restoration but before finalization, startup cannot prove completion and performs additive safety recovery. It can preserve the restored target windows as extras while relaunching the old desktop, leaving a mixed desktop, and the exact target is unavailable for retry.

Alternatives checked
Ordinary retention pruning and the in-memory target explain why uninterrupted replacement can finish, but do not restore the durable recovery input after interruption. Autosave names are not rejected as replacement targets, and pending_replace_backup exposes only marker.backup_name. This is distinct from gqg.23, where mutable Brave expansion can falsely accept an incomplete target; here self-deletion prevents completion proof and forces safety replay.

We would substantially revise this conclusion if autosave-prefixed sessions were rejected as replace targets before safety capture, or every rotation protected the active marker target as well as its backup. Neither is true.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Select an autosave session as the replacement target and make it the oldest autosave beyond the configured retention count.
2. Start replace.
3. Observe target loaded in memory and marker written, then rotate_autosaves protecting only the safety backup.
4. Rotation deletes the named target before replacement/recovery finishes, so an interruption can make exact completion or recovery impossible.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: Derive a protected session-root set from every active replacement marker phase and include both safety backup and named target. Rotation excludes all protected roots even for retain 0/1 until transaction resolution; after marker clearing, later ordinary retention may apply normally. Preserve the in-memory effective plan, marker backward compatibility, atomic rotation, and unrelated autosave ordering. Recovery must report a missing legacy target conservatively rather than clearing evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests cover target oldest/newest, backup oldest, retain 0/1/N, every marker phase, same backup/target rejection, malformed/legacy marker, rotation failure, and exact survivor ordering. Actual-CLI e2e uses the storage fixture for uninterrupted and readiness-interrupted replacement; assert target and backup manifests/hashes survive while marked, exact marker transitions, later cleanup policy, exit/stdout/stderr, and bounded redacted JSONL. Include non-autosave target and no-marker controls, retry/idempotence, no live user files/services/sleeps, and no session-content logging.

title: Generic initial titles let relaunch fallback consume an unrelated sole window
description:
Observation
- title_identity_agrees at src/restore.rs:780-786 accepts equality of initial titles as positive relaunch evidence, and process_command_matches_target accepts only an executable-basename match.
- relaunch_fallback_identity_matches at src/restore.rs:811-849 therefore accepts a changed-address generic window when those two application-wide signals agree, even when both current runtime title and captured working directory conflict.
- strong_identity_conflict at src/restore.rs:698-718 suppresses its title-and-CWD veto whenever initial titles agree. add_context_score treats a known CWD mismatch as only a score penalty at src/restore.rs:657-669.
- Kitty windows ordinarily share initialTitle = kitty and executable kitty; tests/fixtures/sample_clients.json:11-15 contains this exact application-wide initial title.

Root cause
The relaunch fallback treats application identity as window ownership. Generic initial title and executable basename are shared by every instance, yet their conjunction can override two window-specific negative observations. The uniqueness guard proves only that one weak candidate is visible, not that it is the saved logical window.

Production trigger and impact
Capture Kitty A with capture_cwd enabled, then close it. Open unrelated Kitty B in another directory with a different runtime title. B has the same class, initial title, and executable but a different address and CWD. As the sole fallback candidate it passes uniqueness, is consumed as A, and is moved to A placement or reported unchanged. A is never launched, the requested CWD remains absent, and an unrelated active terminal is mutated while reconciliation can exit successfully. Plain restore uses the same matcher.

Alternatives checked
Avoiding duplicate launches can justify caution, but not positive ownership in the face of conflicting runtime title and CWD. The identity Canon prohibits moving unrelated same-class windows. This is distinct from gqg.28, which requires two weak candidates and launches an extra after ambiguity collapses to absence, and gqg.12, which requires an addressless legacy title promotion; this path has a modern stale address and exactly one explicit relaunch fallback.

We would substantially revise this conclusion if a downstream gate required matching CWD or another window-specific signal, or if supported Kitty instances had unique initial titles. Neither is true.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Save a terminal target with generic initial title Kitty and known CWD A, then close it while an unrelated Kitty window at known CWD B remains.
2. Reconcile and script the intended relaunched window as delayed.
3. Observe relaunch fallback accepting the sole same-initial-title window despite the positive CWD conflict.
4. The unrelated window is consumed/repositioned and the intended window later appears as an extra.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate Acceptance Criteria field is authoritative. Completion requires deterministic unit/property and actual-CLI evidence, preservation controls, and fail-closed behavior described there.
design: In relaunch correlation, treat every available authoritative positive conflict, including known differing CWD, as a veto; generic application-wide initial title or executable evidence cannot override it. Use the Matched/Absent/Ambiguous resolution from gqg.28 and continue bounded polling for the intended candidate rather than consuming the unrelated window. Missing CWD remains inconclusive rather than a conflict. Preserve ordinary uniquely corroborated relaunches, existing extras, and fail-closed timeout behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property truth tables cover same/different/unknown CWD, generic/specific initial and current titles, stable ID/address, PID/start identity, command evidence, sole/multiple candidates, delayed intended mapping, and candidate order. Assert known conflict never matches. Actual-CLI e2e coordinates process and fake-Hyprland fixtures for Kitty A versus unrelated Kitty B; assert exact observation/mapping sequence, zero dispatch to B, selected intended address or explicit ambiguity, final extras, exit/stdout/stderr, and bounded redacted JSONL. Include matching-CWD and legacy missing-CWD controls, no sleeps/live services, JSON-only stdout where supported, and mutation-free second pass.

title: Reused safety addresses make completed replacement recovery reject strong stable identity
description:
A replacement can finish placing its target while the durable marker is still InProgress. Launch correlation permits a newly launched target to reuse a pre-launch compositor address when process evidence proves ownership. Completion recovery currently compares the safety snapshot to current clients by raw address first and returns incomplete before considering a positively different stable window identity.

Root cause: a recyclable dispatch handle is treated as stronger evidence than the stable identity captured to distinguish address reuse. This can reject a completed target, replay safety windows beside it, or retain a blocking marker after partial recovery.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Capture safety window S at address X with stable ID S1.
2. Replace it with target T and let Hyprland reuse X with stable ID T1.
3. Stop Hyprloom after T is placed but before Finalizing is durable.
4. Start a mutating command. Completion recovery sees X in the safety address set and rejects the completed target without comparing S1 and T1.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. Definitive identity conflict must allow exact target-completion proof to continue; inconclusive evidence must remain fail-closed and preserve recovery state.
design: Introduce one shared tri-state safety identity relation: Same, Different, or Unknown. Evaluate stable window identity, address, PID and start identity before applying any safety-presence veto. Same address with complete unequal stable IDs is Different; missing or one-sided evidence remains Unknown and preserves conservative recovery. Use one enriched compositor observation for both safety exclusion and exact target completion so the two decisions cannot drift.
acceptance_criteria: Implement the tri-state identity relation and remove the raw-address early return. Deterministic unit and property matrices must cover reused/same/missing stable IDs, same and different addresses, PID/start-time equality and reuse, same/different classes, multiple safety windows, and both complete and incomplete target plans. Fault tests must cover failure before and after Finalizing persistence and retain the marker/backup whenever proof is Unknown. Actual CLI e2e must use the .36.2 stateful Hyprland and .36.4 marker fixtures to seed an InProgress transaction after final placement, replay startup through the real binary, and assert exact current-client state, zero safety replay on definitive identity conflict, marker and backup lifecycle, exit status, human stdout/stderr, JSON-only stdout when requested, ordered redacted JSONL, and availability of a second mutating command. Include same-stable-ID and missing-evidence negative controls, legacy markers, no sleeps or live desktop, and second-run idempotence.

title: Safety-window checks ignore definitive Brave profile conflicts during completion recovery
description:
Replacement completion recovery uses class, stable/address identity, titles, and CWD to decide whether a pre-replacement safety window survived, but omits the unambiguous Brave profile directory already required by replacement preflight and retained by observation.

Root cause: generic page-title agreement can veto completion even when complete window-specific profile evidence proves that the current browser window belongs to a different profile. Recovery can then skip the safety target as ambiguous and leave the marker blocking later mutation.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Capture a safety Brave window for unambiguous Profile A.
2. Replace it with unambiguous Profile B showing the same page title.
3. Stop after Profile B is placed but before Finalizing is durable.
4. Restart recovery. Title agreement claims Profile A may remain even though the observed directory is definitively Profile B.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. Complete unequal profile identity must be negative ownership proof; missing or ambiguous profile identity must remain conservative.
design: Extend the shared safety identity relation with window-specific Brave profile evidence. When both observations are complete, unambiguous, nonempty, and unequal, classify the pair as Different before title fallback. Equal, missing, incomplete, or ambiguous profile evidence cannot prove difference. Removing a safety veto never establishes completion by itself; the exact target plan must still match one-to-one.
acceptance_criteria: Use authoritative profile evidence in safety-presence decisions without weakening the independent target-completion plan. Unit matrices must cover equal and unequal profiles, absent directories, ambiguous and incomplete discovery, shared-process profiles, equal and changed titles, stable-ID/address combinations, and multiple Brave windows. Fault tests must preserve the marker and backup whenever profile evidence is unavailable or ambiguous. Actual CLI e2e must use .36.2, .36.3, and .36.4 to model safety Profile A, completed target Profile B, equal titles, and an InProgress crash point; assert exact clients, no additive safety launch on definitive conflict, marker/backup disposition, subsequent command availability, exit code, stdout/stderr separation, optional JSON-only stdout, and ordered redacted JSONL with synthetic profile identifiers only. Include matching-profile and incomplete-discovery negative controls, legacy snapshots, no sleeps/live desktop, and second-run idempotence.

title: Kitty hint restore hardcodes an unvalidated zsh dependency
description:
Terminal capture recognizes sh, bash, fish, and zsh, but LaunchInfo discards which shell was selected. Kitty hint restore then generates an invocation containing a hardcoded nested zsh executable. Replacement preflight validates only the outer terminal binary.

Root cause: shell identity is lost at the capture-to-persistence boundary and destructive preflight models only argv zero even though Kitty executes the nested child program.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable last-command capture for a Kitty window whose interactive shell is Bash, Fish, or sh.
2. Save the session on a host without zsh.
3. Run replacement. Preflight accepts Kitty and closes the desktop.
4. The generated Kitty argv requests unavailable zsh, so neither target nor equivalent safety terminal can be recreated as planned.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. Supported shell identity and all runtime executable dependencies must survive capture, persistence, validation, restore, and recovery without silent shell substitution.
design: Persist an optional validated terminal-shell enum in LaunchInfo and capture only supported sh, bash, fish, or zsh identity. Build hint display argv from that enum and include every nested executable in target and safety preflight. Legacy hint-bearing sessions without shell metadata must launch the terminal without the hint and emit a bounded actionable diagnostic rather than inventing zsh. The hint remains display-only and is never executed as the captured command.
acceptance_criteria: Preserve the captured supported shell and validate all nested executables before destructive work. Unit tests must cover sh/bash/fish/zsh capture, serialization round trip, generated Kitty argv and escaping, missing shell binaries, unsupported/login-shell spellings, configured terminal binaries, no-hint behavior, and legacy sessions without shell metadata. Fault tests must prove target and safety preflight stop before backup/marker/close on an unavailable nested shell and preserve the live desktop. Actual CLI e2e must use .36.3 controlled process/launch helpers and the real binary to capture then restore each shell, log exact synthetic argv and lifecycle events in ordered redacted JSONL, and assert saved fields, spawned argv, marker/files, desktop mutations, exit code, human stdout/stderr, and JSON-only stdout where supported. Include ordinary restore, dry-run, replacement, recovery, negative/legacy controls, no sleeps/live desktop, and second-run idempotence.

title: Build deterministic production-bug verification infrastructure
description:
This epic owns reusable verification infrastructure for the production-bug audit. It does not replace issue-specific tests: each implementation Bead still owns regression cases for its exact root cause, negative controls, compatibility behavior, and user-visible reporting.

The infrastructure must preserve production interfaces. It runs the actual compiled CLI with isolated XDG data/config/runtime roots and controlled fake external executables. It records enough ordered evidence to diagnose a failed run without leaking session contents or depending on the user's desktop.

## Success Criteria

- A base CLI/e2e runner and focused Hyprland, process-launch, and storage/systemd fixtures are available to all audit children.
- Fixtures use deterministic state machines, explicit readiness signals, fixed identities/times, and bounded redacted JSONL logs rather than sleeps, live services, or uncontrolled process values.
- Each retained Bead includes comprehensive unit and CLI/e2e coverage, exact exit/output/state assertions, and a feature-preservation control.
- Human diagnostics remain on stderr; JSON-report stdout is exactly one parseable document when a report exists and empty for fatal pre-report failures.
- The suite is registered with the existing Rust test/CI path and prints actionable evidence on failure while cleaning isolated artifacts on success.
design: Use a layered test architecture. The base runner owns isolated process execution, output contracts, artifact lifecycle, redaction, and a stable JSONL event envelope. Three domain fixtures extend it at external boundaries: stateful Hyprland IPC, deterministic process/launcher lifecycles, and storage/lock/systemd fault injection. Product Beads depend on the smallest relevant fixture and retain ownership of their exact regression matrices. Deterministic fakes are the CI oracle; an optional nested-compositor smoke tier may supplement but never replace them. Logs use monotonic case-local sequence numbers and synthetic identities, cap untrusted output, omit secrets/user content, and preserve enough before/after evidence to identify the failed phase.
acceptance_criteria: All retained implementation Beads name the unit and CLI/e2e regressions that prove their trigger, fix, failure behavior, and compatibility controls. Shared fixtures execute the real compiled CLI in isolated XDG environments; capture ordered, redacted evidence; never touch the live desktop or user systemd manager; and run deterministically under cargo test --locked and CI. The live child rollup, lint, dependency-cycle check, and verification-contract audit must all pass before this epic closes.

title: Create isolated CLI/e2e runner with forensic JSONL traces
description:
Existing CLI tests prove selected paths but do not provide one reusable, stateful, diagnostically rich harness for the audit. Individual fixes would otherwise invent incompatible shell fixtures and make failures hard to reproduce.

The runner must invoke the real compiled binary. It may fake only external boundaries, must isolate all filesystem/environment state, and must never contact a live Hyprland compositor or systemd user manager.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run two existing CLI fixtures that need ordered multi-call external state and compare their ad hoc setup/log formats. There is no shared case identity, before/after snapshot, output-channel assertion helper, readiness protocol, or bounded redaction policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. Also prove a representative fixture failure prints the case ID, failed assertion, sanitized trace tail, and retained artifact location; prove a passing run cleans its directory. The harness must preserve all existing test entry points and require no live desktop state.
design: Provide Rust support APIs around assert_cmd and tempfile: a CaseBuilder creates unique HOME and XDG roots, prepends a fixture bin directory to PATH, scrubs unrelated environment, invokes the compiled CLI, captures stdout/stderr separately, and snapshots an allowlisted state manifest. A TraceSink writes one JSON object per event with schema version, case ID, sequence, component, operation, normalized synthetic arguments, outcome, and bounded sanitized details. Assertions attach trace context; Drop removes successful cases while a failure guard retains artifacts and prints their exact location. No wall-clock ordering, host PIDs, or live services participate in assertions.
acceptance_criteria: Provide reusable Rust test support that launches the actual compiled hyprloom binary with unique temporary HOME/XDG_DATA_HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME/XDG_RUNTIME_DIR roots and a controlled PATH. Record deterministic ordered JSONL evidence with case ID, sequence, fixture version, normalized argv, allowlisted environment keys, stdout, stderr, exit status, before/after state hashes, and assertion summaries. Redact secrets and user content; bound captured output; use explicit readiness signals instead of sleeps. Run representative success, fatal-pre-report, human-output, and --report-json contract tests under cargo test --locked and existing CI. Clean successful-case artifacts and retain/print a precise artifact location and trace tail on failure.
close_reason: Implemented by tests/support/mod.rs (Case harness) + tests/harness_contract.rs (6 contract tests). Real compiled binary via CARGO_BIN_EXE_hyprloom with env_clear-scrubbed unique HOME/XDG roots and fixture-bin PATH prefix; ordered JSONL trace (schema version, case id, monotonic seq, fixture version, normalized argv, redacted allowlisted env, bounded stdout/stderr, exit status, sha256 before/after state manifests, assertion summaries); explicit bounded readiness signals; drop guard cleans successful cases and retains artifacts with trace tail on failure. Deviation from design field: std::process::Command instead of assert_cmd (cargo_bin! is deprecated); acceptance-criteria field remains fully satisfied. Gate: cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --locked (280 tests), htF sync check all pass.

title: Build stateful fake-Hyprland contract fixture
description:
Placement and recovery bugs require more than fixed JSON responses: their correctness depends on ordered compositor transitions, changing window identities, focus context, and reply semantics. This task provides one deterministic external-boundary simulator shared by those regressions.

An optional nested-compositor smoke test may be added only as a separately selected environment contract. It must never target the user's live compositor and must skip with an actionable reason when prerequisites are unavailable; deterministic CI correctness remains owned by the fake.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run a multi-step restore against the current stateless fixture. It can return canned clients JSON and record argv, but it cannot verify post-dispatch state, delayed mappings, identity reuse, focus preservation, dialect negotiation, or second-pass convergence.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. Fixture logs must include case ID, monotonic sequence, request kind, normalized argv/logical operation, scripted reply, and before/after state identity without recording titles, URLs, CWDs, or command hints unless a synthetic sentinel is required by the test.
design: Implement the fake as a state machine behind a PATH-injected hyprctl executable or reusable scripted server. Its scenario declares initial clients/monitors/workspaces/focus/cursor, supported dispatch dialect/capabilities, mapping events, reply scripts, and fault points. Every query/dispatch advances a deterministic event sequence and atomically persists state; a test API validates invariants and final topology. Support direct and batch framing independently, including exit-zero rejection text, malformed replies, address reuse with new stable IDs, delayed appearance, and user-focus interleavings. Keep titles/CWDs/URLs synthetic and redact them from general traces.
acceptance_criteria: Implement a scripted/stateful fake hyprctl boundary covering clients, monitors, workspaces, active-window/cursor context, version/capability probes, direct dispatch, batch dispatch, mapping delays, address reuse, stable identities, provider dialects, and injected replies/failures. Log every request and logical state transition in ordered redacted JSONL. Unit-test fixture semantics; run CLI scenarios for restore, reconcile, replacement, recovery, dry-run, and second-pass convergence. Assert exact argv/order, final compositor state, report/exit truth, no mutation on preflight/dry-run failure, and no live Hyprland dependency.
close_reason: Implemented tests/support/fake_hyprland.rs (stateful fake-Hyprland boundary) + tests/fake_hyprland_fixture.rs (10 contract tests). PATH-injected sh relay forwards each hyprctl request to a deterministic in-test state machine; responses returned via per-request files as explicit readiness signals (bounded 60s relay timeout, no fixed sleeps in assertions). Covers clients/monitors/workspaces/activewindow/cursorpos/version probes, direct dispatch with state effects (movetoworkspacesilent, focuswindow, closewindow, pin, resize/move pixel), batch framing reusing hyprloom::hyprctl::parse_dispatch_args so the fake cannot drift from product framing, exit-nonzero and exit-zero-text batch rejection dialects, scripted faults, delayed mapping events, and address reuse via scenario state. Every request is logged to artifacts/hyprland.jsonl with case ID, monotonic seq, kind, normalized argv, logical operations, reply summary, and sha256 before/after topology identity; titles/URLs/CWDs never enter the log. CLI scenarios prove additive reconcile (unchanged = zero dispatches), batch-framed workspace repair, second-pass convergence (idempotent, zero further dispatches), and that a faulted repair exits nonzero with topology preserved. Nested-compositor smoke tier intentionally deferred: deterministic fakes remain the CI oracle per parent epic. Gate: fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --locked (290 tests), htF sync check all pass.

title: Build deterministic process and launch correlation fixture
description:
Capture and launch-correlation regressions need deterministic process lifecycles and exact argv evidence. Host /proc timing, arbitrary PIDs, and wall-clock sleeps make those cases flaky and obscure whether a failure is in capture, authorization, spawning, or correlation.

This fixture owns reusable helpers at the process-launch boundary. Product Beads continue to own their issue-specific assertions and unit tests.

## Steps to Reproduce

Attempt to reproduce daemonization, foreground-job selection, or spaced argv with ordinary short-lived host processes. Timing and PID allocation vary, and current fixtures do not provide an ordered causal trace spanning spawn, process evidence, compositor mapping, and report output.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. Add self-tests for every scripted lifecycle and for cleanup after failed child processes. Diagnostics must identify phase and synthetic target without leaking the full environment or arbitrary captured command content.
design: Provide small controlled helper executables plus an injected process-observation model. Scenario files/readiness pipes coordinate spawn, exec, fork/daemonize, foreground-group change, exit, mapping, and PID/start-identity reuse without sleeps. The helper logs argv as an array (never flattened), lifecycle transitions, and synthetic identity; the process provider can return complete, partial, or failed observations. Compose with the Hyprland fixture for end-to-end capture/correlation cases. Bound and redact command diagnostics, reap all children, and use explicit cleanup guards on failure.
acceptance_criteria: Provide controlled executable helpers and injected process observations for argv boundaries, foreground process groups/TTYs, descendant trees, daemonization, delayed window mapping, process exit, PID/start-identity reuse, missing binaries, and single-instance handoff. Coordinate with the fake-Hyprland fixture through readiness pipes/state files, never sleeps. Log exact synthetic argv and lifecycle events with stable case-local identities, bounded redaction, and no host-process assumptions. Cover capture-to-session-to-restore round trips, timeout/failure, retry, dry-run, replacement preflight, and no duplicate or unrelated placement.
