title: Build storage, locking, crash, and systemd fault fixtures
description:
Storage, replacement-recovery, autosave, and systemd lifecycle defects need reproducible failures at exact durability and external-command boundaries. Existing tests cover useful units but lack a common CLI fault-injection fixture and ordered before/after evidence.

The fixture must operate only under unique test directories and fake executables. Tests requiring an unavailable ownership primitive must use an injected metadata provider or explicitly gated platform case rather than elevated mutation.

## Steps to Reproduce

Seed a marker or unit file and inject a failure between two current CLI operations. Existing ad hoc fixtures cannot consistently prove the precise phase, retained bytes, directory-sync outcome, systemctl invocation order, later retry, and user-visible output in one trace.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. Self-tests must prove failure injection occurs at the named boundary, successful cases clean up, failing cases retain sanitized evidence, and no scenario reads or changes the user's real sessions, configuration, runtime lock, or systemd state.
design: Expose fault-injectable adapters for filesystem durability, session scans, operation-lock acquisition, marker phases, and systemctl calls, plus PATH fakes for full CLI coverage. A case manifest seeds only isolated paths and specifies exact failure boundaries (write, sync, rename, permission/metadata check, command spawn/reply). Readiness pipes coordinate multiple CLI processes without timing guesses. Capture ordered operation events and before/after path metadata/digests, never file contents. Model retries and crash-seeded states explicitly; real ownership/systemd behavior is optional platform coverage, while injected deterministic contracts remain the CI oracle.
acceptance_criteria: Provide reusable isolated fixtures for session files, permissions/types/ownership where safely testable, operation-lock contention with readiness signaling, atomic-write crash points, migration/rotation journals, replacement marker phases, fake systemctl query/enable/disable failures, and generated-unit execution under a stripped manager environment. Record ordered filesystem/systemd events and before/after manifests without file contents or secrets. Assert durability boundaries, preserved backups/sources, exact exit and output channels, retry/idempotence, and zero contact with the real user manager. Run under cargo test --locked and CI without timing sleeps.
close_reason: Implemented the storage/locking/systemd fault fixture layer: tests/support/systemd_fixture.rs (fake systemctl with ordered argv-array log, scripted is-active/is-enabled state answers, per-subcommand failure scripting, legacy-unit seeding, private-file checks), Case::spawn_run/wait_run/RunHandle (bounded multi-process CLI execution with kill-and-reap on timeout and Drop), Case::remove_file, and a request gate in the fake-Hyprland responder that holds a CLI mid-operation while a gate file exists. Proven by tests/storage_systemd_fixture.rs (5 tests): autosave --install writes both units under the isolated config root and never contacts the manager; autosave status reports unconfigured / installed-but-inactive / active states purely from fake systemctl exit codes; a scripted disable failure during uninstall is recorded in order ([disable, disable]) and surfaced as a warning while uninstall still exits 0 (deterministic evidence for gqg.5); operation-lock contention is choreographed causally (process B provably cannot finish while the gate holds A - an impossibility, not a timing observation) and both processes complete with consistent store visibility after release; crash-seeded atomic-write orphans are expressible as private 0600 temp-grammar files with listing still succeeding. Successful cases clean up; failing cases retain sanitized evidence via the existing Case guard; no scenario touches the user's real sessions, config, runtime lock, or systemd state. Marker phases and migration/rotation journal seeding build on write_file/save_session and are exercised per implementation Bead; generated-unit execution under a stripped manager remains optional platform coverage per the design. Gate: fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --locked (309 tests), htF sync check all pass.

title: Autosave service loses installer XDG paths under the user-manager environment
description:
The service-content generator emits an autosave command whose storage and configuration paths are resolved from the service process environment. A systemd user service inherits the user manager's environment, not necessarily the interactive installer shell's XDG overrides, so a successfully installed timer can read a different config and write a different session store.

This is separate from the sibling installation-path defect: even when the unit files are placed in a directory systemd searches, the service execution context can still diverge.

## Steps to Reproduce

Install from a shell with explicit nondefault XDG data/config paths while a fake user manager has a stripped environment. Execute the generated service command in that manager environment and observe it resolving default paths rather than the paths used by interactive commands.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. The fix must preserve the established timer command, hardening, default-path behavior, and user-manager isolation while carrying only the minimum approved path state.
design: Resolve and validate the minimal path environment at install time, then serialize explicitly set absolute XDG data/config/state values with systemd's Environment= escaping into the service unit. Unset variables remain unset so standard defaults continue to resolve normally. Reject unrepresentable or nonabsolute explicit overrides before changing unit files; never persist XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, PATH, HOME substitutes, or unrelated environment. Keep unit location, unit transaction, and service execution-environment concerns separate but share a typed path/escaping helper.
acceptance_criteria: Persist only explicitly set, validated absolute XDG_DATA_HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, and XDG_STATE_HOME values needed by the generated service, using systemd-safe Environment= serialization; never copy the ambient environment or bake XDG_RUNTIME_DIR. Preserve default-path behavior when variables are unset. Unit-test exact generated bytes for unset/set paths, spaces, percent signs, quotes/backslashes, nonabsolute and invalid values. Actual-CLI e2e installs with fake systemctl, then executes the generated service command under a stripped manager environment and proves capture/config/session paths match the installer context. Assert exact stdout, stderr, exit codes, unit argv/bytes, path state, and ordered redacted JSONL; prove existing default installations remain compatible.

title: Decide the empty-workspace topology restore contract
description:
The current model guarantees restoration of saved windows and their placement, but it does not persist independent empty-workspace topology. Adding it is a potentially useful feature; automatically binding or moving empty workspaces can also move live extras, change focus, and alter an additive-restore guarantee. The repository does not currently supply the policy needed to choose among those outcomes.

This decision Bead owns the normative choice, not implementation. The linked feature must remain blocked until the choice is explicit.

## Steps to Reproduce

Capture a desktop containing an empty focused named or special workspace, then restore with changed monitor availability or a live conflicting workspace binding. The current session has no topology record, and several plausible implementations produce materially different effects on unrelated current state.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. The decision record must enumerate affected users/state, alternatives, compatibility, safeguards, and a plausible reviser; it must leave no implementation-critical boundary implicit.
design: Treat this as a decision gate. Present the current no-topology behavior and at least three serious alternatives: preserve it; capture topology but apply only when no live conflict exists; or define mode-specific topology authority. For each, enumerate effects on extra windows, workspace bindings, focus/cursor, missing monitors, named/special workspaces, legacy sessions, dry-run/reporting, and replacement recovery. Record only the maintainer's explicit objective/rationale. If the guarantee changes, update the owning routed current-state Canon page and create a validation matrix before unblocking implementation; do not infer policy from code or tests.
acceptance_criteria: Obtain an explicit maintainer decision for normal restore, reconciliation, and replacement: whether empty named/special workspaces are captured or recreated; precedence when live workspace bindings or extra windows conflict; missing-monitor behavior; focus/cursor guarantees; failure/report/exit behavior; and legacy-session defaults. Record supplied rationale only, update the smallest routed Canon current-state page and any user-facing compatibility contract if the guarantee changes, and give the implementation Bead a complete test oracle. Do not authorize moving unrelated current windows or silently invent policy.

title: Case-only duplicate app keys make launch configuration nondeterministic
description:
Configuration accepts app keys that differ only by ASCII case. Runtime lookup first tries exact spellings and then performs an unordered case-insensitive HashMap scan, so a compositor class with a third spelling can receive either policy.

Root cause: the accepted namespace is case-sensitive while fallback resolution is case-insensitive and unordered. The ambiguity can select different binaries, capture settings, profile mappings, or default workspaces across runs.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure distinct entries for apps.Foo and apps.foo.
2. Observe a client whose class is FOO, matching neither key exactly.
3. Load the config on repeated processes. HashMap iteration chooses an eligible policy without a deterministic ownership rule.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. Ambiguous app-key namespaces must be rejected before any config-dependent effect; a single case-insensitive fallback remains compatible and deterministic.
design: Build a deterministic ASCII-case-folded app-key index during structural validation. Reject every folded key with more than one original spelling and report the conflicting names in sorted order before app_config_for can run. Feed this error through the typed invalid-config outcome owned by gqg.13 so no command substitutes defaults after detecting the ambiguity.
acceptance_criteria: Reject case-fold collisions deterministically while preserving exact-key and unique mixed-case fallback behavior. Unit tests must cover every insertion order, two- and three-way collisions, exact matches, initial-class fallback, unrelated keys, and non-ASCII behavior under the documented ASCII fold. Actual CLI e2e must use .36.1 with isolated config and the real binary; seed colliding binary/capture/profile policies and assert exit 1 before launch, dispatch, capture, marker, or rotation, empty stdout on fatal failure, sorted path-specific stderr, unchanged files/state, and ordered redacted JSONL. Include valid legacy config and omitted optional fields, no sleeps/live desktop, and second-run deterministic refusal. The fix is not complete until gqg.13 prevents invalid-config fallback.
close_reason: Fixed: validate_config_structure now builds an ASCII-case-folded index of app keys and rejects any fold with more than one original spelling, reporting the conflicting names in sorted order (e.g. 'Foo', 'foo'); the error flows through the gqg.13 typed invalid-config outcome so mutating commands refuse with exit 1, empty stdout, and the named conflict on stderr before any launch, dispatch, capture, marker, or rotation. app_config_for's fallback is rewritten as exact-class, exact-initial-class, then deterministic unique-fold lookups (validation guarantees at most one spelling per fold, so HashMap iteration order can no longer choose a policy). Evidence: unit tests for two- and three-way sorted collisions, unique and non-ASCII keys staying valid, deterministic fallback across casings; CLI e2e through the isolated fixture asserts the refusal names 'Foo'/'foo' sorted with exit 1 and empty stdout, an unchanged store manifest, identical refusal on second run, and successful operation after correcting the namespace. Gate: fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --locked (329 tests), htF sync check all pass. Canon impact: none.

title: Autosave uninstall reports success when systemd timer disable fails
description:
Autosave uninstall calls a disable helper that discards spawn failures and reduces nonzero systemctl results to warnings, then deletes current and legacy unit files and returns success.

Root cause: a required external state transition is best-effort while the enclosing destructive operation unconditionally commits file deletion. A loaded timer can remain active after its definition is removed, while the CLI prints that autosave was removed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install current or legacy autosave units.
2. Make systemctl unavailable or make disable --now return nonzero.
3. Run autosave --uninstall.
4. Observe unit-file deletion and success despite an unconfirmed live timer state.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. Required timer disable/stop must be confirmed before unit removal, and every uncertainty must produce a usable nonzero refusal with files retained.
design: Inject a typed systemctl command runner returning spawn failure, exit status, and bounded stderr. Uninstall must successfully disable and stop both current and legacy timers before removing any unit. On any uncertain or failed transition, retain every unit file, return a stage-and-unit error, suppress success output, and allow an idempotent retry.
acceptance_criteria: Propagate every required disable/stop failure and remove no units until all required timer transitions are confirmed. Deterministic unit and fault tests must cover command spawn failure, nonzero status with empty and nonempty stderr, current/legacy ordering, one timer already disabled, failure on the second timer, unsafe/non-regular unit paths, retry, and complete success. Actual CLI e2e must use .36.4 with fake systemctl and isolated unit directories, invoke the real binary, and assert exact normalized systemctl argv/order, ordered redacted JSONL, unit bytes and modes before/after, retained files on failure, exit 0/1, no success text on failure, stdout/stderr separation, bounded sanitized diagnostics, and zero real user-manager contact. Include legacy/current compatibility and second-run idempotence; use readiness state, not sleeps or live systemd.
close_reason: Fixed: uninstall now requires confirmed disable/stop of every installed timer (current and legacy) before any unit file is removed. Added a typed SystemctlRunner seam (spawn failure, exit status, bounded stderr) with RealSystemctl; uninstall_with refuses with a stage-and-unit error naming the timer and retaining ALL unit files when a required disable fails; the removal phase only runs after confirmed transitions, so success output is suppressed on failure and retries are idempotent. Required disables are scoped to timers whose unit file exists locally, so absent timers (which cannot stay loaded after removal) do not block legacy-only or partial uninstalls. Unit tests (autosave.rs): current-timer failure, second-timer failure, exact disable order before deletion, retry idempotence, no-op without units, non-regular unit refusal with disables confirmed first, converted removal test to the injected runner. CLI e2e via the .36.4 fake systemctl: refusal exits 1 with no success text, names the timer, retains current and legacy units, attempts exactly the first required disable, and an idempotent retry succeeds ('Autosave timer removed.', disables confirmed in order for both timers, all units removed). Gate: fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --locked (315 tests), htF sync check all pass.

title: Legacy autosave migration can silently erase an enabled schedule
description:
Legacy autosave migration collapses a disabled timer and a failed state query into the same false value, then disables and removes legacy units before proving the replacement schedule. Enable and disable errors do not reach the install transaction boundary.

Root cause: migration lacks a typed external-state result and destroys the old schedule before the required replacement state is durable and verified. An enabled legacy timer can be lost while install reports success.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Begin with an enabled legacy HyprFlow autosave timer.
2. Make systemctl state query, replacement enable, or legacy disable fail.
3. Run autosave --install.
4. Observe legacy-file removal or success without proof that the Hyprloom timer preserves the enabled schedule.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. Migration must distinguish disabled from unknown, preserve the prior enabled state, and retain a recoverable legacy schedule on every failed transition.
design: Represent legacy timer state as Enabled, Disabled, or QueryError through the same typed systemctl runner as gqg.5. Establish and verify the replacement timer state required by the legacy state before disabling or removing legacy units. Propagate every error through install, retain legacy units on uncertainty, and make partial transitions idempotently retryable without silently losing the working schedule.
acceptance_criteria: Preserve the enabled or disabled legacy schedule across migration and propagate every query/enable/disable failure. Deterministic unit and fault tests must cover enabled, disabled, query spawn and nonzero failures, replacement enable failure, legacy disable failure, already-migrated units, partial prior state, rollback/retry, unsafe paths, and successful cleanup. Actual CLI e2e must use .36.4 fake systemctl and storage fixtures with the real binary; assert exact query/enable/disable argv and ordering, ordered redacted JSONL, exact unit files/modes and enabled-state model, retained legacy recovery path on failure, exit status, stdout/stderr separation, no false Created message, and zero real manager access. Include old unit compatibility, no sleeps, and second-run convergence without duplicate activation.
close_reason: Fixed: legacy autosave migration now runs on the typed SystemctlRunner (gqg.5 seam, extended with the exit code) and classifies the legacy timer state as Enabled/Disabled/QueryError by systemctl exit code (spawn failure and unexpected statuses are query errors, never silently 'disabled'). Migration order is establish-and-verify: an enabled legacy schedule first enables the Hyprloom timer and verifies it via is-enabled before the legacy timer is disabled and its units removed; every query, enable, verify, disable, or removal failure propagates through install as a stage-and-unit error naming the retained legacy recovery path, so install can no longer report success (or a false 'Created' message) after losing a working schedule. The obsolete warn-only disable_timer helper is removed. Evidence: 6 new unit tests (enabled migration call order query/enable/verify/disable; disabled migration never enables the replacement; query error with exit 2 refuses and retains legacy units with no further transitions; enable failure retains the legacy schedule with no disable; legacy disable failure retains the units; absent legacy is a no-op with zero calls) and 2 CLI e2e tests through the .36.4 fake systemctl (enabled schedule preserved with exact query/enable/verify/disable argv order and legacy removal; enable failure refuses with exit 1, no Created message, named error, legacy units retained, and no disable issued). Disabled, already-migrated, unsafe-path, and retry controls covered by unit tests. Gate: fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --locked (333 tests), htF sync check all pass. Canon impact: none - autosave-lifecycle already normatively requires preserving whether the legacy timer was enabled; migration now conforms.

title: Monitor-scale omission mixes physical and logical geometry during restore
description:
Hyprland monitor mode width and height are physical pixels, while monitor origins and client geometry are compositor logical coordinates. The captured and live monitor models omit scale, and placement combines these quantities directly.

Root cause: geometry adaptation lacks the unit conversion needed to compare saved and current monitor extents. Equal scales can mask the error, but scale or scale-plus-transform changes deterministically produce wrong sizes, positions, and clamps.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Save a window on a 3840 by 2160 monitor at scale 1.
2. Restore against the same mode at scale 2.
3. The logical monitor extent halves, but the current ratio remains one because scale is absent.
4. Hyprloom emits or accepts geometry twice the intended logical size or offset.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. New snapshots must carry scale compatibly, all geometry math must use logical units, and old unknown-scale snapshots must degrade conservatively rather than silently asserting a wrong conversion.
design: Capture an optional finite positive monitor scale in both Hyprctl and session monitor models. Convert saved and current mode dimensions into one logical-coordinate representation before ratio, transform, bounds, and clamp calculations. Old snapshots with unknown saved scale must not claim proportional adaptation: preserve captured logical coordinates conservatively and clamp only to known current logical bounds, while reporting that relative scaling was unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: Use consistent logical units throughout geometry adaptation and preserve backward-compatible deserialization. Deterministic unit/property tests must cover scale 1 to 2 and 2 to 1, equal and changed modes, mixed mode-plus-scale, rotations and flips as supported by their owners, origins, edge clamps, zero/negative/nonfinite scale input, absent legacy scale, overflow bounds, and exact unchanged round trips. Actual CLI e2e must use .36.2 with saved/current monitor JSON and the real binary; assert exact dispatch argv/order, final fake-compositor geometry, report status and exit truth, JSON-only stdout under --report-json, human diagnostics on stderr, ordered redacted JSONL, no mutation in dry-run/unknown-monitor cases, and second-run unchanged convergence. No sleeps or live compositor.

title: Terminal last-command capture selects old background jobs by PID
description:
When last-command capture is enabled, terminal hint selection walks all descendants of the selected shell, filters helpers and plain shells, and chooses the minimum PID.

Root cause: process age is treated as foreground ownership. A common long-lived background job can be older than many later foreground commands, so the saved and displayed hint is deterministically wrong even though it is not executed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a long-lived background job from a supported terminal shell.
2. Start a newer foreground command in the same shell.
3. Save with capture_last_command enabled.
4. The minimum-PID rule records the background job as the current or last foreground command.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. Only positive foreground-process evidence may produce a hint; ambiguity or missing evidence must safely omit it without changing unrelated terminal capture features.
design: Extend process evidence with session ID, controlling TTY, process group, and foreground process group. A last-command hint may come only from a unique descendant in the selected shell foreground process group and matching terminal session. Missing, inconsistent, or ambiguous foreground evidence omits the hint. PID order is never a foreground proxy.
acceptance_criteria: Capture only a positively identified foreground command and preserve omission on ambiguity. Deterministic unit/property tests must cover older background plus newer foreground jobs, pipelines and one process group, nested descendants, multiplexers, stopped jobs, multiple shells, no controlling TTY, unavailable proc fields, PID reuse, helper filtering, persistence, and template rendering. Actual CLI e2e must use .36.3 controlled TTY/process helpers and the real binary; coordinate through readiness pipes/state files, capture a synthetic background and foreground topology, and assert exact selected session field or omission, no unrelated argv, exact exit and stdout/stderr, ordered redacted JSONL with synthetic identities, no host PID assumptions, no sleeps, and a capture-save-restore round trip preserving existing CWD behavior.

title: Quick-exiting or daemonizing launchers lose post-launch correlation
description:
Launch correlation records only the immediate child PID and start time, waits before observing clients, and later requires that root to remain readable before traversing descendants. Wrappers, daemonizing launchers, and single-instance clients can transfer work and exit before the first observation.

Root cause: the initially spawned process is treated as a durable ancestry root even when supported launch contracts legitimately outlive it. The intended window opens but cannot be proven, so Hyprloom times out or leaves it unpositioned. Accepting class alone would be unsafe and is not part of the fix.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure an authorized wrapper that forks the GUI process and exits immediately, or invoke a supported single-instance client that hands work to an existing server.
2. Let the intended window appear before or after the first 100 ms interval.
3. The original PID has disappeared, so descendant correlation cannot run.
4. Restore reports failure or launches again despite the intended window being present.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. Correlation must retain positive causal evidence across parent exit and remain fail-closed when no such evidence survives.
design: Model launch correlation as an evidence-bearing ticket rather than a durable immediate-child PID. Poll without an initial blind delay, retain PID/start identities of descendants observed while ancestry is provable, and correlate only those identities after the root exits. Requests handed to a pre-existing single-instance process require an explicit app-specific positive handoff adapter using a pre-launch baseline and unique new window evidence; generic class or fresh address alone remains insufficient.
acceptance_criteria: Safely correlate supported immediate-exit, daemonizing, and explicitly adapted single-instance launchers without weakening ambiguity refusal. Deterministic unit/property/fault tests must cover direct exec, immediate exit, double fork, descendant evidence captured then reparented, root PID reuse, process-evidence loss, delayed mapping, existing server handoff, supported browser adapters, Google Chrome classification where supported, an adversarial same-class sibling, multiple new candidates, timeout, retry, and one-to-one reservation. Actual CLI e2e must use .36.2 and .36.3 with controlled launch helpers, readiness signals, and stateful fake clients; assert exact spawned argv, lifecycle and compositor request order, one correlated address, exact placement/final state, no unrelated mutation or duplicate launch, report JSON and exit status, human stderr, ordered redacted JSONL, no sleeps/live desktop, and second-run idempotence.

title: profile_workspaces config keys matched case-sensitively while the rest of the pipeline is case-insensitive
description:
Root cause: filter_profiles_by_config (src/brave.rs:77-85) does an exact HashMap key lookup contains_key(&p.directory), while every other profile comparison in the pipeline is case-insensitive (brave.rs:99 eq_ignore_ascii_case; process.rs:386 lowercased dedupe; restore.rs:3746; config.rs:103-110 app_config_for is deliberately case-tolerant).
Failure: user writes profile_workspaces = { "default" = 1 } (name as seen lowercased elsewhere); Local State directory is "Default"; contains_key("default") -> false -> that profile silently absent from the captured session, while the identical name passes the active-directories branch. Inconsistent case policy causes silent capture data loss.
Fix: compare mappings case-insensitively (lowercased key set or iter().any(eq_ignore_ascii_case)).
