title: Partial replacement recovery has no user-authorized terminal resolution
description:
A conservative additive safety-recovery pass can return skipped or failed outcomes and leave the replacement marker active. Every later mutating command reruns recovery before command dispatch, but the CLI exposes no durable user-authorized way to accept the current desktop while preserving the safety snapshot.

Root cause: retryable recovery and explicit abandonment are represented by the same active marker state. The existing proposal to classify an ambiguous skip as automatically terminal is unsafe because current desktop identity evidence can later change.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Leave an InProgress replacement whose safety target conflicts with an indistinguishable current same-class window.
2. Run a mutating command. Conservative recovery skips the target and retains the marker.
3. Repeat the command. Recovery reruns and the requested operation remains gated.
4. Observe that recover offers only another automatic pass; safe resolution otherwise requires manual marker manipulation.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. Automatic recovery must remain fail-closed, while an explicit user action can preserve the backup, record acceptance of current state, clear recovery, and unblock later mutation atomically.
design: Keep automatic recovery conservative and add explicit recovery primitives: status, retry, and accept-current with a required preserve-backup-as session name. Acceptance must atomically copy or rename the safety snapshot out of autosave rotation before clearing the active marker. Any backup promotion or marker-clear failure leaves the original marker and backup intact. Automatic startup never treats an ambiguous skip as terminal because desktop evidence can later change.
acceptance_criteria: Provide a usable explicit disposition without auto-finalizing ambiguity. Deterministic unit/state-machine/fault tests must cover retryable partial reports, unchanged ambiguity, later-resolved evidence, backup-name validation and collision, promotion write/sync failure, marker-clear failure, rotation protection, repeated status/retry, and legacy marker phases. Actual CLI e2e must use .36.2 and .36.4 with the real binary to seed ambiguous InProgress recovery, invoke two blocked mutating commands, status, retry, and explicit accept-current; assert exact clients and zero unintended dispatch, marker phase, source and promoted backup bytes/modes, rotation set, exit codes, human stdout/stderr, JSON-only stdout if structured status is added, and ordered redacted JSONL. After successful explicit resolution the next mutating command must proceed; failures must remain idempotently recoverable. No sleeps, live desktop, or secret snapshot contents in logs.

title: Safety recovery treats class+title-only match as strong identity and can grab an unrelated new window
description:
Root cause: safety recovery's fail-closed gate allowed_match_with_policy (restore.rs:919, allow_ambiguous_identity=false) rejects only ClassFallback/ambiguous-title edges, but add_application_identity_score (restore.rs:644-646) PROMOTES MatchKind to ExactIdentity on any exact title match even with zero window/process evidence, and the ExactIdentity doc means 'stable window identity matched exactly' (368-369). Addressless targets also skip the cross-address relaunch-proof gate (560-572). The codebase itself states 'a matching title/class is not ownership proof' (restore.rs:926-930) — the recovery loop does not enforce that.
Failure: interrupted replacement with pre-address-era backup recovered at login; backup's addressless target has title 'Project'; user meanwhile opened a NEW same-class window with identical title -> passes as 'exact identity' -> recovery yanks the user's unrelated window to the backup's workspace/geometry and labels the pairing matched-exact. Violates session-operations + identity-and-launch canon ('must not move an unrelated same-class window', 'uncertainty must not be resolved by targeting an arbitrary window'). Safe-recovery tests all give targets addresses, so the hole is untested.
Fix: under !allow_ambiguous_identity require an actual identity element (saved-address parity, stable-id pair, profile, or cwd); do not promote kind to ExactIdentity on class+title agreement alone.
close_reason: Duplicate of hyprloom-production-bug-audit-2026-08-30-gqg.12 — same root cause: title-equality promotion to ExactIdentity bypasses ownership proof

title: Replace loses its completed structured report when final marker persistence fails
description:
Replacement computes a complete ReconcileReport after close and restore. If durable Finalizing marker persistence then fails, the error variant carries only text, so the report is discarded and report-json produces empty stdout despite known window outcomes.

Root cause: post-mutation transaction status and reconciliation outcome share an error boundary that cannot transport both values. Automation cannot distinguish which windows changed even though Hyprloom computed the result.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run replace --report-json and allow reconciliation to complete successfully.
2. Inject a failure writing or syncing the Finalizing marker.
3. The restore layer returns TransactionAfterRestore without the report.
4. Main exits nonzero with diagnostics but emits no structured window outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. Every post-restore failure must retain and emit the already-known report exactly once while preserving nonzero exit and a separate finalization error.
design: Change the post-restore error variant to carry the completed ReconcileReport and the separate finalization source. Main must serialize the report exactly once before nonzero exit when report-json is requested, keep diagnostics on stderr, and expose finalization status as an additive stable code rather than raw path or OS text. Do not replay safety recovery after a completed target merely because final marker persistence failed.
acceptance_criteria: Preserve every known window outcome across post-restore transaction failure and keep cleanup truth separate. Unit and serialization tests must cover a successful report followed by finalizing marker read/write/rename/sync failure, JSON writer failure, human mode, and the already-existing partial-report and later marker-clear paths. Do not require impossible Finalizing failures after skipped or failed reconciliation because Finalizing is attempted only for a complete report. Fault tests must prove target state and backup/marker bytes remain diagnosable. Actual CLI e2e must use .36.2 and .36.4 to inject a deterministic final marker failure after placement; assert exact fake desktop state, one versioned JSON document on stdout, all window statuses/counts, nonzero exit, finalization code and actionable stderr, no duplicate JSON/human text, no safety replay, ordered redacted JSONL, and retry/second-run marker behavior. Use no sleeps or live desktop.

title: Marker-backed replace silently skips closing stable-ID-less windows yet commits success and rotates away the safety backup
description:
Root cause: observed_window_identity_matches (restore.rs:1919-1924) returns false on the (None,None)-stable-ID arm before PID/start-time logic when has_reliable_process_start_time() is true (always in production), and safety_snapshot_identity_matches hard-fails missing stable IDs (1955-1960). In the marker-backed close loop such windows hit protected_addresses.insert + continue (2285-2294) — never closed; the non-marker path correctly returns Err(WindowIdentityChanged) (2295), proving divergence is not intended. Commit predicate counts only failed/skipped, so report is 0/0: marker -> Finalizing (2392-2396), main clears marker + ROTATES THE BACKUP (main.rs:440), prints success, exit 0.
Failure: hyprloom replace X on any desktop with stableId-less clients (XWayland/electron — repo's OWN fixture has brave-browser+obsidian without stableId): old windows survive as extras, safety backup may be pruned, exit 0 claims replaced desktop. Unit tests inject EmptyProcessInfo (reliable=false), routing around the failing arm. Violates session-operations canon ("replacement closes the current Hyprland clients").
Fix: track baseline-snapshot windows retained for unprovable identity separately; if any remain, keep marker+backup and exit nonzero as incomplete; gate the (None,None) veto to actual multi-window-same-PID ambiguity (identity_is_ambiguous_without_stable_id, 1888-1896).
close_reason: Rejected after production-entry reachability review: main captures the safety snapshot and validate_safety_snapshot_with_config rejects every client with a missing or empty stable ID before saving the backup, writing a replacement marker, or dispatching any close. The cited marker-backed protection branch is therefore unreachable from the supported CLI. Reopen only if a supported production entry point bypasses that preflight.

title: Replace human summary omits skipped count and claims success while exit status and JSON say incomplete
description:
Root cause: replace human summary (main.rs:410-419) has no {skipped} field (reconcile's summary at 292-300 does), while the exit gate at main.rs:424 treats failed>0 || skipped>0 as incomplete.
Failure: any replace pass ending with skipped>=1, failed==0 prints "Replaced desktop with 'X' (..., 0 failed)." — no mention of skips — followed by stderr "Replacement was incomplete; attempting safety recovery...", exit 1. Human output says success, JSON truthfully says "skipped": N: the two classifications of the same run contradict each other (canon invariant 7: outcomes must distinguish safe skips regardless of verbosity). Trigger likely via browser session-restore reopening two same-class windows mid-pass (has_ambiguous_reopened_webapp skip, restore.rs:2930-2941).
Fix: add {skipped} to the replace summary and word the first line conditionally when failed||skipped>0.
close_reason: Rejected as presentation-only: every skip detail is printed, the following message states replacement was incomplete, recovery is attempted, and exit status is nonzero. Omitting the aggregate count does not conceal success state.

title: Reconciliation repeatedly re-enriches every client process tree for every target
description:
Observation
- Reconciliation performs a full enriched observation at src/restore.rs:2731 and again before every non-dry-run target at src/restore.rs:2803-2812; target zero repeats the initial observation before any mutation.
- Each observation walks terminal descendants, reads process state, and performs Brave profile discovery for every current client at src/restore.rs:3402-3460.
- The supported ceiling is 512 targets and 512 current windows.

Root cause
Correct compositor freshness and expensive process enrichment are fused into one operation. The per-target identity refresh therefore repeats process-tree work for all unrelated clients, producing O(targets * clients * process-tree) reads in an ordinary reconciliation.

Production impact
Launch-heavy desktops, especially browsers with large child trees, repeat thousands of /proc reads and full profile searches while restoring sequential targets. This can add user-visible seconds and increases race exposure. gqg.3 owns a separate duplicate same-PID Brave traversal inside one observation.

Constraint
CWD, descendants, and profile evidence can change for a live process, so blanket caching by PID/start-time would be unsound. Per-close client queries are also deliberate identity revalidation and are outside this finding.
acceptance_criteria: Separate cheap compositor refresh from selective process enrichment while preserving the freshness and identity guarantees. Avoid the provably redundant target-zero enrichment and reuse only evidence with an explicit validity rule; re-enrich candidates whose changing process evidence can affect a decision. Add call-count or benchmark coverage that demonstrates sub-quadratic enrichment on many unrelated clients and correctness tests for a terminal or browser whose evidence changes between targets.
close_reason: Duplicate of hyprloom-production-bug-audit-2026-08-30-gqg.3 — same root cause: redundant re-enrichment per iteration

title: Rotated-monitor geometry conversion is not invertible on non-square monitors
description:
The quarter-turn canonicalization formulas use different axis extents in the forward and inverse operations. On a non-square monitor, transform 1 round-trips x by an added height-minus-width offset and transform 3 similarly shifts y.

Root cause: the pre-rotation extent of the wrong axis is used, so the two formulas are not inverses except on square displays. Geometry adaptation therefore moves or clamps windows even when monitor metadata is unchanged.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Save an in-bounds rectangle on a 1920 by 1080 monitor with transform 1 or 3.
2. Restore against identical monitor metadata.
3. Run the current canonical transform and inverse.
4. The coordinate shifts by the difference between monitor extents and may clamp to an edge.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. Unchanged non-square transforms 0 through 3 must round-trip exactly before clamp; changed transforms must follow one documented coordinate convention.
design: Define one canonical rectangle transform for Wayland transforms 0 through 3 and derive or directly verify its inverse instead of maintaining independent axis formulas. Use checked extents in the pre-rotation coordinate system and apply origin translation, transform, scaling, inverse transform, and clamp in an explicit order. Flipped transforms remain owned by gqg.26 and scale units by gqg.7.
acceptance_criteria: Make transforms 0 through 3 algebraic inverses on non-square monitors and preserve unchanged geometry before clamping. Deterministic unit/property tests must exhaust small rectangular extents, every in-bounds position and size, varied global origins, edge-touching rectangles, transform pairs, rounding, saturation, and invalid zero extents; include 1920x1080 and 1080x1920 regressions and prove no scope drift into transforms 4 through 7. Actual CLI e2e must use .36.2 with transformed saved/current monitor fixtures and the real binary; assert exact request order, zero dispatch and Unchanged report for unchanged metadata, correct final geometry when rotation changes, JSON-only stdout, exit status, ordered redacted JSONL, dry-run nonmutation, and second-run convergence. No sleeps/live compositor.

title: Complete launch specification is authorized only by mutable session fields
description:
Session structure validation bounds launch strings but launch trust compares the executable with class and initial-class values from the same mutable JSON record. Identity-derived commands may contain relative or absolute paths, and generic argv is appended without independent provenance. Capture can persist a self-reported path-like class as its command.

Root cause: no independent boundary authorizes the complete launch specification. Matching mutable fields in one record does not prove that an executable path or exec-capable argument shape came from a supported capture/config source.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a client that self-reports /tmp/evil as its class and capture the session, or edit a private session so class and launch command agree on that path.
2. Alternatively make class and command Kitty and add exec-capable argv.
3. Restore or run replacement preflight.
4. The same-record equality passes and the resolved executable plus unvalidated argv can be spawned automatically.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. One fail-closed validator must cover executable and argv provenance, preserve supported structured launch features and safe legacy sessions, and prevent every unproven launch before any desktop or recovery-state mutation.
design: Create one validator over executable plus argv with independently recomputed provenance. Identity-derived executables must be safe basenames matching a normalized app identity and may use only empty argv or a known structured adapter. Configured paths must exactly match the current apps entry. Brave, Ghostty, validated webapps, terminal CWD, and terminal hint adapters each validate their complete command shape. Safe basename and empty-argv legacy sessions remain compatible; unsupported legacy argv fails closed with an actionable migration diagnostic.
acceptance_criteria: Authorize the complete launch specification before dry-run success, spawn, replacement backup/marker mutation, or close. Unit/property tests must cover absolute and relative paths, separators and traversal, safe basenames, class/initial-class case, explicit configured paths, executable modes, empty and exec-capable argv, Kitty/Ghostty/Brave/CWD/hint adapters, validated and adversarial webapps, field-code/action desktop entries, legacy records, binary disappearance, and bounded strings. Fault tests must prove zero ProcessLauncher calls and zero desktop/storage effects on rejection. Actual CLI e2e must use .36.3 controlled executables and the real binary to exercise a captured path-like class and hand-edited Kitty -e record; assert exact session input identity, no malicious sentinel execution, no spawn/dispatch/marker, exit 1, empty stdout on fatal failure or one JSON report where contractually available, sanitized stderr without argv/user content, ordered redacted JSONL, valid configured/legacy feature preservation, dry-run parity, and second-run deterministic refusal. No sleeps or live desktop.

title: Session launch args bypass authorization: trusted binaries get exec-style flags (-e, --load-extension) from the file
description:
Root cause: trust validation checks only argv[0] (restore.rs:3887-3916); build_launch_command appends session args verbatim (restore.rs:3855). The webapp branch proves the intended contract — it validates the COMPLETE argv "before allowing a saved session to run them automatically" (restore.rs:3904-3911, 3961-4001) — but no other class gets argv validation.
Failure: {"class":"kitty","launch":{"command":"kitty","args":["-e","/tmp/evil"]}} -> restore spawns kitty -e /tmp/evil (exec semantics — restore itself relies on this at 3857-3866); Chromium/Brave --load-extension=/tmp/x gives arbitrary code inside the trusted browser; ghostty --initial-command. Verified in sandbox. Capture side worsens it: desktop Exec= trailing tokens (field codes %u unstripped, and [Desktop Action] group Exec lines kept — parse ignores sections, capture.rs:407-421,469-473) become stored args the user never ran.
Fix: extend webapp-style full-argv validation to every trusted class (deny exec-capable flags, or allow only flag shapes capture legitimately produces); restrict desktop parsing to [Desktop Entry] and strip field codes.
close_reason: Duplicate of hyprloom-session-file-arbitrary-exec-sk0 after broadening that owner to validate the complete launch specification. Executable and argv authorization derive from the same mutable session record and must be fixed at one boundary. The generic arbitrary-argv claim also requires private-session editing; webapp desktop-entry argv already has a complete validator.

title: Single-instance apps (and google-chrome) can never correlate their own window; restore false-fails despite success
description:
Root cause: correlation accepts only PID-descendant evidence for non-browser targets (gate at restore.rs:3629-3636: !is_browser_target -> continue until timeout), and is_browser_target covers only brave + chromium + chrome-* webapps (1095-1097,1141-1147). Single-instance apps (code, google-chrome, most Electron/IDE launchers) forward to the pre-existing process and exit; the new window is owned by a non-descendant.
Failure: VS Code already running, restore spawns `code <dir>` -> window opens but is uncorrelatable -> target reported FAILED and left unpositioned, exit 1 on an actually-successful launch; every repeat spawns another forwarder (feeds spawn-child-unreaped-stdin). google-chrome sessions are wholly unrestorable (not in any browser-identity class list).
Fix: extend positive handoff evidence to single-instance apps (candidate PID == live instance PID recorded at capture, class+title+stable-id agreement), or special-case known forwarding launchers; add google-chrome/chrome to browser identity handling.
close_reason: Duplicate of hyprloom-production-bug-audit-2026-08-30-gqg.9 — same root cause: forwarder/daemon launchers break PID-descendant correlation

title: Spawned Child dropped without reaping (zombies) and with inherited stdin
description:
Root cause: RealProcessLauncher::spawn (restore.rs:156-171) reads id()/start-time then DROPS the Child; no try_wait/wait anywhere in the crate. stdin is left inherited.
Failure: single-instance forwarders (finding single-instance-apps-uncorrelated) exit within ms -> zombies accumulate (20 Brave/webapp targets -> ~20 zombie rows for the run's duration); a configured forwarding CLI child can read the user's terminal keystrokes after hyprloom returns to the prompt. Impact bounded/low but real on every launch-heavy pass.
Fix: retain Child handles and opportunistically try_wait() per poll tick; set .stdin(Stdio::null()).
close_reason: Rejected as non-material in the ordinary path: dropped children create only run-bounded zombies, and normal shell job control prevents an old process group from reading prompt input. Material impact requires a specially configured launcher or unusually long run.

title: start-time guard kills the documented identity fallback so stable-id-less compositors misreport launched windows as extras
description:
Root cause: observed_windows_are_same (restore.rs:345-351) returns false whenever EITHER observation has process_start_time set; observe_clients_with_monitors always sets it in production (3420). That vetoes the address+PID+start-time fallback arms at 352-362 (including its Some(x)==Some(x) arm), making them dead code and contradicting the struct's documented 'conservative fallback' (310-314). Test 4439 pins only the stable-ID-loss branch, not this arm.
Failure: on a compositor that omits stable_id, every live window identity comparison fails -> a window launched for target X (recorded consumed at 3087) cannot be recognized in the final pass (3119) -> report simultaneously says '1 launched' and '1 extra left alone' about the SAME window; consumed-filtering at 2828/1715 silently no-ops (harmless only because dispatch separately fails closed when identity is unprovable — see single-instance-apps-uncorrelated).
Fix: make the documented address+PID+start-time comparison reachable when stable IDs are absent on both sides, or delete the dead arms and exclude same-pass-consumed windows from extras by address.
close_reason: Same dead stable-ID-less fallback reviewed and closed under gqg.1. Supported Hyprland 0.54+ supplies stable IDs; no supported-runtime trigger was established for this accounting variant.

title: Crash before the first replacement close leaves an unrecoverable closing marker
description:
Replacement writes a durable Closing marker immediately before its first close dispatch. A crash in that interval, or a synchronously rejected close whose error path cannot prove non-application, leaves the original window visible. Recovery returns unknown forever and exposes no supported resolution.

Root cause: the durable protocol has no negative close outcome and no explicit user-authorized disposition for the unavoidable persisted-before-result interval. A timeout cannot prove that an asynchronous request was never queued.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start replacement and persist the Closing marker for the first identified window.
2. Stop before dispatch, or make the provider reject the close syntax synchronously.
3. Restart a mutating command while the original window remains.
4. Recovery cannot distinguish untouched state from a queued close and retains the marker, blocking mutation repeatedly.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. Proven rejection must unwind safely; uncertain submission must remain conservative but gain an explicit resolution path that preserves the backup.
design: Distinguish an authoritative synchronous close rejection from an unknown post-submit result. When the transport proves the compositor did not accept the close, durably return the marker to Prepared or clear it before reporting failure. IO loss or any possibly queued request remains Closing. Extend the explicit recovery status and accept-current backup-preservation primitive from recovery-terminal-state-lockout to Closing markers, requiring marker identity and target fingerprint confirmation.
acceptance_criteria: Avoid permanent lockout after proven rejection without auto-clearing an ambiguous queued close. Deterministic unit state-machine and fault tests must cover crash before dispatch, authoritative syntax rejection, transport loss before and after submit, queued delayed close, confirmed disappearance, same and reused address, stable/PID/start evidence, compositor unavailability, marker rollback write/sync failure, repeated startup, and explicit resolution with backup preservation. Actual CLI e2e must use .36.2 and .36.4 to inject each close outcome through the real binary; assert exact dispatch argv/order, current clients, marker phase/bytes/mode, safety backup, exit status, human stdout/stderr, optional JSON-only stdout, subsequent command blocking or availability, and ordered redacted JSONL. Include legacy markers and supported provider dialects, no sleeps/live compositor, and second-run idempotence.
notes: Related supported-runtime evidence adds a non-crash trigger: if the first close dispatcher is synchronously rejected before Hyprland queues it (for example, the Lua-provider syntax incompatibility in hyprloom-dispatch-syntax-incompatible-hyprland-056-f4o), replacement still leaves the Closing marker. The error path re-enters replacement_close_started, which cannot return Some(false) while the original window remains, so the same permanent lockout follows even though the dispatch result itself proved that no close was accepted. Keep this as a variant of the same missing durable/explicit negative-resolution state, not a separate issue.

title: systemctl failure indistinguishable from disabled/inactive: migration drops enabled-state, uninstall falsely succeeds
description:
Root cause: unit_state_is (autosave.rs:451-456) returns false both for "disabled/inactive" and for spawn/exec failure; disable_timer (462-464) silently no-ops when systemctl cannot even be spawned (no warning, unlike the ran-and-failed path at 468-472). was_enabled for legacy migration derives from that function (482).
Failure: hyprloom autosave --install with legacy hyprflow-autosave.timer enabled but systemctl --user unreachable (no XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/user bus) -> was_enabled=false -> legacy files removed (484-488), new timer never enabled -> autosave silently stops forever. Same collapse on --uninstall: files removed while the live timer keeps running, yet main.rs:584 prints "Autosave timer removed." exit 0.
Fix: tri-state (enabled/disabled/error); on error abort migration and print the exact systemctl command for the user; treat disable/spawn failure as a reported error.
close_reason: Duplicate of hyprloom-production-bug-audit-2026-08-30-gqg.5 — same root cause split across gqg.5 (uninstall false success) and gqg.6 (migration drops enabled-state)

title: capture_cwd emits Kitty launch flags for configured non-Ghostty terminals
description:
The generic capture_cwd option emits Ghostty working-directory syntax for recognized Ghostty classes and Kitty directory syntax for every other configured application. Other ordinary terminals use different flags or subcommands.

Root cause: a per-application feature is implemented as a two-branch terminal dialect table whose fallback silently means Kitty. Valid Alacritty, foot, or WezTerm configurations therefore persist argv unsupported by the selected binary.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure capture_cwd for Alacritty, foot, WezTerm, or another non-Ghostty terminal.
2. Capture a window with a known shell CWD.
3. Inspect LaunchInfo: every unknown class receives Kitty --directory syntax.
4. Restore; the terminal rejects the option or starts with the wrong invocation shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. CWD restoration must use an explicit validated terminal adapter, preserve argv token boundaries, and fail closed for unknown syntax.
design: Use a closed registry of supported terminal launch adapters keyed by normalized class and resolved configured binary. Each adapter produces structured CWD argv for Kitty, Ghostty, Alacritty, foot, or WezTerm and is validated by the complete launch-spec owner. If capture_cwd is enabled for an unknown adapter, reject configuration or capture with an actionable message; never silently apply Kitty syntax. Do not add a free-form shell template as the default interface.
acceptance_criteria: Generate only terminal-specific validated CWD argv and preserve all existing supported terminal behavior. Unit/property tests must cover Kitty, Ghostty, Alacritty, foot, WezTerm start shape, class aliases and case, configured absolute binary paths, CWD as one argv token including spaces and leading dashes, empty/non-UTF path policy, unknown adapters, capture disabled, legacy Kitty/Ghostty sessions, and interaction with hint metadata. Actual capture-to-session-to-restore CLI e2e must use .36.3 controlled terminal executables and the real binary; assert exact saved argv and spawn argv boundaries, no shell re-tokenization, lifecycle correlation, no spawn/dispatch on unknown adapter, exit and stdout/stderr, ordered redacted JSONL without real CWD contents, dry-run parity, and second-run idempotence. No sleeps/live desktop.

title: Pixel geometry planned for tiled windows: movewindowpixel no-ops, resizewindowpixel drags split ratios, repair never converges
description:
Root cause: placement.rs:305-318 emits resizewindowpixel/movewindowpixel exact and treats at/size mismatch as repair-needed regardless of FLOATING state, but in Hyprland 0.56.2 CAlgorithm::moveTarget (Algorithm.cpp:131-135) no-ops for tiled windows and resizeTarget routes tiled into CDwindle::resizeTarget (DwindleAlgorithm.cpp:310+) adjusting split RATIOS, never exact pixels. The float-first precondition is enforced only when the float STATE differs.
Failure (verified against 0.56.2 source): saved ws with two tiled dwindle windows; user closes one; restore --reconcile matches survivor, plans exact resize+move, reports Moved, both silently no-op (single node has no ratio parent, move ignored tiled) -> next run identical plan -> perpetual churn, never Unchanged; with >=2 siblings each pass applies a fresh ratio delta and shrinks the neighbor every restore. Violates session-operations idempotency canon. Consumers restore.rs:2857-2878, 3691-3696.
Fix: gate the geometry comparison AND the resize/move emission on the planned final floating state: tiled => skip at/size repair, layout owns geometry.
close_reason: Duplicate of hyprloom-production-bug-audit-2026-08-30-gqg.29. Both records own the same root: absolute floating-window geometry commands are treated as authoritative for tiled layouts and dispatch acknowledgement is mistaken for postcondition satisfaction. gqg.29 covers matched repair, launched targets, layout reflow, final verification, and second-run convergence.

title: Partial legacy migration can resurrect a snapshot deleted through the CLI
description:
Legacy migration copies candidates one at a time and writes one completion marker only after the loop. If a later atomic copy fails, earlier destinations remain durable without provenance, while main warns and continues into the requested command.

Root cause: partial import and user deletion are represented by one all-or-nothing completion marker. A session successfully imported before the failure can be deleted through the CLI, then copied again from the retained legacy source on the next startup.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Provide valid legacy sessions A and B.
2. Let A copy successfully and inject an atomic-write failure for B.
3. In the warning-continued invocation, delete migrated A through the supported CLI.
4. Restart. With no completion marker or per-source provenance, migration recopies A and undoes the deletion.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. Durable per-source provenance or an equivalent atomic protocol must prevent recopy after user deletion without suppressing retry of an uncommitted source.
design: Replace the single all-or-nothing completion bit with a private atomic migration journal keyed by source filename and content digest. Record durable Pending before copy, then Imported after the destination and directory are durable; record Shadowed when a destination already owns the name. On restart, reconcile Pending against matching destination content and retry only genuinely uncommitted sources. Imported or Shadowed names are never copied after later destination deletion. Convert to the completion marker only after all candidates are durably classified.
acceptance_criteria: Never resurrect an imported or shadowed legacy snapshot while preserving safe retry for genuinely uncopied sources. Deterministic unit/property/crash tests must inject failure before and after journal write, destination write/rename/sync, Imported update, completion marker, and each later candidate; cover delete after partial import, destination collision, matching and changed digest, malformed/unsafe/oversized source, dangling/non-regular destination, journal corruption/symlink/permissions, retry, and final cleanup. Actual CLI e2e must use .36.4 with the real binary to fail the second copy, run supported delete in the permitted phase, restart, and complete migration; assert exact source/destination/journal/marker manifests and modes, no resurrection or overwrite, exit codes, stdout/stderr, ordered redacted JSONL containing hashes but no file contents, and second-run idempotence. No sleeps or user storage contact.

title: Empty-command Unchanged fast path skips window-liveness revalidation, letting replace commit success over a vanished window
description:
Root cause: the empty-command Unchanged fast path (restore.rs:2853-2878) consumes the window and increments report.unchanged using geometry from the per-target refresh at 2806, with NO revalidation — the address-disappeared guard (dispatch_existing_repairs revalidation, 1851-1865) runs only for non-empty command sets. Enrichment (per-window /proc walks, Brave profile scans; ms-to-tens-of-ms) happens between observation and the decision.
Failure (TOCTOU, medium confidence): hyprloom replace (or reconcile): target T's matched window X is already correctly placed -> commands empty; X is closed during the same iteration's enrichment interval -> reported Unchanged for a dead window; the non-empty path would have counted WindowDisappeared as failed and blocked finalization. With failed==0&&skipped==0 the replace marker finalizes (2393) and the transaction commits success while the restored desktop is silently missing that window.
Fix: run the same address-existence revalidation for the empty-command case (single get_clients, or reuse the post-loop observation at 3114 to downgrade Unchanged->Failed/relaunch).
close_reason: Rejected as mis-scoped timing hardening. A target can disappear after any observed unchanged, moved, or launched outcome; another immediate get_clients call only moves the race and does not make the empty-command path uniquely incorrect. Any defined final-state verification belongs in the shared post-reconciliation contract, with vanished outcomes covered under gqg.29 if that contract is adopted. Reopen only with a deterministic supported trigger unique to this branch.

title: Unknown config keys silently select defaults that can drive destructive autosave rotation
description:
Serde currently accepts unknown fields in the top-level, general, filters, and app configuration objects. A misspelled retention table or key parses successfully, so the intended value is omitted and default retention five becomes operational without warning.

Root cause: forward-compatible unknown data is treated as validated operator intent even when omission authorizes irreversible rotation. This is distinct from gqg.13, which owns present-but-detected-invalid fallback.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Retain more than five autosaves and configure a larger intended retention using a misspelled table or key.
2. Run autosave --now or let the timer invoke it.
3. Parsing succeeds because the unknown field is ignored.
4. The recognized retention remains five and rotation permanently deletes older snapshots without an unknown-key diagnostic.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. Unknown schema fields must be reported with their path and stop every config-dependent destructive effect; omission of documented optional fields and dynamic profile names must remain compatible.
design: Detect unknown fields with a path-aware schema for the top-level config, general, filters, and each app object; profile_workspaces keys remain intentionally dynamic profile identifiers. Feed every schema error into the Absent, Valid, or Invalid config outcome owned by gqg.13. Config-dependent or mutating commands must stop before capture, recovery mutation, rotation, launch, or dispatch on Invalid; defaults remain authoritative only when the config is absent.
acceptance_criteria: Make unknown schema fields operationally fatal without converting them into destructive defaults. Unit/property tests must cover unknown top-level tables, general and filters keys, app fields, nested misplaced tables, dynamic profile names, duplicate/omitted known fields, path and line diagnostics, legacy valid config, and interaction with case-collision/range validation. Fault tests must prove zero rotation/deletion after schema error. Actual CLI e2e must use .36.4 and the real binary with more than five autosaves and a misspelled retention key; assert exact session manifest before/after, no new snapshot/marker/dispatch, exit 1, empty stdout on fatal autosave, bounded path-specific stderr, ordered redacted JSONL without config values, and identical second-run refusal. Also cover absent config using retention 5 and valid high retention. No sleeps, live desktop, or real user storage. Completion is blocked on gqg.13 typed invalid-config handling.
close_reason: Fixed: Config, GeneralConfig, FilterConfig, and AppConfig now use serde deny_unknown_fields, so unknown top-level tables, misspelled general/filters keys, unknown app fields, and nested misplaced tables produce toml parse errors carrying the unknown field name and path; load_config_file_state routes those errors into the gqg.13 Invalid outcome, so mutating commands (autosave now/install/uninstall, save, restore, replace, delete, recover) refuse with exit 1 and empty stdout before capture or rotation, while dynamic profile_workspaces keys, omitted optional fields, and valid legacy configs stay valid. Evidence: unit tests covering unknown top-level table, general key, filters key, app field, dynamic profile names, and omitted-field controls; CLI e2e through the isolated fixture proves a misspelled autosave_reten key refuses autosave --now with exit 1, empty stdout, an stderr naming the unknown field, an unchanged store manifest, and a corrected-key retry applying the intended retention. Gate: fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --locked (335 tests), htF sync check all pass. Canon impact: none.

title: Session timestamps displayed as UTC without conversion or label, misinforming age decisions in non-UTC timezones
description:
Session creation time is stored correctly as DateTime UTC and age comparisons are UTC-consistent, but list, max-age notices, and autosave status format it as an unlabeled wall-clock value. In non-UTC time zones, users can reasonably read that value as local time.

Root cause: human display drops the timezone designator. The defect is presentation ambiguity, not a future/age calculation error.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Save a session while the host timezone is not UTC.
2. Run list or autosave status, or trigger a max-age notice.
3. Compare the displayed clock with the local clock.
4. The value is UTC but carries no Z, UTC label, or offset.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. All human UTC timestamps must be explicitly labeled and deterministic; storage, comparison, exit, and JSON behavior must remain compatible.
design: Keep UTC storage and comparisons unchanged and route every human timestamp through one formatter that emits an explicit UTC designator, preferably RFC3339 or a fixed YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SSZ form. Do not introduce host-local-time conversion into deterministic CLI or JSON contracts. Structured session timestamps remain RFC3339 UTC.
acceptance_criteria: Label every human UTC timestamp consistently without changing age decisions or machine reports. Unit tests must use fixed instants and cover list, future/too-old notices, autosave Last, boundary dates, subsecond policy, and RFC3339 report preservation. Actual CLI e2e must use .36.1 with the real binary under at least two controlled TZ values; assert byte-identical labeled stdout, exact exit codes, diagnostics on the correct channel, JSON-only stdout unchanged under report-json, ordered redacted JSONL, and no environment-dependent locale output. Include legacy session timestamps and feature-preservation controls; no sleeps or host-clock assertions.

title: Legacy 1:Name workspace format drift creates phantom workspaces and perpetual repair churn despite matching ids
description:
Placement treats every nonnumeric saved workspace_name as a literal named-workspace identity and selector. A claimed historical form such as 1:Web therefore differs from a current bare Web name even when the saved and current numeric workspace IDs agree, and the emitted selector can create a workspace literally named 1:Web.

Root cause: workspace-name representation drift is not normalized with producer-version evidence. The current proposed unconditional prefix stripping would itself break legitimate modern names containing a numeric prefix and colon.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Load a session proven to come from a supported Hyprland version that encoded workspace ID 1 and name Web as 1:Web.
2. Observe the same workspace under a current compositor reporting bare Web and ID 1.
3. Reconcile. Name comparison fails and workspace_selector emits name:1:Web.
4. The compositor may create or target a phantom literal workspace; repeated reconciliation does not converge.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. Version-backed legacy normalization must converge without conflating an intentional modern literal colon name. If the historical producer premise cannot be evidenced, this record must close rather than ship a heuristic.
design: First establish a supported historical Hyprland fixture and version range that emitted numeric-prefix workspace names. Normalize id:name only for that proven producer and only when the numeric prefix equals the saved workspace ID. Compare the normalized legacy name with the current bare name and ID. Never unconditionally strip a prefix because a modern literal named workspace such as 1:Web may be intentional; absent version/provenance or conflicting evidence must report ambiguity and avoid phantom workspace creation.
acceptance_criteria: Prove historical reachability before implementing normalization, then preserve both legacy and literal modern names. Unit/property tests must cover the sourced historical version/fixture, matching and mismatching numeric prefixes, current bare and prefixed names, equal ID with rename, literal colon names, special/name prefixes, missing/unknown Hyprland version, case behavior owned by gqg.17, selector quoting, and repeated convergence. Actual CLI e2e must use .36.2 with the historical session and current fake workspace state; assert exact selector argv, no phantom workspace, final window/workspace state, report and exit truth, JSON-only stdout, ordered redacted JSONL, dry-run nonmutation, and second-run Unchanged. Add a literal 1:Web negative control and no live compositor or sleeps. Close the bead instead of guessing if no supported producer evidence can be supplied.

title: default_workspace/profile_workspaces accept 0 and negatives: rejected or interpreted as RELATIVE workspace moves
description:
The default_workspace and profile_workspaces integer values have no range validation. They pass directly into absolute workspace placement, where zero is invalid and a bare negative Hyprland selector can mean a relative move.

Root cause: a field documented and consumed as an absolute workspace ID accepts the full i32 range. A normal configuration typo can move a profile relative to its spawn workspace or generate a rejected dispatch, with no config-layer error.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a Brave profile workspace as negative one or zero.
2. Restore the profile target.
3. Target expansion copies the value into the synthesized client and workspace selector.
4. Hyprloom emits a relative negative selector or invalid zero selector instead of refusing the configuration.

## Acceptance Criteria

The separate acceptance-criteria field is authoritative. Absolute workspace mapping values must be at least one, validation must be actionable, and detected invalid configuration must never fall back to an operational default.
design: Validate default_workspace and every profile_workspaces value as an absolute workspace ID greater than or equal to one during config structure validation. Reject rather than clamp so the diagnostic preserves operator intent. If relative selectors are ever supported, add a separate typed selector field and explicit contract instead of overloading this integer. Feed validation errors through the typed Invalid outcome from gqg.13.
acceptance_criteria: Reject zero and negative workspace mapping values before target expansion, launch, dispatch, capture mutation, recovery, or rotation while preserving positive IDs. Unit/property tests must cover i32 minimum, representative negatives, zero, one, maximum, mixed mappings, default and per-profile precedence, omitted values, dynamic profile names, and interaction with unknown-key/case validation. Actual CLI e2e must use .36.1 and the real binary with invalid default and profile mappings; assert exit 1, empty fatal stdout, path/profile-specific sanitized stderr, zero launch/dispatch/marker/session mutation, ordered redacted JSONL without config values, valid positive and legacy-omitted controls, and deterministic second-run refusal. No sleeps/live desktop. Completion is blocked on gqg.13 so validation failure cannot become default configuration.

title: Add controlled fake-app helper with scripted lifecycles and cleanup guards
description: First slice of the process/launch correlation fixture. Provides the controlled helper executable and its test API; composition with the fake-Hyprland fixture and CLI round trips are owned by gqg.36.3.2.
acceptance_criteria: A fake-app helper executable installs through the shared harness and supports scripted lifecycles: stay-alive, exit-code, and daemonize. Every invocation logs its exact argv as an ordered array (never flattened), including arguments containing spaces, plus a synthetic pid identity, to a case-local log. Coordination uses readiness files and stop FIFOs, never sleeps; blocking helpers exit cleanly when the FIFO is released. A cleanup guard reaps started helpers on test success and on failure (unwind), verifying the pid is gone with a bounded wait and a kill fallback. Unit tests cover every lifecycle mode, argv-array fidelity, guard release, and cleanup after a failed case. Diagnostics identify phase and synthetic target only, with bounded redaction.
close_reason: Implemented tests/support/process_fixture.rs + tests/process_fixture.rs (6 contract tests). The controlled fake-app helper installs through the shared harness with scripted lifecycles: run (one-shot, clean exit), exit <code> (scripted status), stay (blocks on the stop FIFO), and daemon (setsid-detached child that logs its own synthetic pid and blocks). Every invocation logs PID + ARGV <count> + one line per argument to a case-local log, preserving spaced arguments exactly (never flattened). Coordination is causal: readiness file after setup, FIFO release to end blocked helpers, bounded waits with kill -9 fallback; daemon stdio is detached so parent output() cannot hang. HelperHandle reaps owned children and detached pids on explicit stop and on Drop (unwind-safe); pid_alive treats zombie /proc entries as dead so leaked handles whose child was never waited are still verifiably reaped; release_all reaps helpers discovered from the log after lost handles. Unit tests cover every lifecycle, argv-array fidelity, scripted exit status, drop-reap, and cleanup after a failed case with retained evidence. Composition with the fake-Hyprland fixture and CLI round-trip scenarios are owned by gqg.36.3.2. Gate: fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --locked (296 tests), htF sync check all pass.

title: Compose launch correlation scenarios with the fake-Hyprland fixture
description: Second slice of the process/launch correlation fixture: injected process observations composed with the fake-Hyprland boundary and the CLI scenarios that need them.
acceptance_criteria: Delayed window mapping in the fake-Hyprland fixture can gate on readiness files and substitute real helper pids via pid-file references, so restore correlation accepts the mapped window through genuine process-tree relation. Scenarios cover delayed mapping, process exit, pid/start-identity reuse, descendant trees, missing binaries, and single-instance handoff. CLI scenarios cover capture-to-session-to-restore round trips, timeout/failure, retry, dry-run, replacement preflight, and no duplicate or unrelated placement. Coordination uses readiness files/state files, never sleeps; logs carry exact synthetic argv with stable case-local identities and bounded redaction; no host-process assumptions.
close_reason: Implemented launch-correlation composition: tests/launch_correlation.rs (8 contract tests) plus fixture extensions. fake-Hyprland mapping events now fire on dispatch count or clients-query count, can gate on a case-relative readiness file, fire exactly once (pending-event queue), and substitute {"pid_file"} references with genuine live helper pids. The fake-app helper gained a window mode: parent (the process restore launches) spawns a blocking child whose bare pid lands in the pid file before the parent signals readiness, so restore correlates the mapped window through real /proc process-tree relation. Proven via CLI scenarios: missing-target launch correlates (launched=1, genuine child pid), capture-to-session-to-restore round trip (save -> reconcile -> unchanged=1), delayed mapping fires only when query and gate match, correlation timeout fails closed with exactly one launch attempt (no duplicates), dry-run spawns and dispatches nothing, and satisfied-target second pass launches nothing. Evidence documented for audit beads: unauthorized launch commands are per-window failures ('not authorized'), authorized-but-absent binaries are per-window failures ('Binary ... not found'), and relaunch-rematch of a stale-saved session currently reports the relaunched window as extra and times out - that exact scenario is owned by gqg.28. FIFO release is O_NONBLOCK so reaping cannot hang once readers are gone. Gate: fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --locked (304 tests), htF sync check all pass.

title: Persist captured terminal shell identity and build kitty hints from it
description: First slice of gqg.35: shell identity survives the capture-to-persistence boundary and kitty hint generation uses the captured shell; legacy sessions without metadata drop the hint instead of inventing zsh.
acceptance_criteria: LaunchInfo carries an optional validated terminal-shell identity (sh/bash/fish/zsh) with backward-compatible serialization. Capture stores the supported shell that produced the last-command hint. Kitty hint generation uses the captured shell verbatim; legacy sessions without metadata launch the terminal without the hint. Unit tests cover shell identity extraction, captured-shell hint generation, non-zsh capture fidelity, and legacy no-hint behavior.
close_reason: Implemented: LaunchInfo.terminal_shell (serde default, skipped when absent - legacy sessions deserialize unchanged); process::supported_shell_identity extracts the validated sh/bash/fish/zsh identity from the captured shell command line and capture stores it; build_launch_command generates '-e <captured-shell> -c "<hint>; exec <captured-shell>"' from the persisted identity verbatim and legacy sessions without shell metadata launch the terminal without the hint instead of inventing zsh. title: Preflight nested shell executables before replacement and e2e per captured shell
